- **WTS/VTS evaluation:** the same authors, [*Cost-effective learning-based strategies for test case prioritization in continuous integration of highly-configurable software*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10664-021-10093-3), Empirical Software Engineering, 2022.

The [research guide](research.md) connects those studies and the original algorithm,
dataset and statistical-method papers to the corresponding examples.

A successful data conversion or replay demonstrates that a workflow runs. A claim
about policy effectiveness also needs suitable source evidence, independent
observations and a protected comparison. The [evidence status](roadmap.md)
records what is available and what remains unverified, including the unfinished
historical cross-corpus confirmation.

## Build with us

[Contributing](contributing.md) covers development, documentation and review.
[Maintainability](maintainability.md) records the measured architectural and
docstring priorities. Compatibility history lives in the
[release archive](release-history.md), away from the learning path.



### FILE: docs/input-data.md

# Prepare a test history

The native TCPCI runner consumes recorded test executions grouped into modeled
builds. Use Parquet for new inputs. If you already have a supported public source,
prefer its [dataset adapter](datasets.md): analytical records retain details that
cannot fit in the native replay projection.

## Native layout

```text
data/
└── example-ci/
    └── features-engineered.parquet
```

Set `experiment.datasets_dir: data` and `experiment.datasets: [example-ci]`.
Each dataset directory represents one replay history. The
[first-run tutorial](getting-started.md) creates a complete file programmatically.

| Column | Meaning for a native replay | Preparation responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BuildId` | Numeric modeled round; the loader processes sorted IDs | Assign order explicitly; a provider's numeric ID is not proof of chronology |
| `Name` | Test identity, normalized to text | Keep identity stable and explain renames, collisions and method/class granularity |
| `Duration` | Recorded execution cost used by scheduling | Use finite nonnegative seconds for a seconds-based replay; verify the source unit |
| `Verdict` | Native binary outcome: `1` failed, `0` passed | Keep skipped, cancelled, unavailable and infrastructure outcomes in analytical evidence; define any projection explicitly |
| `CalcPrio` | Mutable priority slot used by the replay | Initialize to zero |
| `LastRun` | Legacy history field | Preserve its declared source meaning; it does not certify feature availability |

Contextual workflows may use additional columns configured under
`contextual_information`. See [policies](policies.md#contextual-policies) before
including current-build features.

The legacy loader accepts semicolon-delimited CSV with a deprecation warning. Its
normalization is intentionally permissive in places: for example, a missing
numeric duration can become zero. That legacy behavior is **not missing-value
validation**. Check input semantics before native projection; use typed
[measurements](domain-results.md) to preserve unknown or unavailable values.

## Keep source records and replay inputs separate

An analytical row can retain a method's original status, source location, stage,
attempt and units. A native row is a deliberately narrower interpretation that
supports the runner. Keep both, along with counts and exclusion reasons.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S[Original source bytes] --> A[Analytical records]
    A --> P[Explicit replay projection]
    P --> N[Native input]
    A --> Q[Source qualification]
    N --> R[Native runner]
    Q --> E[Eligible evidence, if gates pass]
```

An exclusion is a recorded decision about the projection. It must not silently
turn an unexecuted test into a pass. Shared jobs, stages, variants and retries
must retain grouping in later evaluation.

## Durations and budgets

The native file does not carry a machine-readable unit alongside `Duration`.
Source-specific adapters and experiment documentation must supply that contract.
A ratio budget is a fraction of the recorded full-suite duration; a fixed-time
budget is expressed in seconds; a subset-size budget is a test count.

Summing recorded test durations yields a serial test-work model. It does not
measure queue time, setup cost or parallel runner occupancy. Use
[resource accounting](resource-replay.md) for explicitly observed or modeled
physical costs.

## Configurable systems

A whole-test-set history also has `data-variants.parquet`, with a `Variant` column
linking executions to configurations. Separate variant histories use their own
folders and learning state. See [WTS and VTS](highly-configurable.md) and the
[LibSSH adapter](hcs-parquet-etl.md) for complete layouts and sparse-cell handling.

## Next steps

Run a prepared file with [configuration](configuration.md), or choose a verified
source workflow in [datasets](datasets.md). For claims that depend on what was
known at decision time, continue with [point-in-time observations](point-in-time-observations.md).



### FILE: docs/integration-guide.md

# Connect experiments to a CI workflow

Start by deciding whether you need offline replay, a library integration or a
study of recommendations beside a running CI system. These routes share the
native runner and typed contracts, but collect different kinds of evidence.

## Choose an integration route

| Your need | Start here | What it gives you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run recorded test histories | [First experiment](getting-started.md), [library API](api/experiment-api.md) | Native ranking, modeled budgets, results and checkpoint continuation |
| Register bounded application operations | [Application API](application-api.md) | Shared library services and an optional MCP transport |
| Add a policy, hook or artifact | [Extensions](extensibility.md), [artifact API](api/artifacts.md) | Native lifecycle callbacks and typed result publication |
| Inspect a proposed CI schedule | [Operational pilot](operational-pilot.md) | Decision intent, selected work and independent accounting |
| Distinguish serial and parallel costs | [Resource replay](resource-replay.md) | Explicit reservations, occupancy, overhead and released work |
| Record prospective recommendations | [Shadow evaluation](prospective-shadow.md) | Frozen pre-outcome recommendations while the required suite continues |
| Learn what a public provider exposes | [Public CI feasibility](public-ci-feasibility.md) | Bounded Actions metadata collection with explicit missing evidence |
| Monitor an experiment | [Observability](observability.md) | Optional OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana and ClickHouse setup |

## A conservative adoption path

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    H[Inspect recorded source data] --> R[Run comparable offline experiments]
    R --> Q[Check eligibility and uncertainty]
    Q --> S[Record shadow recommendations]
    S --> O[Review actual outcomes and resource use]
    O --> D[Decide under a declared adoption protocol]
    Q --> F[Insufficient evidence: keep conservative fallback]
    O --> F
```

The public-provider feasibility example does not collect a complete required-test
inventory or physical runner occupancy. A successful provider API response is
therefore not enough to authorize skipping required tests. Use the documented
contracts to retain what is available and what remains unknown.

## Extend at the appropriate boundary

Use `coleman.api` for native experiments. Use `coleman.application` when you need
its bounded registered workflows. HTTP, process execution, CLI and MCP adapters
stay at the transport boundary. Domain measurement, observation, selection and
evaluation contracts remain independent of those transports.

The [architecture guide](setup.md) shows the relationships. The
[API reference](api-reference.md) helps locate a symbol, while
[contributing](contributing.md) explains how to preserve the boundaries when adding one.



### FILE: docs/java-fault-matrix.md

# Run a controlled Java fault matrix

Collect three curated upstream fixes across Apache Commons CLI and Codec with
one frozen plan. Each cell runs buggy and fixed source against the same declared
fixed-tree fixture, retaining every observed pass, failure, test error and
incomplete collection. This is controlled functional evidence for TCPCI research;
it is separate from historical CI and policy comparisons.

The published **4.17 wheel** includes the matrix transport. It reuses the existing
single-pair producer and the generic [controlled-observation
domain](controlled-faults.md). It does not introduce a learning runner or change
existing source recipes, results, checkpoints or raw-capture semantics.

The installation below uses the current collector. The initial Docker outcomes
retain their original qualifications; they were not recollected with the current release.
Capture producers bind the whole SDK and package version, so reopening old
observations requires their original package. The [4.15 admission adapter](corpus-admission.md)
revalidates the retained 4.13 captures with their original pinned wheel and raw
parsers; unchanged legacy capture code alone cannot relabel a producer.

## Install and collect outside checkout

Use Python 3.14+, uv, POSIX and a native Linux arm64 Docker engine. These frozen
recipes pin Temurin `11.0.32.1`, the arm64 image digest and
`America/Los_Angeles`. A different architecture needs a separately reviewed
recipe; changing its label does not validate another runtime.

Install the verified published wheel into a fresh external environment; no checkout
is required:

```bash
uv venv /tmp/coleman-matrix-env --python 3.14
uv pip install --python /tmp/coleman-matrix-env/bin/python "https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.17.0/coleman-4.17.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=e5a272ddc0edf72bd909a743fa2b3bc0dfeb8a02871c487ab22683cddeea40ca"

# Explicit operator preparation; COLEMAN never pulls an image.
docker pull --platform linux/arm64 eclipse-temurin@sha256:e4b3ff0f1a427efb2deb02b092ff8316d58573480260720d767d6ecdd69999d8

mkdir -p /tmp/coleman-matrix-workspace
cd /tmp/coleman-matrix-workspace
/tmp/coleman-matrix-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.junit_matrix \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-java-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-java-observations --fetch > matrix-summary.json

# Same plan/trials: validate committed evidence rather than collect it again.
/tmp/coleman-matrix-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.junit_matrix \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-java-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-java-observations
```

Only the first acquisition needs `--fetch`; it permits the existing individually
pinned HTTPS source/JAR downloads. Subject execution has no network. Both cache
and output must be outside Git and separate from each other. The system temporary
directory must also be outside Git. No third-party source or raw capture is bundled.

The JSON summary reports the content-addressed receipt, optional completion path,
collection status, two declared project labels and three curated focal-fix labels.
Exit 0 means collection completed, including negative outcomes. Incomplete source
captures publish an index with `completion: null` and exit 2. Infrastructure,
preflight and publication errors exit nonzero and retain earlier durable evidence.
None of these statuses grants scientific admission.

Validate a saved index without Docker or source execution:

```bash
MATRIX_RECEIPT="$(/tmp/coleman-matrix-env/bin/python -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("matrix-summary.json"))["receipt"])')"
/tmp/coleman-matrix-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.junit_matrix \
  --validate \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-java-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-java-observations < "$MATRIX_RECEIPT"
```

Offline integrity validation can republish identical source-view cache metadata.
It verifies actual source members, context, raw protocol packets and normalized
observations; it starts no process and fetches nothing. Integrity is correspondence,
not authentication of execution truth or benchmark efficacy.
The CLI reads at most 8 MiB of receipt JSON from stdin; `--validate` accepts no
file path. The operator explicitly supplies the input descriptor. Referenced
controlled datasets remain confined to their declared output tree. The Python
API accepts the already parsed typed receipt.

## Frozen source selection

| Curated fix | Direct upstream revisions | Common fixture | Relationship to framework metadata |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CLI-13 | `8f46f467a33ace44ccd9f394910940b6c48a3827` → `b0e1b80b6d4a10a9c9f46539bc4c7a3cce55886e` | Existing published 95-test recipe, unchanged | Defects4J Cli **1**, not Cli13 |
| CLI-51 | `b0e1b80b6d4a10a9c9f46539bc4c7a3cce55886e` → `2ff9573ffb08dd52ec3a55a49f2d77a1e94efbdf` | Same fixed-tree policy, 96 tests | Defects4J Cli2 |
| CODEC-65 | `9c0cabead7cf075308b11362172ae1a48d41321c` → `52d82d1dfff8c2b2ded9d843e0b03017af6d747c` | Explicit partial fixed-tree fixture, 166 tests | Defects4J Codec1 |

The [CLI-51 fix](https://github.com/apache/commons-cli/commit/2ff9573ffb08dd52ec3a55a49f2d77a1e94efbdf)
changes PosixParser and adds BugCLI51Test. The [CODEC-65
fix](https://github.com/apache/commons-codec/commit/52d82d1dfff8c2b2ded9d843e0b03017af6d747c)
changes locale handling in several encoders. These are direct parent/fix source
reproductions with a common fixed fixture, not a full Defects4J reconstruction.
Framework subject labels do not replace source rights or reconstruction evidence.
Those labels were checked against the pinned Defects4J metadata revision
`8c16da8230843cdc918eaf4ddb449637f02b83c6` for
[Cli](https://github.com/rjust/defects4j/blob/8c16da8230843cdc918eaf4ddb449637f02b83c6/framework/projects/Cli/active-bugs.csv)
and [Codec](https://github.com/rjust/defects4j/blob/8c16da8230843cdc918eaf4ddb449637f02b83c6/framework/projects/Codec/active-bugs.csv).

Codec retains all 25 production Java files per role, 15 fixed fixture Java files,
and original `LICENSE.txt`/`NOTICE.txt`. Fixture selection was frozen
**before observing new source outcomes**. The source exclusions are explicit:

- `DoubleMetaphoneTest.java` embeds separately noticed aspell data and non-UTF8
  bytes. It is outside the existing homogeneous-terms/UTF8 source-view profile.
- `SoundexTest.java` also contains non-UTF8 bytes and is excluded without transcoding.
- `AllTests.java` references those excluded classes and is excluded as their suite
  aggregator. Per-TestCase discovery does not require it.

All other fixed-tree Java fixture files remain. This includes
`RefinedSoundexTest.java`, a different file. Missing focal-class coverage stays
visible; this is not the complete upstream suite. No outcome-based filtering is
applied after collection.

Source views preserve exact bytes and original notices. Apache-2.0 subject terms,
Commons Lang 2.1 terms and JUnit 3.8.1 CPL-1.0 terms remain separately reviewed and
pinned. The [Codec NOTICE](https://github.com/apache/commons-codec/blob/52d82d1dfff8c2b2ded9d843e0b03017af6d747c/NOTICE.txt)
identifies the omitted third-party test data; COLEMAN does not relabel it as
Apache-2.0. Codec needs only the pinned JUnit JAR; CLI retains its original two
dependencies. The recipe-only policy keeps foreign content in the external cache.

## Observed results and their limits

The initial installed-producer qualification collected **714 role observations**,
or **357 same-test/trial pairs**, under the frozen runtime:

| Fix | Both pass | Both fail | Assertion failed → passed | Reversed | Inconclusive |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CLI-13 | 92 | 2 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| CLI-51 | 93 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| CODEC-65 | 163 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 0 |

CLI-51's focal buggy test raises `UnrecognizedOptionException`; the fixed role
passes. The existing strict classifier calls this **inconclusive**, because a
test error is distinct from an assertion failure. The matrix preserves that
classification and raw diagnostic. Both CLI fixtures retain the two assertions
that fail in both revisions. A fixed revision is not presented as wholly correct.

The three Codec assertions belong to Caverphone, Metaphone and RefinedSoundex
`testLocaleIndependence` methods. They concern **one** curated fix. The two CLI
fixes share project history. Tests, trials, seeds and JVM repetitions do not become
independent projects or new faults. These observations are runtime/fixture-specific,
not a guarantee about every future run.

Subsequent source inspection identified unseeded `java.util.Random` inputs in
[Base64Test](https://github.com/apache/commons-codec/blob/52d82d1dfff8c2b2ded9d843e0b03017af6d747c/src/test/org/apache/commons/codec/binary/Base64Test.java#L705),
[HexTest](https://github.com/apache/commons-codec/blob/52d82d1dfff8c2b2ded9d843e0b03017af6d747c/src/test/org/apache/commons/codec/binary/HexTest.java#L118)
and [DigestUtilsTest](https://github.com/apache/commons-codec/blob/52d82d1dfff8c2b2ded9d843e0b03017af6d747c/src/test/org/apache/commons/codec/digest/DigestUtilsTest.java#L40).
Generated bytes and seeds are unavailable in the capture protocol. All 166
selected tests remain; only an explicit limitation was added to the recipes.
Source/dependency/runtime/harness pins and fixture selection are unchanged.
Saved observations replay deterministically, while fresh execution does not
reconstruct identical generated inputs. Source admission must assess that limit.

Each role uses the existing shared JVM and lexical test-ID order. Test-order
independence is unverified. Integer case nanoseconds include setup/teardown; parent
process nanoseconds also include startup/compilation. Observed zero remains zero;
unavailable elapsed values are null with `status: unavailable`. Negative counts,
negative elapsed counters, non-finite values and incompatible units reject. Neither
timer is CI queue time, parallel elapsed time, peak memory or removable runner work.
The existing guards bound each role to 60 seconds, 1 MiB combined output, two CPUs,
64 PIDs, 128 MiB tmpfs and 1 GiB memory in these presets. A resource limit is not
a measured peak. Captures are trusted-source reproductions within those guards.

## Contract, artifacts and recovery

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    plan[Frozen typed Java matrix plan] --> preflight[Matrix storage and all-cell budget preflight]
    preflight --> frozen[Immutable plan.json before source execution]
    frozen --> source[Existing source cache and deterministic views]
    source --> capture[Existing bounded JUnit producer]
    capture --> raw[Durable role start markers and raw packets]
    raw --> controlled[Existing generic ControlledDataset]
    controlled --> verify[Offline context and raw observation validation]
    verify --> index[Content-addressed typed matrix index]
    index --> state{All roles collected?}
    state -->|yes| complete[Atomic immutable complete.json last]
    state -->|no| incomplete[Incomplete index; no completion marker]
    complete --> replay[Offline verified replay; no runtime preflight]
```

Plans require schema version 1 and allow at most 16 cells / 4 MiB. Receipts require
schema version 1 and are bounded to 8 MiB. Canonical JSON and SHA-256 identities
include explicit source recipes, trial IDs, selection protocol and implementation
provenance. Reordering declared cells/roles does not change identity. Different
collected clocks or observations legitimately change a receipt; determinism means
identical captured evidence serializes identically, not that new executions have
identical elapsed time.

Duplicate cell IDs and duplicate recipe/trial collections reject. Counts refer to
observed same-test pairs; `unobserved_pairs` preserves completely absent tests.
One-sided evidence remains inconclusive. The index references separately verified
controlled dataset fingerprints and actual raw packet digests, never arbitrary
transport dictionaries. It does not convert controlled observations into native
CI duration columns or historical builds.

The original source producer owns role recovery. A start marker without a committed
packet recovers as interrupted, with no invented cases or elapsed time. It does
not silently rerun that role. Choose a new trial ID for a new collection; it stays
in the same declared dependence group. Concurrent ownership conflicts reject
without duplicate execution; retry after the owner finishes. A crash before matrix
completion leaves the frozen `plan.json` and committed role/data artifacts usable
for recovery. Unattempted cells remain visible in that plan without invented results.
An incomplete index is retained without `complete.json`; an all-role collected
index acquires that marker only after validation and immutable index publication.

Idempotence uses the retained output/capture tree. A fresh output directory does
not restore another directory's acknowledgments; use new trial IDs for a fresh
physical collection. Copying an index alone is insufficient: offline validation
also needs its controlled datasets and the independently verified source cache.

Existing completion is revalidated before any runtime preflight. Corrupt/unknown
schema or producer versions reject. Missing and older matrix schema versions are
unsupported; there is no implicit migration. The producer identity hashes all
COLEMAN package code and resources without importing those modules. Hidden files,
generated bytecode and interpreter caches are excluded. Any other packaged-byte
change, including an unrelated module or a new resource format, conservatively
selects a new generation; the package version also participates. Previous bytes
remain intact. Explicit offline validation requires the matching reviewed producer.
Existing single-pair
JUnit recipes, source caches, controlled artifacts, native results and learning
checkpoints keep their previous contracts and require no migration.

## Python and verification

The optional producer API is also callable without its command-line parser:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from coleman.artifacts import ArtifactWriter
from coleman.corpus.materialization import SourceCache
from coleman.transports.junit_matrix import (
    capture_junit_matrix, load_junit_matrix, validate_junit_matrix,
)

cache = SourceCache("/tmp/coleman-java-source-cache")
writer = ArtifactWriter("/tmp/coleman-java-observations")
plan = load_junit_matrix()
outcome = capture_junit_matrix(plan, cache, writer)  # Offline acquisition by default.
validate_junit_matrix(outcome.receipt, cache, Path(writer.run_root))
assert outcome.receipt.admission == "not_evaluated"
```

Use `--recipe /absolute/path/matrix.json` for another reviewed typed plan. The
generic controlled domain stays independent of CLI, Docker transports and MCP.
Protected source admission and policy evaluation require separate evidence;
source collection alone does not establish either.

Normal tests use owned small fixtures with no downloads. With the image prepared
and all three recipes acquired into an external cache, repeat installed real-source
capture, offline matrix validation, import-boundary checks and an independent owned
native CI/checkpoint workflow:

```bash
COLEMAN_JUNIT_REAL_CACHE=/tmp/coleman-java-source-cache \
  uv run pytest tests/corpus/test_installed_junit_matrix.py --no-cov
```

The native CI fixture has its own exact-answer costs and outcomes; Java harness
elapsed counters are not substituted for CI costs. Actual historical-CI ETL/replay
remains available in the [Karaf](lrts-parquet-etl.md),
[ActiveMQ/Log4j](lrts-stage-views.md) and
[RTPTorrent](rtptorrent-parquet-etl.md) workflows.

[Pre-execution protocol records](release-history.md#pre-execution-protocol-records)
retain the historical declaration evidence for audit.

## Continue the workflow

Read [controlled-observation semantics](controlled-faults.md), then retain source/context dependence
in [source admission](corpus-admission.md) and [evaluation](evaluation-guide.md).



### FILE: docs/junit-source-capture.md

# Reproduce a pinned Java fault pair

COLEMAN's optional JUnit3 producer collects source evidence before benchmark
admission. Its packaged Apache Commons CLI recipe compiles two pinned upstream
revisions against the same fixed-tree test fixture and records all 95 discovered
tests. It reuses the existing source cache, controlled-observation contracts and
immutable artifact writer. Native TCPCI experiments still use the existing runner.

The recipe contains integrity metadata only. Subject sources, dependencies,
container images and raw captures remain outside the repository. It does not
execute Defects4J or claim its complete reconstruction protocol. The generic
[controlled domain](controlled-faults.md) imports no Docker, CLI or MCP adapter.

For a predeclared multi-fix workflow, the published 4.10 wheel includes a separate
[controlled Java matrix](java-fault-matrix.md), reusing this producer unchanged.
It includes CLI-13, CLI-51 and an explicitly partial CODEC-65 fixture, with
negative/inconclusive results retained.

## Prepare and run

The published 4.17 wheel includes this single-pair producer and the matrix
command; use the verified [setup command](setup.md#default-run-no-docker-required).
The bundled preset requires POSIX,
Docker, an arm64 host and arm64 Docker engine. It pins Temurin `11.0.32.1` and
`America/Los_Angeles`. Other platforms require a separately reviewed recipe;
changing a platform label does not validate a different image.

Prepare the public image explicitly:

```bash
docker pull --platform linux/arm64 eclipse-temurin@sha256:e4b3ff0f1a427efb2deb02b092ff8316d58573480260720d767d6ecdd69999d8
```

From an external workspace, using the installed environment:

```bash
python -m coleman.transports.junit \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-junit-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-junit-results \
  --trial source-001 --fetch
```

`--fetch` permits only the individually pinned public source/JAR downloads from
`raw.githubusercontent.com` and `repo.maven.apache.org`. The HTTPS adapter verifies
TLS and exact entity lengths, and rejects redirects, credentials, queries, partial
responses and encoded transfers. It uses no ambient authentication or proxy
configuration. The producer never pulls an image. Once cached, omit `--fetch` for
offline acquisition; subject execution has no network even during the first run.
Source-cache and output directories must be separate and physically outside
Git worktrees. The producer reuses the cache's shared storage guard to reject
repository directories, linked-worktree marker files and symlink aliases. Provided
output roots are checked before runtime queries/source acquisition; concrete cache
blob, capture-session and staging paths are rechecked before content writes.
Staged members cannot introduce case-insensitive `.git` path components. The system
temporary directory must also be outside Git for source staging. Metadata-only
exports retain their existing publication rules.

The JSON summary includes dataset/state paths, role collection statuses, pair
counts, admission and generalization. Exit 0 means both role protocols completed;
assertion failures remain recorded outcomes. Incomplete collection publishes its
evidence and returns 2. Validation, infrastructure or publication exceptions exit
nonzero. Neither exit status certifies benchmark admission or algorithm efficacy.

To supply another frozen recipe, add `--recipe /absolute/path/recipe.json`.
Recipes are bounded to 2 MiB, require schema version 1 and pin the installed
COLEMAN-authored harness. Missing, future or unknown versions reject. Updating the
harness requires an explicit reviewed recipe update, never silent migration.
Existing native results, learning checkpoints and older source artifacts retain
their meaning and require no migration.

## What the recipe freezes

The [buggy revision](https://github.com/apache/commons-cli/tree/8f46f467a33ace44ccd9f394910940b6c48a3827)
and [fixed revision](https://github.com/apache/commons-cli/tree/b0e1b80b6d4a10a9c9f46539bc4c7a3cce55886e)
are the selected public CLI-13 pair. Each production view includes all `src/java`
blobs plus `LICENSE.txt` and `NOTICE.txt`; the common fixture includes all fixed-tree
`src/test` blobs plus those notices. Every raw file and derived ZIP is separately
size/digest pinned. The deterministic ZIP fixes member order, epoch, regular-file
permissions and stored bytes; it is a COLEMAN-derived view, not upstream archive
bytes. Its contract permits at most 128 homogeneous-license members, 8 MiB per
file, 16 MiB decoded total and 32 MiB output. It adds no TAR or ZIP64 support.

The dependencies are Commons Lang 2.1 and JUnit 3.8.1. Apache subject and Commons
Lang Apache-2.0 terms remain separate from JUnit's CPL-1.0 terms. The version-specific
[JUnit POM](https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/junit/junit/3.8.1/junit-3.8.1.pom)
declares CPL-1.0; the recipe records the reviewed [full terms](https://opensource.org/license/CPL-1.0).
Commons Lang's terms digest identifies `META-INF/LICENSE.txt` inside its independently
pinned JAR; its `NOTICE.txt` is retained. The COLEMAN MIT license does not replace
these terms. The recipe-only policy keeps foreign content in the external cache.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    recipe[Pinned Java source recipe] --> raw[Reviewed raw source and dependency cache]
    raw --> views[Deterministic source views]
    views --> guards[Shared optional container guards]
    guards --> producer[Optional bounded Docker producer]
    harness[Packaged COLEMAN JUnit3 harness] --> producer
    producer --> packets[Raw v1 role packets and v2 ownership markers]
    packets --> report[Controlled report plus diagnostic members]
    report --> domain[Existing offline controlled conversion]
    domain --> artifact[Immutable controlled artifact]
```

Each role uses a fresh non-root, read-only container, four explicit read-only
input mounts, no network, no added capabilities, no privilege escalation, two
CPUs, 64 PIDs, a 128-MiB temporary filesystem and a 1-GiB memory default. The
parent bounds collection to 60 seconds and 1 MiB combined stdout/stderr by default;
recipes may select only the contract's bounded ranges. These guards support
trusted public-source reproduction; they are not a hostile-code security sandbox.

Diagnostic packaging has its own explicit budget: each complete role packet is
bounded to 16 MiB, the normalized report remains bounded to 8 MiB, and the decoded
envelope total is at most 40 MiB. The shared deterministic ZIP encoder preserves
stored bytes and existing ZIP64/entry policies; source-view limits remain
8 MiB per file and 16 MiB total. This accommodates the permitted 4-MiB output
profile without dropping raw streams or parsed diagnostics. Before acquisition
or execution, the producer computes a conservative normalized-report size bound
from declared test/trial labels and maximal field sizes. Unsupported combinations
reject before a source trial can create unpublishable completed role checkpoints.
The sizing records are never published as observations.

The filtered runtime receipt retains host/Python/package versions, Docker
client/server architecture and versions, kernel and target image config digest
and size. It excludes credentials, context names, unrelated containers, image
tags and hostnames. Actual producer module bytes, recipe and harness are input
receipts, so modified implementation bytes change context identity.

## Evidence and recovery

A fresh local execution collected 190 observations: 92 same-test pairs passed in
both revisions, two failed in both and CLI-13 failed then passed. The two other
failures (`BugsTest::test19383`, `BugsTest::test27635`) remain visible. No causal
explanation or extra unique-fault count is inferred. These are observations of
this runtime and fixture, not a promise that every future run has the same result.

Each case runs in the role's shared JVM in lexical test-ID order, including JUnit
setup/teardown. Independence from test order has not been established. Its strict
integer monotonic nanoseconds mean harness elapsed time, never removable runner
cost or wall-clock CI savings. Zero is observed; unavailable counters are null.
The separate parent timer includes startup and compilation. UTC capture instants
are explicitly quantized by the producer to microseconds; higher-precision input
strings reject rather than silently truncate. No collection clock becomes
historical CI chronology or a predecision feature.

An immutable start marker precedes each role execution. A completed raw packet
replays without executing that role again. A start marker without a committed
packet recovers as `interrupted`: streams and counters remain unavailable, no
partial cases are promoted. Use a new trial ID for a fresh execution. Both trials
remain in the same dependence group. A POSIX advisory lock rejects concurrent
producers for the same context/trial; a process crash releases it. Cleanup targets
only the producer's deterministic container name. A cleanup failure propagates
without committing a role packet; the next call retries cleanup and retains the
interrupted observation state. Source acquisition, staging and
publication failures never certify a completed learning checkpoint. New start
markers use schema version 2 and persist the original output namespace and exact
container name. Their name is validated against the logical context/trial/role
before cleanup. Version 1 markers remain readable and recover using their original
state-prefix container naming rule; unknown versions reject before cleanup. V2
markers are bounded to 8 KiB and legacy v1 markers retain their 4-KiB bound. Raw
role packets and controlled datasets retain their existing version 1 contracts.

Successful protocols require the exact discovered test sequence and a final
trailer. Discovery loads excluded classes without initializing them. Output from
test-class initializers and constructors is retained in the role's bounded raw
stderr, separately from protocol stdout and per-case diagnostics/timing. Discovery
errors restore the original streams and fail collection without inventing cases.
Each case declares exactly one run and at most one terminal failure or
error; contradictory counters cause a protocol error rather than a normalized
test outcome. Malformed/partial protocols, timeouts, output limits and process errors
retain bounded raw evidence without promoting partial cases into assertions.
On replay, exited process/protocol error labels are rederived from the stored
exit code and raw protocol; relabeling a valid complete packet cannot silently
discard its observations. Unavailable streams require an unknown exit code and
unavailable parent elapsed counter; observed streams require both observed process
facts. A timeout must reach its declared parent deadline, and an output-limit
packet must retain the complete bounded prefix. These checks reject contradictory
evidence; coherent timeout/output-limit labels remain producer attestations rather
than authenticated proof of which guard fired.
Both role packets are separately digest-pinned report members; normalized
observations reference their diagnostic member digest. An entirely unobserved
trial has no invented pairs. Negative, reversed and inconclusive comparisons
remain valid. All outputs retain `not_evaluated` and `insufficient_evidence`.

## Validate the installed flow

The normal suite exercises owned fixtures without external downloads. To repeat
the actual source flow from a wheel installed outside the checkout, first populate
the source cache with the command above and prepare the pinned image, then run:

```bash
COLEMAN_JUNIT_REAL_CACHE=/tmp/coleman-junit-cache \
  uv run pytest tests/corpus/test_installed_junit.py --no-cov -q
```

This explicit source reproduction checks all 190 observations and the observed
pair counts, then repeats the same trial to verify byte-identical recovery. It
mocks no source compiler, JVM, cache, converter or artifact writer. It establishes
functional reproduction only. Chronological benchmark admission, additional
languages/faults, independent observations, fair baselines and all seven diversity
regimes require additional source evidence and comparative evaluation.

New v2 container ownership includes the resolved output namespace. Equal logical
trials in separate output roots cannot collide or clean each other's containers;
observation identities retain their original meaning. Keep incomplete ownership
state together when moving an output tree: a version 2 marker still identifies
the original container after relocation. Legacy v1 names retain their global
context/trial scope; their missing output namespace cannot be inferred
retroactively. Retain the original reviewed producer
package when reopening older captures; changing package bytes changes the source
context and does not automatically discover an older producer's generation.

## Continue the workflow

Expand a pair through the [Java fault matrix](java-fault-matrix.md), or inspect how its evidence is
interpreted in [controlled observations](controlled-faults.md).



### FILE: docs/lrts-parquet-etl.md

# Download LRTS, convert to Parquet and run COLEMAN

This workflow uses **real public Karaf test reports**, not the owned correctness
fixture. It downloads pinned source bytes, converts eight selected reports into
Parquet, writes a completion/provenance manifest and executes Random and UCB
through the existing native TCPCI runner. Repeating the command reuses verified
inputs and resumes the same native checkpoint.

For additional projects and explicit multistage correspondence, see
[ActiveMQ and Log4j stage views](lrts-stage-views.md). That new recipe family
preserves these original single-stage contracts and receipts.

Use Python 3.14+ and the published 4.17.0 wheel. Pip verifies its SHA-256:

```bash
python -m pip install "https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.17.0/coleman-4.17.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=e5a272ddc0edf72bd909a743fa2b3bc0dfeb8a02871c487ab22683cddeea40ca"
```

Choose cache and output directories outside Git. No Docker, optional MCP SDK,
credentials or provider account is required:

```bash
python -m coleman.transports.lrts_etl \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-lrts-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-lrts-data \
  --fetch --run

# Reopen the same source/data and continue the same native run, offline:
python -m coleman.transports.lrts_etl \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-lrts-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-lrts-data \
  --run
```

`--fetch` explicitly permits the two pinned public HTTPS downloads. A verified
cache hit makes no request. Each request has a 15-second inactivity timeout and
a 300-second elapsed budget checked between reads; this is not an OS deadline
for DNS/headers. Failed acquisitions publish no complete source blob. A retry
reuses completed blobs and restarts any incomplete download from byte zero.
Without `--run`, the command only prepares data. Exceptions return nonzero and
never print a successful ETL summary. The final JSON reports the completion path,
analytical table, native datasets directory, exclusions and native run location.

## What the recipe selects

The preset `lrts-karaf-first-eight-v1.json` pins:

- `karaf.zip` from [LRTS raw reports v3](https://zenodo.org/records/15603448):
  16,571,092 bytes, SHA-256
  `d87c5fa06f5b220ca0f719ba4032719396a5da3dd0776994ceaa32cc2fcd5841`;
- the 13,698,468-byte metadata CSV at repository revision
  `2c1b68e9b1d4ec6c4f304869e36af2e3168da889`, previously matched byte-for-byte
  to the [original code artifact](https://zenodo.org/records/12662090);
- eight outer ZIP members and each nested ZIP's decoded JSON, with independent
  SHA-256 and byte counts;
- separately reviewed CC BY 4.0 record evidence for metadata and raw reports.

Credit: Runxiang Cheng, Shuai Wang, Reyhaneh Jabbarvand and Darko Marinov,
[*Revisiting Test-Case Prioritization on Long-Running Test Suites*, ISSTA 2024](https://doi.org/10.1145/3650212.3680307).
Their dataset/component terms remain separate from COLEMAN's MIT license. The
recipe-only disposition keeps downloaded and converted content in external local
storage; COLEMAN bundles metadata/pins, not third-party rows or archives.

The slice contains the first eight Karaf builds when sorting the pinned metadata
by its scheduled label, PR and source build ID. It is a declared bounded slice,
not the entire project/corpus or the authors' confirmatory profile:

| Replay round | Source PR | Source build |
| ---: | --- | ---: |
| 1 | PR-1213 | 3 |
| 2 | PR-1077 | 2 |
| 3 | PR-1213 | 4 |
| 4 | PR-1077 | 3 |
| 5 | PR-1287 | 1 |
| 6 | PR-1287 | 2 |
| 7 | PR-1288 | 1 |
| 8 | PR-1289 | 1 |

## Files you can actually use

The JSON summary points to a content-addressed export directory:

```text
corpus-etl/<export-id>/
  observations.parquet
  builds.parquet
  datasets/karaf/features-engineered.parquet
  complete.json
```

`observations.parquet` preserves **6,876 source method executions**, including
repeated labels, skipped/unknown outcomes, unavailable durations, observed zero,
raw suite/node/enclosure identities and raw suite timestamp spelling. Duration
columns explicitly include seconds, source meaning and availability status.
`execution_id` identifies the actual project/PR/build/suite/case position.
`replay_name` separately identifies an assumed cross-round label correspondence.
Neither identifies a unique fault.

`builds.parquet` maps every modeled round back to its actual source PR/build and
preserves typed metadata as canonical JSON. Scheduled epoch labels remain
separate from `outcome_available_at`, which is null. Per-round replay counts and
eligibility retain rounds with no compatible reported cases.

The native Parquet has **6,567 compatible executions** with the existing
`BuildId`, `Name`, `Duration`, `CalcPrio`, `LastRun` and `Verdict` columns, plus
`SourceExecutionId` for the audit join. The **309 not-run methods** remain in the
analytical table and are explicitly excluded from runnable input. Unknown
outcomes and unavailable durations have separate exclusion reasons; neither is
filled with zero or pass. All 29 reported failed executions remain runnable.

`complete.json` is written last using the existing immutable artifact writer. It
binds the full recipe, actual producer digest, writer version, logical-row digest,
three file digests/sizes/counts, source dataset identities and conserved metadata
and method exclusions. A partial export lacks this receipt. Individual complete
files/cache blobs can survive an interruption and are checked again on retry.
Concurrent identical exports converge; conflicting contents fail closed.

Inspect the result using the exact path printed by the command:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import polars as pl

root = Path("/absolute/export/path/from/the/completion/summary")
observations = pl.read_parquet(root / "observations.parquet")
print(observations.group_by("outcome", "replay_exclusion").len())
print(pl.read_parquet(root / "builds.parquet"))
native = pl.read_parquet(root / "datasets/karaf/features-engineered.parquet")
assert native.height + observations.filter(pl.col("replay_exclusion").is_not_null()).height == observations.height
```

## Meaning of the native run

The default run uses existing Random and UCB (`c=1`) policies, RNFail, seed 42
and a 50% ratio budget, with native Parquet results and checkpoints. Eight rounds
times two policies produce 16 native result rows. Repeating the command resumes
those rows rather than appending another experiment. The exact ETL receipt is
included in the native artifact manifest. Native run parameters/provenance remain
available through the existing RunSpec/API, without a second runner.

This is explicitly a **post-hoc serial simulation**:

- rounds follow scheduled source labels, not verified completion/availability;
- costs add reported method seconds, not measured runner occupancy or CI latency;
- feedback uses `budget-censored-native-RNFail-zero-nondetection`: detected
  failures within budget earn reward 1; all other prioritized cases, including
  unscheduled ones, earn reward 0. Zero reward means nondetection, not an observed
  pass or a calibrated failure probability. Source verdicts remain unchanged;
- matching suite/context/class/method labels and occurrence order are an assumed
  correspondence, not verified stable cross-build identities;
- `CalcPrio=0` is a neutral native input and empty `LastRun` retains unavailable
  history, without creating a wall-clock date;
- verdicts count reported failing executions, never independently mapped faults.

The [source assessment](lrts.md) remains in force. Admission stays
`blocked_source_evidence`, generalization stays `insufficient_evidence` and
protected temporal evaluation remains unavailable. The generated files are usable
for inspection and this declared simulation; results cannot establish policy
superiority, prospective savings or confirmatory cross-corpus generalization.
Seeds, PRs and repeated executions do not become independent projects/faults.

Legacy receipts declaring `full-reported-labels-after-modeled-round` remain
readable and their analytical Parquet remains verifiable. New exports, downloads
and native execution reject that declaration: the existing RNFail learner never
provided full-label feedback. To opt into the corrected model, explicitly create
a recipe with `feedback="budget-censored-native-RNFail-zero-nondetection"` and
export again. This creates a new recipe/export/run identity; retain the old
receipt unchanged for audit. Missing/unknown feedback declarations reject rather
than acquiring an implicit meaning. Existing results must not be silently relabeled.

## Architecture and compatibility

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    H[Explicit pinned HTTPS download] --> C[Existing verified external cache]
    C --> Z[Separate bounded selected-member ZIP recipe]
    Z --> J[Existing nested ZIP materializer]
    M[Pinned metadata CSV] --> C
    J --> L[Existing typed LRTS parser]
    C --> L
    L --> P[Analytical and native Parquet]
    P --> R[Completion receipt written last]
    R --> A[Existing native API and RunSpec]
    A --> N[Native results and learning checkpoint]
```

The old complete-package v1 ZIP contract still allows at most 128 entries and
rejects ZIP64. The **separate selected-member recipe** allows an explicitly
bounded directory of up to 4,096 entries and 2 MiB metadata. It validates every
name/type/local header before decoding only the declared members (at most 128,
64 MiB selected total). Unselected payloads are not decoded/certified. Full
container SHA-256 and selected/nested digests remain mandatory. No archive path
is used as an output filesystem path.

New ETL/selection contracts require schema version 1 and reject missing/future
versions. Existing native Parquet, source receipts, results and checkpoints keep
their meanings. No legacy migration is performed. Fixed Parquet settings and the
recorded Polars version support byte reproducibility; logical-row identities are
independent of physical encoding. `validate_lrts_etl` rechecks actual cached
sources and actual Parquet schema/rows/bytes offline rather than trusting a JSON
declaration. Integrity checks do not authenticate historical producer execution.

## Reproduce package validation

Normal tests use only owned tiny fixtures. For installed real-source verification,
first populate the explicit cache above, then run from the source checkout:

```bash
COLEMAN_LRTS_ETL_REAL_CACHE=/tmp/coleman-lrts-source-cache \
  uv run pytest tests/corpus/test_installed_lrts_etl.py --no-cov -q
```

This installs a wheel outside the checkout, verifies core import boundaries,
converts real source bytes and runs/reopens actual native checkpoints. Network
acquisition remains a separate explicit verification. For larger histories, use the [stage-view workflow](lrts-stage-views.md), while
[baseline matrices](comparable-baselines.md) provide comparable candidate preparation.
Protected historical confirmation remains [unfinished](roadmap.md#historical-corpus-status).

## Continue the workflow

Inspect [LRTS source meaning](lrts.md), expand to [separate stage views](lrts-stage-views.md), then
assess the evidence through [source admission](corpus-admission.md).



### FILE: docs/lrts-stage-views.md

# Run larger LRTS histories without merging their stages

Use four-build ActiveMQ and Log4j source profiles to turn verified public Jenkins
reports into analytical Parquet and checkpointed TCPCI runs. ActiveMQ supplies a
larger single-stage history; Log4j keeps its reported Ubuntu and Windows contexts
separate. Each view runs Random and UCB through the existing native API.

The published **4.17 wheel** includes this stage-view workflow and retains
[Karaf](lrts-parquet-etl.md) and [RTPTorrent](rtptorrent-parquet-etl.md). It contains
the typed contracts and frozen public source recipes; large archives remain
separate operator downloads.

## Install outside checkout and acquire exact bytes

With Python 3.14+ and uv, install the published wheel into a fresh external
environment. Its SHA-256 is verified before installation. Keep sources, cache
and outputs outside any Git repository; no checkout is needed:

```bash
uv venv /tmp/coleman-stage-env --python 3.14
uv pip install --python /tmp/coleman-stage-env/bin/python "https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.17.0/coleman-4.17.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=e5a272ddc0edf72bd909a743fa2b3bc0dfeb8a02871c487ab22683cddeea40ca"
mkdir -p /tmp/coleman-stage-sources

# Explicit operator downloads can resume; the ETL separately verifies full hashes.
curl --fail --location --continue-at - \
  https://zenodo.org/records/15603448/files/activemq.zip \
  --output /tmp/coleman-stage-sources/activemq.zip
curl --fail --location --continue-at - \
  https://zenodo.org/records/15603448/files/log4j.zip \
  --output /tmp/coleman-stage-sources/log4j.zip
```

The [authors' raw-report record, v3](https://zenodo.org/records/15603448) declares
CC BY 4.0 for the dataset. The new recipes pin the specific record, reviewed
[CC BY 4.0 terms](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode.txt),
complete archive bytes, selected nested ZIPs and decoded reports. Data terms do
not establish rights to execute subject code. No subject repository is executed.
Downloaded and converted data stay external; COLEMAN bundles recipes, not rows.

| Complete source | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `activemq.zip` | 161,568,227 | `5fe63b10167fb0e9995484bbc4131e4ab6ece462acc76faf6db7813c9484ab1f` |
| `log4j.zip` | 41,551,352 | `dc6639607b5378451a4a1a558289d4fdf899a3f176e0c9d81a813a18dcdc635c` |

Metadata is the same pinned 57,437-row, 21,255-build paper snapshot used by the
existing reader: repository revision
`2c1b68e9b1d4ec6c4f304869e36af2e3168da889`, 13,698,468 bytes, SHA-256
`49570f8dca753c385f25346f8aaaded3a841b0e67dabf36fbb67260a79b02987`.
It is distinct from the later collection described by the authors' README.
Credit: Runxiang Cheng, Shuai Wang, Reyhaneh Jabbarvand and Darko Marinov,
[*Revisiting Test-Case Prioritization on Long-Running Test Suites*, ISSTA 2024](https://doi.org/10.1145/3650212.3680307).

## Convert, run and resume

```bash
/tmp/coleman-stage-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.lrts_stage_etl \
  --preset activemq --archive /tmp/coleman-stage-sources/activemq.zip \
  --fetch-metadata --cache /tmp/coleman-stage-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-stage-activemq --run

/tmp/coleman-stage-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.lrts_stage_etl \
  --preset log4j-ubuntu --archive /tmp/coleman-stage-sources/log4j.zip \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-stage-cache --output /tmp/coleman-stage-log4j-ubuntu --run

/tmp/coleman-stage-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.lrts_stage_etl \
  --preset log4j-windows --cache /tmp/coleman-stage-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-stage-log4j-windows --run

# Reverify and resume the identical ActiveMQ run, with no network or archive path.
/tmp/coleman-stage-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.lrts_stage_etl \
  --preset activemq --cache /tmp/coleman-stage-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-stage-activemq --run
```

Only `--fetch-metadata` enables network access, for the pinned CSV through the
existing bounded public HTTPS adapter. Its inactivity/elapsed limits are
unchanged. Alternatively supply the exact local CSV with `--metadata PATH`.
`--archive` always checks the explicitly supplied complete archive, even when
verified cache blobs already exist. Download failures or partial files do not
become complete source artifacts. Both archives use the existing ordinary ZIP
selection profile, not a widened legacy ZIP policy or the ZIP64 reader.

Omit `--run` to prepare data only. The final JSON identifies the analytical files,
completion receipt, native run, conserved exclusions and temporal blockers.
Runner logs go to stderr; JSON goes to stdout. Invalid source, unknown versions,
ambiguous mapping or unsafe destinations fail nonzero. Repeating the same
arguments reuses the same immutable export and native checkpoint.

Actual source/installed-package checks produced:

| Native view | Analytical methods | Native cases | Outside stage | Not run in selected stage | Native result rows |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ActiveMQ | 18,901 | 18,668 | 0 | 233 | 8 |
| Log4j Ubuntu | 30,066 | 14,957 | 15,014 | 95 | 8 |
| Log4j Windows | 30,066 | 14,906 | 15,052 | 108 | 8 |

Each view has four modeled rounds and two policies. Unknown-outcome and
unavailable-duration exclusions are zero in these particular slices, not
globally assumed absent. The two Log4j analytical row sets overlap completely;
do not add their row counts as if they were independent source observations.

## Frozen source selection and stage correspondence

Candidates are selected by reported scheduled label, PR and source build ID,
without conditioning on failures. Labels order modeled rounds; they are not
verified outcome chronology. The four-build slice keeps each project under
50,000 methods and each decoded report under 16 MiB.

| Project | Selected PR/build keys | Processed stages per build |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| ActiveMQ | PR-644/1, PR-656/1, PR-669/3, PR-679/1 | 1 |
| Log4j | PR-441/2, PR-442/1, PR-392/9, PR-443/1 | 2 |

The three recipes are `lrts-activemq-first-four-stage-v1.json`,
`lrts-log4j-ubuntu-first-four-stage-v1.json` and
`lrts-log4j-windows-first-four-stage-v1.json`, inside `coleman.corpus.resources`.
The last two select different native views of the **same full source reports**.

Every binding explicitly pins source PR/build, processed `stage_id`, the **exact
ordered** `enclosingBlockNames` array and complete raw node-ID set. ActiveMQ's
`single` maps to `[Tests]` / node `92` in the selected reports. Log4j bindings are:

| PR/build | `Ubuntu_Test` → `[Ubuntu, Test]` node | `Windows_Test` → `[Windows, Test]` node |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PR-441/2 | 79 | 67 |
| PR-442/1 | 78 | 66 |
| PR-392/9 | 67 | 73 |
| PR-443/1 | 78 | 66 |

All selected metadata stages and all raw suites, including empty suites, must
match the relation exactly. Extra, missing, conflicting or ambiguous bindings
reject. There is no underscore concatenation, substring matching or automatic
slug inference. `[a_b, c]` and `[a, b_c]` are distinct contexts. Raw
`enclosingBlocks` remains a separate array; it need not have the same length as
the name array. Node IDs are local to a build and do not establish test continuity.
Reported Ubuntu/Windows labels do not certify runner OS or machine topology.

## Files, identities and explicit semantics

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    P[Pinned metadata and complete public source archive] --> C[Existing verified external cache]
    C --> R[Existing typed complete-report reader]
    R --> B[Exact processed stage / raw context / node binding]
    B --> A[All methods and all processed stages in analytical Parquet]
    B --> V[One explicitly declared native stage view]
    A --> F[Immutable files then versioned completion receipt]
    V --> F
    F --> N[Existing native RunSpec API and checkpoint]
    F --> E[Temporal evidence blockers remain explicit]
```

Each content-addressed export contains exactly three Parquet roles followed by
`complete.json`:

```text
corpus-etl/<recipe-producer-writer-identity>/
  observations.parquet
  builds.parquet
  datasets/<explicit-dataset-id>/features-engineered.parquet
  complete.json
```

`observations.parquet` retains every original project/PR/build/suite/case identity,
raw status, outcome, node/context arrays, raw timestamp spelling and duration.
Seconds carry their source meaning and availability status. Observed zero is
zero; unavailable duration remains null; skipped and unknown outcomes never
become passes. Negative, NaN and infinite durations reject under the existing
nonnegative source-seconds contract. Distinct processed class/method counts and
raw outcomes are never substituted for one another.

A primary `replay_exclusion` conserves each row: `outside_stage` first, then
`not_run`, `unknown_outcome`, `unavailable_duration`, or null for native eligibility.
Outside-stage rows retain their original outcome and duration, even if skipped.

`builds.parquet` retains **all** processed stage DTOs in canonical `metadata_json`,
stage counts and original source keys. Repeated build-level metadata must agree
across stages. Stage-specific filtered class/method counts and cost sums remain
separate. `outcome_available_at` is null. `source_build_group` is stable over the
same project/PR/build labels; both Log4j views share it and source dataset digests.
Those views are correlated observations, not two independent projects or faults.

Native `Name` includes the explicit stage and suite/class/method occurrence;
occurrences are assigned before eligibility. `SourceExecutionId` joins the exact
raw execution; it is stable across views and is distinct from assumed cross-round
identity. Native `Duration` is additive reported method seconds. Native `BuildId`
is a local modeled round. No native quantity means observed parallel CI savings.

Native RNFail feedback is budget-censored: prioritized cases without detected
failure receive zero nondetection reward, including unscheduled cases. Zero
reward does not mean a reported pass, calibrated probability or full-label update.
The profile does not reproduce the paper's All, DeConf or FirstFail class filters.

## Typed API and compatibility

```python
from pathlib import Path

from coleman.application.corpus import run_lrts_stage_replay
from coleman.artifacts import ArtifactWriter
from coleman.corpus.lrts_stage_contracts import LRTSStageRecipe, LRTSStageReceipt
from coleman.corpus.lrts_stage_etl import export_lrts_stage_parquet, validate_lrts_stage_etl
from coleman.corpus.materialization import SourceCache
from importlib.resources import files

recipe = LRTSStageRecipe.from_json(
    files("coleman.corpus.resources").joinpath("lrts-log4j-ubuntu-first-four-stage-v1.json").read_bytes()
)
cache = SourceCache("/tmp/coleman-stage-cache")  # Acquired with the command above.
completion = export_lrts_stage_parquet(recipe, cache, ArtifactWriter("/tmp/coleman-stage-api"))
receipt = LRTSStageReceipt.from_json(completion.read_bytes())
validate_lrts_stage_etl(receipt, cache, completion.parent)
result = run_lrts_stage_replay(completion, cache, Path("/tmp/coleman-stage-api-native"))
print(result.run_id, receipt.admission, receipt.temporal.model_dump())
```

The new `lrts-stage-parquet-replay-v1` family requires integer `schema_version=1`.
Missing, coerced, unknown or future versions reject. Canonical recipe metadata is
at most 1 MiB; transport recipe/receipt reads are capped at 2 MiB. Native aliases
also reject Windows device names, including case variants and dotted extensions,
on every host before acquisition. Fixed Parquet settings and the recorded Polars
version bind physical bytes; canonical rows
separately bind logical meaning. Validation regenerates source-derived expected
bytes and rejects forged/self-signed Parquet without decoding it.

The actual producer digest binds conversion/contract/storage code. Unknown
producer or writer versions require their recorded implementation; regeneration
under changed code produces a different namespace. Old single-stage recipes,
receipts, producer semantics and RunSpec identities remain unchanged. They use
`export_lrts_parquet`, `validate_lrts_etl` and `run_lrts_replay`; the old exporter
continues to reject multistage reports. **No automatic artifact migration occurs.**
To opt in, create a new explicit stage recipe and export into its own namespace;
retain old artifacts and their pinned environment when reproducing old results.

The immutable writer publishes all three bounded files before the completion
receipt. Interrupted writes may leave individual files; they never certify a new
completed export. Identical concurrent retries converge, byte disagreements
reject, and existing checkpoints resume without duplicate committed results.
Cache/output/native destinations are preflighted before acquisition, including
symlinks and nested Git repositories. These are trusted-local cooperative
filesystem guarantees, not an OS sandbox or a distributed transaction.

## Source-specific admission decision

All new profiles remain `blocked_source_evidence` /
`posthoc-serial-simulation` / `insufficient_evidence`. Exact stage correspondence
is resolved for these reports. Other necessary evidence is still unavailable:

| Required evidence | Source finding and decision |
| --- | --- |
| Executor start | Metadata provides a truncated scheduling label; no certified executor-start event. |
| Outcome availability | Raw suite timestamps are null in these selected reports; schedule plus duration cannot identify outcome availability. |
| Feature availability | Processed/retrospective metadata has no certified decision-time feature publication log. |
| Expected test universe | Reported methods do not establish tests expected but absent from a build. |
| Cross-round correspondence | Stage/suite/class/method occurrence is an explicit matching assumption, not verified stable source test identity. |
| Concurrency topology | Raw node/context links and duration sums do not supply executor overlap, queueing or physical runner occupancy. |

`receipt.temporal.require_temporal_evaluation()` rejects with these blockers.
The selected archives contain raw test reports, not independent build/executor
logs. The [pinned extraction code](https://github.com/lrtsuser/LRTS/blob/2c1b68e9b1d4ec6c4f304869e36af2e3168da889/artifact/extract_test_result.py)
normalizes contexts, filters methods, drops duplicate labels and constructs
class outcomes; that behavior does not make its results available before a
historical decision. See the [original source assessment](lrts.md) for snapshot,
filtering and clock boundaries. No author baseline, algorithm win, independent
fault count or prospective production improvement is claimed.

## Continue the workflow

Keep stage/source dimensions from the [LRTS assessment](lrts.md), and carry their shared build
groups into [repeated observations](corpus-evaluation.md).



### FILE: docs/lrts.md

# LRTS: preserve raw method evidence and processed metadata

Inspect an LRTS source offline before interpreting its replay. It joins one
selected project/PR/build from pinned metadata with a separately pinned raw
Jenkins JUnit report. It retains raw suites, node/enclosing-block links and every
method execution, including repeated labels. Install the verified 4.5 release
wheel to run these examples.

For the real-source download-to-Parquet workflow, use
[LRTS download, conversion and native replay](lrts-parquet-etl.md). It preserves
these admission limits while providing actual analytical/native files and an
explicitly modeled serial simulation.

**Admission remains blocked.** Scheduled build time is not executor start or
outcome availability. Processed stage labels are not an automatic mapping to raw
Jenkins nodes. Reported methods do not establish the complete expected CI suite.
No inferred clock, stage-name normalization, deduplication or reconstructed
history enters protected evaluation through this reader.

## Source assessment and snapshot boundaries

This is a focused primary-source compatibility assessment, not a completed
systematic literature review or an effectiveness experiment. Sources checked on
2026-10-16 UTC include:

- [The authors' ISSTA 2024 paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3650212.3680307)
  ([author PDF](https://shuaiwang516.github.io/pub/longRTS.pdf)). Its evaluation
  snapshot has 21,255 builds and 57,437 suite runs. All, DeConf and FirstFail are
  different outcome definitions. The paper uses serial sums when discussing
  suite durations; those sums are not observed parallel CI latency.
- [Pinned LRTS repository revision](https://github.com/lrtsuser/LRTS/tree/2c1b68e9b1d4ec6c4f304869e36af2e3168da889).
  Its metadata CSV still has the paper-sized snapshot, while its README describes
  a later 32,199-build / 108,366-run collection. These counts must not be pooled.
- [Original artifact record 12662090](https://zenodo.org/records/12662090):
  `LRTS-main.zip`, 288,151,681 bytes, provider MD5
  `be5b2c0c83e46e20453acab18c2a6da7`, independently computed SHA-256
  `9e3ca483a7ed075cc532364ca5b58cc3651d4a622ec5fd58efdefd945b3853d0`.
- [Raw-report record 15603448, v3](https://zenodo.org/records/15603448): its
  `karaf.zip` is 16,571,092 bytes, provider MD5
  `6f0d45a08644d19594692c11e5508300`, computed SHA-256
  `d87c5fa06f5b220ca0f719ba4032719396a5da3dd0776994ceaa32cc2fcd5841`.
  The earlier raw record 15580600 is v2, not this same version declaration.

Both complete downloaded archives passed size/provider-checksum comparison.
The decoded `LRTS-main/artifact/metadata/dataset.csv` is byte-identical to the
pinned Git file: 13,698,468 bytes, SHA-256
`49570f8dca753c385f25346f8aaaded3a841b0e67dabf36fbb67260a79b02987`.
This correspondence supports reviewing the specific artifact's data terms,
rather than inferring data rights from the repository's MIT code license.
The checked Zenodo records declare CC BY 4.0; keep specific terms/version/digest
evidence and use recipe-only disposition when preparing local converted rows.

The original code artifact has 2,037 ZIP entries; the Karaf raw archive has 1,256.
Both exceed the existing materializer v1's hard 128-entry ceiling. A real call
through the published 4.4.1 package rejects the Karaf ZIP with
`ZIP metadata exceeds declared resource limits`. This reader accepts already
pinned **decoded plain members**, not those unsupported archive containers.
Their acquisition/extraction needs a separately reviewed capability or tool;
relabeling an archive as an already validated ZIP would bypass the contract.
No archive policy or automatic fetch command is silently widened here.

### A bounded real-source check

The metadata has 620 Karaf builds, all with the processed label `single`.
All 620 have corresponding paths in the v3 raw archive, which contains another
106 reports. This establishes path coverage, not equivalence of the snapshots
or proof that any stage/test observations are independent.

The separately decoded report
`karaf/PR/PR-1581/testReport_build1.json.zip!testReport_build1.json`
has 508,512 bytes and SHA-256
`351f0bc92ad8659b170750eea61091689ae7258fbbd99b4b0f0d3f33be8f935b`.
The real reader produced:

| Fact | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Metadata rows read | 57,437 |
| Rows outside the selected build | 57,436 |
| Selected processed metadata stages | 1 |
| Raw suites | 228 |
| Reported method executions | 931 |
| Repeated class/method labels retained | 4 |
| Reported passed / failed / skipped methods | 892 / 0 / 39 |

This one descriptive slice is not a large-suite performance study, independent
verification of whole-build success, or a complete LRTS admission. The metadata
and raw count/duration declarations match for this pair. A source change must
still pass the actual correspondence checks; a filename alone proves no join.

The pinned extraction code filters skipped methods, rewrites some class names,
drops selected duplicates and rounds method sums to three places. Those processed
class values remain distinct from this reader's raw method outcomes. Retrospective
flaky labels, full-history outlier filters and FirstFail labels must not silently
become features available before a decision. Author baseline results are not
reproduced COLEMAN results.

## Units, clocks and compatibility

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    M[Pinned plain metadata and reviewed data terms] --> C[Existing immutable external cache]
    R[Pinned decoded Jenkins report and reviewed data terms] --> C
    C --> V[Bounded metadata selection and typed raw report]
    V --> D[Versioned source slice and explicit exclusion counts]
    D --> B[Blocked: outcome availability, stage mapping and expected universe]
    D --> A[Source-correspondence verification and immutable artifact]
    F[Owned constructed serial fixture] --> N[Existing native runner and checkpoint]
    N --> K[Independent exact known-answer check]
```

`LRTSSpec` and `LRTSDataset` require integer `schema_version=1` and recipe
`lrts-source-assessment-v1`. Missing/legacy/future versions and unknown fields
reject. There is no automatic migration from native Parquet, RTPTorrent,
filtered LRTS outcome tables or arbitrary JUnit XML. The exact 23-column paper
metadata header and Jenkins `hudson.tasks.junit.TestResult` layout are required.

The reader reuses `Measurement` for explicit binary64 projections and units.
All five metadata quantities remain separate: truncated build execution seconds,
truncated scheduled Unix-epoch seconds, reported JUnit duration, suite-duration
sum and processed-class-duration sum. No sum is labeled physical runner occupancy
or parallel elapsed savings. Numeric literals must round-trip through canonical
binary64 spelling; nonfinite, negative, underflowed or overprecise values reject.
Genuine signed zero canonicalizes to zero; blank metadata quantities and JSON
null durations retain `value=null`, `status=unavailable` and their declared units.
Null counters remain unavailable integers, never zero. Unsupported not-applicable
encodings reject instead of being invented.

The original `ts_duration`, `passcount`, `failcount` and `skipcount` columns are
build-report aggregates repeated across processed stage rows. They are checked
against the one selected build report. Processed stage sums and `num_*` counts
retain their own scope and may differ across stages. This check establishes no
mapping from processed stages to raw suite/node identities.

[Jenkins Run documentation](https://javadoc.jenkins.io/hudson/model/Run.html)
distinguishes scheduled time from executor start after queueing. The pinned LRTS
code truncates scheduled milliseconds and execution duration to seconds. Adding
those fields cannot certify completion when queue delay is unknown. The source's
`build_date` is also an uninterpreted producer label; its generating code used a
local-time conversion. Raw suite timestamp strings, node IDs and enclosing links
are retained without assigning them outcome-availability semantics.

Source execution identity includes project, PR, build, suite position, method
position and class/method labels. It is stable for the same declared source
executions, not a cross-build logical test mapping. Metadata sorts by processed
stage ID for serialization; raw arrays retain their positions. Identical selected
metadata duplicates have explicit exclusion counts; conflicts reject. Repeated
raw method labels remain separate executions and never become independent faults.
Only the selected build's numeric metadata is interpreted. Other physical rows
are counted as outside the selection after shape/identity checks, not certified
as fully validated observations.

PASSED/FIXED mean reported pass; FAILED/REGRESSION mean reported failure;
SKIPPED means not run. A null status remains unknown unless the source explicitly
says skipped. Contradictory skipped/status flags reject. ABORTED/NOT_BUILT and
other metadata build results remain visible. Neither passing cases nor aggregate
counters promote an unknown method into a pass or establish complete feedback.
The Jenkins exported `empty` flag must agree with the reported method count;
contradictions reject rather than being repaired or published.
Diagnostic text, plugin actions, age and failed-since hints are not decision features.

Limits are 32 MiB for metadata, 16 MiB for one decoded report, 100,000 physical
metadata rows, 16 KiB per CSV line, 1,024 characters per CSV field, 64 characters
per numeric CSV literal, 64 selected metadata stages, 5,000 raw suites and 50,000
reported methods. Limits may be lowered in the frozen spec where exposed.
These are bounded inputs, not an OS memory/CPU sandbox or global cache quota.

## Complete owned CI example

Install the verified 4.5 release wheel in an activated Python 3.14+ environment.
Copy the complete [owned CI example](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/examples/lrts/ci.py)
to `ci.py` outside the checkout. It authors both sources, uses the real cache and
reader, projects only its declared complete serial fixture to native Parquet,
runs Random/RNFail, checks independent exact references and reopens the learning
checkpoint. It downloads no third-party data and creates no observed CI timeline.

```bash
python ci.py owned-ci /absolute/path/outside-git/lrts-cache
python ci.py owned-ci /absolute/path/outside-git/lrts-cache
```

The two calls retain one native result row and the same converted artifact.
With that same copied `ci.py`, this complete SDK example also works outside Git:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from ci import owned_dataset
from coleman.artifacts import ArtifactWriter
from coleman.corpus import SourceCache
from coleman.corpus.lrts import convert_lrts_source, publish_lrts_dataset, validate_lrts_dataset

with TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
    root = Path(temporary)
    cache = SourceCache(root / "external-cache")
    owned, _ = owned_dataset(cache)
    dataset = convert_lrts_source(owned.spec, cache)
    assert len(dataset.cases) == 3
    validate_lrts_dataset(dataset, cache)
    artifact = publish_lrts_dataset(dataset, cache, ArtifactWriter(root / "exports"))
    assert artifact.exists()
    try:
        dataset.require_temporal_evaluation()
    except ValueError as error:
        print(error)  # Expected: source availability/stage/universe evidence is missing.
    else:
        raise AssertionError("A source-assessment slice entered protected evaluation")
```

The copied helper and MIT terms apply only to newly authored fixtures. For real
sources, construct `LRTSSpec` from separately verified permitted metadata/report
receipts and the explicit original report label; never reuse an owned fixture's
license for downloaded data. The cache remains outside Git and physically
separate from outputs. Converted recipe-only rows stay local.

`validate_lrts_dataset` recomputes from the actual pinned bytes; JSON reads alone
only check model invariants. Immutable publication reuses existing concurrent
retry, conflict and interrupted-write behavior, without writing a learning
checkpoint or marking an experiment complete. Filesystem durability/process-kill
temporary-file limits remain those of the artifact writer. The registry and its
original descriptive readiness meanings are unchanged. Separate
[controlled captures](controlled-faults.md), [stress cases](ci-stress-laboratory.md),
[baseline matrices](comparable-baselines.md) and [public CI feasibility](public-ci-feasibility.md)
are implemented at their documented scopes. The final historical confirmation
remains [unfinished](roadmap.md#historical-corpus-status).

## Continue the workflow

Run the [Karaf data path](lrts-parquet-etl.md) or choose [larger stage views](lrts-stage-views.md).
Check [source admission](corpus-admission.md) before making historical effectiveness claims.



### FILE: docs/maintainability.md

# Maintainability review and improvement priorities

This review connects architectural measurements to concrete maintenance choices.
It does not certify the absence of defects. The baseline is the published
4.19.0 source; documentation changes do not establish runtime performance gains.

## What the measurements say

| Dimension | Baseline observation | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SDK size | 276 Python modules; 47,408 source lines | A substantial platform needs a navigable public surface and explicit boundaries |
| Cyclomatic complexity | Maximum callable complexity 20; no callable above Radon C | The current Xenon limits pass; some validation/orchestration paths are near the block limit |
| Average callable complexity | Approximately 4.54, Radon A, across 1,763 distinct reported callable blocks | A low average does not remove local hotspots |
| Maintainability index | All modules A; minimum approximately 22.15 | Some modules are close to the MI ≥ 20 floor |
| Docstring presence | Existing coverage gate requires 100% | Presence alone does not verify parameter or semantic documentation |
| NumPy parameter coverage | 495 of 622 audited public-named signatures had missing parameter entries | A separate documentation backlog was hidden by the presence gate |

The parameter audit counts explicitly defined public functions/methods and
constructors in public classes. Constructor documentation can live on the class.
It excludes function-local/private definitions, does not decide API stability,
and does not inspect generated Pydantic constructor fields or validate description
accuracy. The counts are signature findings, not a count of independently supported
user-facing APIs.

The documentation revision completes **32 audited signatures across seven entry-point
modules**, including experiment execution, artifact publication, domain records,
source materialization and existing spec I/O/identity/sweep functions. The same
repository-wide audit now reports **472 signatures with missing entries**.
Class field descriptions, units, errors, side effects and limits in the edited
contracts were reviewed manually. The global backlog remains explicit; this is
not a claim of complete NumPy documentation across the SDK.

## Architecture: retain the engine, clarify the surface

The [architecture guide](setup.md) maps the current boundaries. The native runner,
RunSpec, results sinks, source cache, artifacts and checkpoints already provide
the reusable mechanisms. Existing domain/import-boundary tests protect separation
from CLI/MCP and transport dependencies.

A wholesale rewrite is not justified by the current structural evidence. The
higher-value redesign is the reader and integration surface: connected task guides,
a complete installed example, a coherent API index and honest evidence status.

The core identity/version contracts are compatibility-sensitive. Avoid moving
large numbers of classes simply to make the folder tree look uniform. Choose a
small internal boundary when an actual behavioral change requires it, preserve
legacy readers/goldens and check import boundaries and installed behavior.

## Hotspots worth understanding

| Location | Measured callable complexity | Maintenance direction |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `application/baseline_observations.py::_check_native` | 20 | Preserve independent native-result checks; isolate an invariant only when its semantics and error ordering remain clear |
| `resources/replay.py::ResourceReplayRun.accounting` | 20 | Keep resource categories and conservation checks visible; do not collapse unknown costs into zero |
