requires a matching persisted receipt and frozen contract, then atomically publishes
validated report content. Point estimates must be present for uncertainty or
confirmatory claims, follow the protocol-defined sign (relative tolerance `1e-12`,
zero absolute tolerance) and lie within their reported interval. Report validation
recomputes Holm corrections from the complete frozen raw p-value family (unavailable
tests count as p=1); stored adjusted values must match that deterministic calculation
exactly. Every report embeds its versioned raw records and verifies their logical
keys and content digests. Reading or persisting a report recomputes the complete
frozen method from those records. Scalar agreement permits relative `1e-12` and
absolute `1e-15` numerical variation across compatible libraries; counts, reasons
and conclusions must agree exactly, so a threshold crossing fails closed.
Failed evaluation leaves the attempt and creates no completed report. Replaying
the same report/sink publication is idempotent.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Metadata[Point-in-time metadata] --> Split[Typed split and exclusion decisions]
    Candidates[Complete candidate configurations] --> Freeze[Immutable frozen protocol and family]
    Split --> Freeze
    Freeze --> Runner[Existing native runner extension]
    Runner --> Records[Versioned raw CI measurements]
    Freeze --> Reserve[Durable access receipt before outcome loading]
    Reserve --> Load[Typed protected outcome loader]
    Records --> Load
    Load --> Check[Unit, provenance, pairing and temporal validation]
    Check --> Method[Frozen method and assumptions]
    Method --> Student[Legacy paired Student t]
    Method --> Bounded[Known-bound independent paired means]
    Student --> Compare[Paired effects, Holm p-values, simultaneous intervals]
    Bounded --> Compare
    Compare --> Report[Versioned report with embedded raw records, keys and digests]
    Report --> Artifacts[Existing ArtifactWriter, local sinks and manifest]
```

## Paired method and conservative conclusions

`PairedObservation` links a candidate ID, `TemporalObservation` and `DomainRecord`.
The metadata's group is the independent unit. Exactly one result per candidate/unit
is accepted, with the same metadata across the pair. Repeated seeds/revisions on
one unit raise `ValueError`. Raw record logical keys must also be globally unique
across every candidate and unit in the report, even if candidate names, metadata
labels, provenance, values or content digests differ; use a predeclared
upstream aggregation if replicates
are required. The evaluator verifies frozen dataset/configuration/context
fingerprints, observed availability and metric units/meaning/objective before
calculating a comparison. Unpaired units and incompatible measurements fail.

The legacy `EvaluationProtocol` provides paired Student-t inference for a **declared normal population of
independent pair differences**. Serial/clustered units or an undeclared normality
assumption raise `NotImplementedError` before loading outcomes. Adjacent builds from
one real repository generally need a justified dependence model; labeling them with
different seeds does not supply one. No automatic normality or independence detector
is provided. Normality/independence declarations are assumptions to justify in a
study, not certifications inferred by the library.

The implementation applies a one-sample t procedure to paired differences,
equivalent to [SciPy's paired t procedure](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.ttest_rel.html).
[Holm's original step-down procedure](https://www.jstor.org/stable/4615733) controls family-wise error across the
entire frozen family; unavailable comparisons remain in that family as p=1.
See the [reference Holm implementation](https://github.com/statsmodels/statsmodels/blob/main/statsmodels/stats/multitest.py).
Intervals use the conservative simultaneous Bonferroni level `1 - alpha/m`, where
`m` is the full family size. They are not unadjusted individual intervals or Holm
intervals. Cross-hypothesis independence is not required by these corrections.

`raw_mean_difference` is candidate minus baseline, in the original metric unit.
`improvement` reverses its sign for minimization. A confirmatory benefit/harm needs
both a Holm-adjusted p-value within alpha and a simultaneous interval entirely
beyond the signed practical-effect threshold. Otherwise the result is inconclusive.
There is **no automatic policy promotion**. Confidence intervals are conditional on
the declared sampling assumptions; p-values are not calibrated failure probabilities
or learning rewards.

Too few units, incomplete outcomes, identical pair differences or nonfinite
uncertainty yield `insufficient_evidence`, with raw signed means retained where
well-defined and unavailable uncertainty represented as null. Unknown outcomes are
not silently removed for a complete-case test. A negative result remains visible.
On a reused holdout, numerical estimates remain available, but a confirmatory
benefit/harm conclusion is suppressed; inspect `confirmatory_eligible` and the
receipt's `prior_test_accesses`. First recorded access means first **within the
complete declared audit history**, not proof that nobody ever saw those data.

Reports contain the complete freeze, access receipt, independent unit IDs, estimates,
conclusions and each embedded raw record's logical key/content digest plus temporal
metadata. The required UTC `completed_at` records when calculation and source
reference assembly finish, after the protected loader and inference. It cannot
predate the access receipt or consumed outcomes. Exported comparison records use
this completion time as `available_at`, never the earlier access request time.
Use the embedded records to verify results against immutable sink records; reserve a
test/verification access before inspecting protected raw outcomes again.
`FamilyReport.domain_records(run_id)` exports [versioned measurements](domain-results.md) with explicit
units/signs/unavailable states and no synthetic learning reward. The full report
retains statistical conclusions and access context that a scalar alone cannot convey.

## Runnable installed-package workflow

Install the reviewed wheel, then copy and run
[ci.py](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/examples/protected-evaluation/ci.py)
from a directory outside the repository:

```bash
pip install path/to/coleman.whl
python ci.py ./protected-ci-output
```

The standalone script freezes Greedy/Random RunSpecs before invoking
`run_with_extension`. Four synthetic repository units exercise the real native
runner, RNFail reward, NAPFD metric and Parquet sink. It traces candidate fingerprints
to saved specs, publishes a queryable report and versioned measurement records, and generates a
manifest. It intentionally returns `insufficient_evidence` for four units under a
20-unit minimum. A repeated access is recorded as reuse before the final manifest
is generated, so both receipts appear in its inventory. These synthetic repositories
validate plumbing, not production independence, normality, effectiveness or ROI.

## Compatibility and limits

Frozen/access/report artifacts require integer `schema_version=1`. Duplicate JSON
keys, unknown fields and missing/older/future versions are rejected. No automatic
migration invents missing provenance, units or access history. Legacy native results,
RunSpec IDs, sweep APIs and descriptive reports retain their existing readers and
behavior. Existing domain records can be evaluated only if they already carry the
matching frozen context and candidate configuration; never relabel old artifacts
silently to claim protected evidence.

The legacy method excludes serial/block/cluster and distribution-free inference;
the new [bounded method](bounded-paired-evaluation.md) adds conservative independent
paired means and explicit practical equivalence. Neither method implements
serial/block/cluster inference, rank/bootstrap intervals, sequential testing/alpha spending, unknown external state verification,
remote artifact transactions and policy activation. Access-history scanning is
linear in scope history, and contention retries are bounded at 1000 publications.
Reports retain the complete consumed record payload and recompute estimates on
validation; their size and verification cost grow with the paired input. Record
hashes and recomputation establish internal consistency, not authenticity of an
externally supplied dataset or proof of independent sampling.
Keep confirmatory access scarce and predeclared. Use the
[independent decision benchmarks](decision-benchmarks.md) for mathematical checks.
The final historical cross-corpus confirmation remains [unfinished](roadmap.md).

::: coleman.evaluation.protected

## Continue the workflow

Prepare [repeated inference units](corpus-evaluation.md), consider the supported [bounded
protocol](bounded-paired-evaluation.md), and interpret conclusions through the [evaluation
guide](evaluation-guide.md).



### FILE: docs/public-ci-feasibility.md

# Public CI collection feasibility

**Observe what public CI actually exposes before designing a TCPCI study.**
This bounded GitHub Actions reference example uses the **published COLEMAN 4.17
base wheel**. The collector is a separate, version-pinned example, not a new SDK
provider, a production ingestion service or a prospective savings experiment.
It makes two explicitly requested anonymous metadata reads for one public run.
It does not trigger workflows, download logs or artifacts, execute source code,
rank tests or change CI decisions.

## Reproduce outside the checkout

In an activated Python 3.14+ environment:

```bash
python -m pip install "https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.17.0/coleman-4.17.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=e5a272ddc0edf72bd909a743fa2b3bc0dfeb8a02871c487ab22683cddeea40ca"
curl --fail --location \
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/198ddb3e65d2027f4fd287a0f222a25160677bd4/examples/public-ci-feasibility/ci.py" \
  --output /tmp/coleman-public-ci.py
python /tmp/coleman-public-ci.py \
  --repository jacksonpradolima/coleman --run-id 39170199990 \
  --capture-id public-example-1 --output /tmp/public-ci-evidence --fetch
# Same immutable capture; no network and no restamped receipts:
python /tmp/coleman-public-ci.py \
  --repository jacksonpradolima/coleman --run-id 39170199990 \
  --capture-id public-example-1 --output /tmp/public-ci-evidence
```

The downloaded script SHA-256 is
`f926725a49f62d8cb68dd80596d4fe9b66ade3b90f1331fbfc513f475f4dd2ef`.
Verify that digest before executing the example.

The public run can eventually disappear or become inaccessible. A missing run,
HTTP error, rate limit, redirect or incompatible response fails rather than
substituting fabricated data. Choose a known, canonical, **public** repository/run
and a new `capture-id` for a later poll. Changing the runtime or example bytes
creates another scope. There is no scheduler or automatic retry loop.
The ordinary tests use tiny owned fixtures and require no network.

The JSON summary prints the capture directory, stable logical run/attempt ID,
normalized semantic fingerprint, returned job count and
`insufficient_evidence_for_forward_tcpci`. This is a valid feasibility outcome.
Inspect the typed result by loading that same example module and calling
`read_capture(Path(capture_directory))`; `snapshot.measurements`,
`snapshot.reality` and `snapshot.history()` expose the existing SDK contracts.
No new CLI installation, MCP dependency or core transport API is required.

## What the endpoints establish

The example requests API version `2022-11-28` and records the returned selected
version when present. It reads the
[workflow run](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs?apiVersion=2022-11-28)
and the [jobs for its explicit attempt](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-jobs?apiVersion=2022-11-28).
Unknown provider fields remain in original response text; only declared fields
enter the typed projection. These endpoints are separate reads, not an atomic
provider transaction. A job may finish between them. Reported run and job
statuses can therefore differ without implying corruption.

| Question | Observable metadata | Remaining boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Logical identity | Repository numeric ID, run ID, attempt, job ID, source SHA | A poll or rerun is not an independent project/build observation |
| Trigger and branch | Reported event and nullable head branch | Branch protection, override authority and policy decisions are unverified |
| Tests, variants and shards | Job names, step ordinals/names and labels | Names do not establish test identities, required membership, shard topology or configuration coverage |
| Completion | Job/step status, nullable conclusion and timestamps | Job success is not a per-test verdict; partial or absent tests remain unknown |
| Timing and costs | Recorded start/end envelope, in seconds | Physical runner occupancy, billed time, queue and shared setup are unavailable |
| Retries and cancellation | Current workflow attempt and explicit job cancellation/timeout conclusions | No test retry, quarantine, cause or cross-attempt correction lineage |
| Availability | Actual local receipt of each complete response | Upstream first availability, a pre-outcome decision seal and missed transitions are unknown |
| Retention | Bytes actually captured now | No historical completeness guarantee; deleted runs/logs/artifacts cannot be reconstructed |

A completed interval with equal timestamps has **observed zero envelope seconds**,
not zero CPU or test work. A completed job missing a clock has `null/unknown`.
An incomplete job has `null/unavailable`. Uncollected physical costs and expected
test count are `null/unavailable`; this observer's policy inference is
`null/not_applicable`. Negative envelope durations reject. Non-finite numeric
JSON, duplicate keys, duplicate job IDs/step ordinals, incompatible units or
fabricated physical measurements reject. Provider timestamps later than their
local receipt reject; the example assumes comparable UTC clocks and does not
correct skew or invent availability estimates.

## Artifacts, recovery and domain boundaries

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    G[Public run and explicit-attempt jobs] --> E[Standalone bounded HTTPS example]
    E --> R[Immutable original bytes and local receipts]
    R --> S[Versioned typed snapshot]
    S --> F[Existing 35-axis reality vocabulary]
    S --> H[Existing point-in-time observation history]
    R --> C[Completion published last]
    S --> B[TCPCI admission remains blocked]
```

The capture directory is scoped by pre-data request, installed-runtime and
example-byte fingerprints. `request.json`, `run.json`, `jobs.json` and
`snapshot.json` are committed with the existing `ArtifactWriter`; `complete.json`
publishes last. Completion means this bounded response inventory is materialized,
**not** that CI completed or every expected test/job was observed. A partial or
empty current job inventory may be a valid metadata capture.

Each response envelope commits the original UTF-8 text, its exact SHA-256, URL,
actual local receipt and selected API version together. Normalized contract
fingerprints intentionally ignore outer artifact JSON whitespace. Original
provider text whitespace/order remains covered by its separate byte digest.
The normalized semantic fingerprint excludes collector receipts/runtime; the
logical identity excludes poll IDs. Digests establish consistency, not source
authenticity, authorship, lawful reuse or statistical independence.

The existing trusted-local POSIX process lock rejects concurrent ownership and
releases on process death; callers must serialize threads themselves. Repeating
a completed request verifies and returns its first committed records unchanged.
After interruption, only missing response checkpoints need fetching; existing
receipts are not restamped. A response received but lost before its atomic
commit is unrecorded; recovery may acquire a later response with a later receipt.
The reader fails closed on missing/changed content, source mismatch or future
versions. All new contracts require integer schema version 1. There is no older
collector schema to migrate; native Parquet/results/checkpoints remain untouched.
A future collector migration must be explicit, retaining original bytes and
semantics rather than rewriting a completed v1 capture.

`snapshot.history()` uses the **materialized snapshot as the source producer**:
only observed completed job intervals enter the point-in-time observation history,
with availability and receipt at snapshot assembly. The original HTTP receipts remain separate.
This conservative offline projection never asserts when the provider first
exposed a field. An unfinished interval produces no completed observation.
Each poll is a distinct predeclared source; this is not an appendable receiver
with global first-receipt/correction lineage. It does not synthesize prospective
build admissions, feedback or a decision seal.

Every snapshot also supplies all **35 existing production-reality axes**. Source
identities, trigger, current attempt and runner labels can be reported; explicit
cancellation, timeout and partial metadata can be retained when present. Other
axes retain missing values and limitations. Owned fixtures label their positive
facts `synthetic`. This view is not a `NativeSourceProfile`, data card or automatic
entry in the admitted benchmark corpus.

## Permissions, resources and public data handling

The [provider endpoint documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-jobs?apiVersion=2022-11-28)
permits unauthenticated access to public resources; authenticated production access
requires a separate permission design. This example supplies no token, cookie or
credential lookup and refuses private or unverifiable base/head repositories
before persisting the run response. It never follows redirects or enumerates
repositories. A repository becoming private/inaccessible causes acquisition to
fail; an existing local capture is not automatically revoked or erased.

Each body is capped at **2 MiB**, one complete jobs page at **100 jobs**, and each
job at **256 steps**. Larger/truncated inventories reject; no silent pagination
loss. Socket waits are capped at 10 seconds, with a cooperative 30-second body
window and 64 KiB reads. OS/DNS/socket waits are not a hard wall-time sandbox.
Budget/rate-limit/backoff and scalable pagination are deferred. Use trusted local
storage; there is no hostile-filesystem sandbox or authenticated audit service.

Public metadata can expose account names, email addresses, repository and runner
identifiers in raw fields. Outputs stay outside Git; do not publish raw responses
without a separate disclosure and terms review. Visibility does not grant a
benchmark redistribution license. Preserve component terms, citations and
permission provenance for any future corpus. This study publishes aggregate
facts and source identifiers, not foreign raw payloads. It collects no logs or
artifact bodies. Provider
[retention and limits](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits)
and [artifact availability](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/artifacts)
constrain historical recovery; a collector needs its own authorized retention and
deletion policy. Never execute untrusted workflow contents; consult the provider's
[secure-use guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use)
before extending this example.

## Actual bounded study and the next gate

On 2026-10-18 the separate example ran **outside the checkout against the actual
published 4.17 wheel**, through anonymous public HTTPS, on COLEMAN's
[run 39170199990](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/actions/runs/39170199990),
attempt 1, job 117801477664. Both fixed-version endpoint reads succeeded; the
reader verified their original byte digests and projection. Offline retry kept
all committed files unchanged. This qualifies acquisition and deterministic
local recovery for that bounded metadata profile, not general provider coverage.

Earlier exploratory reads of the same public run observed in-progress and
terminal metadata separately. The first receipt was **21:59:49 UTC**, after the
job began at **21:58:56** and its test step at **21:59:07**. The run's `updated_at`
was **21:58:56**, which cannot establish availability of that later step. Actual
unfinished `completed_at`/conclusion fields were JSON null. Those exploratory
reads used a different all-attempt endpoint and did not record API-version
selection; they are not relabeled as the pinned example's receipts. They show
why a reconstructed timestamp must not stand in for a sealed decision.

The feasible next path is an explicitly authorized collector that records an
expected test/shard universe and pre-outcome decision seal, first local receipts,
physical cost boundaries, correction lineage and privacy/retention policy while
leaving protected CI decisions unchanged. The current metadata-only path is
**blocked for forward TCPCI evaluation**. Use observation-only collection and
retain the existing CI order until those contracts are satisfied; do not claim
savings, calibrated probabilities, causality or algorithm promotion.

This completes the bounded public collection-feasibility scope. The final
historical confirmation was [closed with unmet criteria](roadmap.md#historical-corpus-status),
without claiming completion. Four required historical/HCS regimes remain unadmitted; the
[corpus admission report](corpus-admission.md) and
[repeated-evaluation protocol](corpus-evaluation.md) remain authoritative. More
polls, seeds or constructed cases cannot fill those independent-evidence gaps.

## Continue the workflow

Use [point-in-time observations](point-in-time-observations.md) for retained metadata, then follow
the [integration guide](integration-guide.md) to identify what a prospective study still needs.



### FILE: docs/python-source-capture.md

# Reproduce a controlled Python fault

COLEMAN can collect unchanged buggy and fixed PySnooper source against one common
upstream pytest fixture. Two frozen locale profiles show why execution conditions
belong in result provenance: the original Unicode error reproduces under the
declared ASCII locale, while both revisions pass under UTF-8.

This optional producer reuses [controlled observations](controlled-faults.md),
source views, the verified external cache and immutable artifacts. Native TCPCI
experiments continue to use the existing application API, policies and checkpoints.
No historical CI events or scheduling costs are inferred from source execution.

The installation below uses the current collector. The initial Docker outcomes
retain their original qualifications; they were not recollected with the current release.
Capture producers bind the whole SDK and package version, so reopening old
observations requires their original package. The [4.15 admission adapter](corpus-admission.md)
revalidates the retained 4.13 captures with their original pinned wheel and raw
parsers; unchanged legacy capture code alone cannot relabel a producer.

## Install and collect outside checkout

The SDK requires Python 3.14+, uv and POSIX. These presets additionally require a
native Linux arm64 Docker engine. The subject interpreter is separately pinned to
CPython 3.8.1; it does not change the SDK's Python requirement. Other architectures
need independently reviewed recipes and runtime qualification.

Install the published **4.17 wheel** into a fresh external environment. The
SHA-256 fragment verifies the release bytes before installation; no checkout is
required. Runtime preparation is a separate, explicit operator action.

```bash
uv venv /tmp/coleman-python-env --python 3.14
uv pip install --python /tmp/coleman-python-env/bin/python "https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.17.0/coleman-4.17.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=e5a272ddc0edf72bd909a743fa2b3bc0dfeb8a02871c487ab22683cddeea40ca"

# Explicit operator preparation; the producer never pulls an image.
docker pull --platform linux/arm64 docker.io/library/python@sha256:ffae7d875975e38d38378ce65d10ab62c2156eb198e2e798664ec6c793015c03

mkdir -p /tmp/coleman-python-workspace
cd /tmp/coleman-python-workspace
/tmp/coleman-python-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.python \
  --preset pysnooper-1-ascii-v1 --trial python-source-trial-1 \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-python-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-python-observations --fetch > ascii-summary.json

# Collect the predeclared contrast, sharing the same fault/dependence group.
/tmp/coleman-python-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.python \
  --preset pysnooper-1-utf8-v1 --trial python-source-trial-1 \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-python-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-python-observations --fetch > utf8-summary.json

# Same recipe/trial/producer: revalidate and replay, without executing tests again.
/tmp/coleman-python-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.python \
  --preset pysnooper-1-ascii-v1 --trial python-source-trial-1 \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-python-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-python-observations
```

Only explicit `--fetch` permits the individually pinned public source, wheel and
notice downloads. Runtime acquisition is separate; subject containers have no
network. Source cache, observations and system temporary directories must be
outside Git, and cache/output roots must be separate. No foreign source, wheel,
fixture or raw outcome is bundled in COLEMAN.

The summary reports dataset, state and receipt paths, role statuses, planned,
unobserved and classified pairs. Exit 0 means both protocols completed, including
negative test outcomes. Incomplete evidence has status `incomplete`, no completion
marker and exit 2. Invalid source/state or infrastructure failures raise instead
of becoming successful tests. The CLI also accepts a bounded versioned recipe via
`--recipe-stdin`; recipe fields cannot supply shell commands.

## Frozen source and environment

The source and environment were frozen before observing subject outcomes.
Both profiles use the inputs listed below.

The qualified observer pins its harness and uses an atomically allocated
mode0700 temporary directory in container tmpfs for dependency storage.
Subject/fixture/test, wheel, image and locale declarations remain unchanged;
original packets and their original producer are retained without reinterpretation.

| Input | Frozen selection |
| --- | --- |
| Buggy source | PySnooper `e21a31162f4c54be693d8ca8260e42393b39abd3`, the direct parent of the fix |
| Fixed source | PySnooper `56f22f8ffe1c6b2be4d2cf3ad1987fdb66113da2`, upstream issue 124 |
| Production trees | All five original `pysnooper/*.py` files and LICENSE in each revision |
| Common fixture | Unchanged fixed-tree `tests/__init__.py`, `tests/utils.py`, `tests/test_chinese.py`, LICENSE |
| Selected test | Exactly `tests/test_chinese.py::test_chinese`; an explicitly partial suite |
| Runtime | Official CPython 3.8.1, native linux/arm64, image digest in the command above |
| Contexts | `C` / `ANSI_X3.4-1968` / filesystem ascii; `C.UTF-8` / `UTF-8` / filesystem utf-8 |
| Shared flags | TZ=UTC; PYTHONUTF8=0; PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0; PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8; PYTHONHASHSEED=0; no bytecode or automatic pytest plugins |
| Parent guards | 60 seconds and 1 MiB combined stdout/stderr per observed Docker process |
| Container guards | Non-root, read-only, no network/capabilities, no-new-privileges, 2 CPUs, 64 PIDs, 1 GiB memory, 128 MiB tmpfs |

The original unpinned bootstrap is replaced explicitly. Eight exact pure wheels
are installed only inside container tmpfs, with isolated pip, no index, dependency
resolution, source builds, project `setup.py` or compilation. The image supplies
pip 20.0.2, setuptools 45.1.0 and wheel 0.34.2 unchanged. Actual interpreter,
architecture, locale, encoding, distribution versions and selected discovery are
checked against the frozen bootstrap plan before promoting case evidence.

The bootstrap plan declares `private-runtime-tempdir-v1`. Python's temporary
directory API allocates the actual dependency location atomically with mode0700
and removes it after observation; no predictable shared directory is trusted.

The parent deadline covers the observed Docker process, including interpreter and
wheel installation overhead. It does not bound the entire acquisition workflow,
staging or the separate cleanup command. The historical image is a benchmark
condition; SDK dependency audits do not establish its security or support status.

## Component terms and attribution

Every input has independent byte/version/terms pins. The subject and selected
fixture retain their MIT LICENSE. Four production files have explicit MIT headers;
`variables.py` relies on the project LICENSE and is not described as separately
headed. BugsInPy `11c5f1eea954a42132cfd06bf257766a7963e0fd` is a curation reference;
its framework code, patches and fixtures are not copied.

| Wheel | Version | Recorded component terms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| exceptiongroup | 1.3.1 | MIT and copied Python standard-library PSF notice |
| iniconfig | 2.1.0 | MIT |
| packaging | 26.2 | Apache-2.0 OR BSD-2-Clause; both complete texts retained |
| pluggy | 1.5.0 | MIT |
| pytest | 8.3.5 | MIT |
| python-toolbox | 1.3.2 | Component review below; not blanket MIT |
| tomli | 2.5.0 | MIT |
| typing-extensions | 4.13.2 | PSF declaration; complete historical Python license text retained |

PythonToolbox's root MIT notice lists Envelopes (MIT), SortedContainers
(Apache-2.0) and decorator (BSD; its actual header has two clauses). Two unused
GUI files declare the wxPython license. The [official wxPython license page](https://wxpython.org/pages/license/)
identifies wxWindows 3.1; pinned wxWidgets licence, LGPL, GPL and preamble files
are retained separately. SortedContainers' original copyright/license notice and
the full Apache license text are retained separately as well.

The unused `test_python_toolbox/third_party/forked_mapping_tests.py` has no own
notice. Similarity with public CPython 3.3.0 mapping tests suggests copied or
derived code; exact origin is **not established**. The typed component record
labels this attribution as inferred and retains the full pinned CPython LICENSE
conservatively. This remains an explicit source-admission limitation. A recorded
terms review is not proof of legal permission or provenance for unreviewed inputs.

All original wheel bytes remain intact. The producer separately inspects selected
metadata/notices with the existing bounded ZIP reader, while checking every
entry's path/type/local metadata and whole-archive sizes. Unselected member bodies
are bound by the whole-wheel SHA-256, not independently decoded or certified.
PythonToolbox's original Python installation script has its own pin; pip may
install it but does not execute it. No dependencies are silently stripped or
fixtures patched to avoid inconvenient imports.

## Outcomes, units and evidence limits

The first installed qualification collected four role observations across the two
contexts, with identical source/fixture bytes:

| Locale | Buggy | Fixed | Unchanged generic classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C / ASCII | `test_error`, `builtins.UnicodeEncodeError` | `passed` | `inconclusive` |
| C.UTF-8 | `passed` | `passed` | `both_pass` |

The ASCII run reproduces the observed failure/fix under its declared conditions.
The generic classifier reserves `expected` for assertion-failure-to-pass pairs;
an exception is never relabeled to increase that count. The UTF-8 contrast is a
valid negative reproduction context. These are one curated fix and one selected
test, not two independent bugs, a full suite or a generalization result.

Case elapsed values are nonnegative integer **nanoseconds** spanning pytest
setup/call/teardown and observation overhead. Parent elapsed values are separately
labeled producer-process nanoseconds. Neither is removable CI runner work,
end-to-end savings or evidence of a faster policy. Actual UTC capture instants
have explicitly declared microsecond precision and are not historical CI clocks.
Observed zero remains zero. Missing/uncommitted observations have unavailable
counters, not imputed zero. Negative process exit codes are valid POSIX facts;
negative elapsed, non-finite quantities and incompatible units reject.

Raw packets retain bounded observer stdout/stderr and actual pytest exception/skip
diagnostics. They are not a complete filesystem or I/O audit of the subject.
Malformed records never promote cases. Valid partial streams can retain completed
cases before interruption; missing cases stay unobserved. Setup/teardown and other
non-assertion exceptions remain test errors. Scientific admission and temporal
evaluation remain separate: `constructed`, `not_evaluated`, `insufficient_evidence`.

## Recovery and offline validation

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R[Typed source and component recipe] --> C[Existing verified external cache]
    C --> P[Immutable pre-execution plan]
    P --> S[Durable role ownership]
    S --> K[Shared optional transport isolation guards]
    K --> D[Bounded Docker: private dependencies and pytest]
    D --> B[Atomic raw role packets]
    B --> V[Reparse and bind actual protocol]
    V --> G[Existing controlled dataset and immutable artifacts]
    G --> I[Typed receipt]
    I --> F[Completion only if both roles collected]
    S --> X[Uncommitted recovery: interrupted and unavailable]
    X --> V
```

Python, C and JUnit share container isolation arguments. Each retains its own
runtime, observer and wire contracts; Python keeps its original scratch mount
semantics. The Python and C CLIs share argument parsing and accounting display.
These helpers live in the optional transports; the controlled domain remains
independent of CLI and runtime execution.

A nonblocking POSIX lock prevents concurrent producers within the same output
generation from observing the recipe/trial/implementation twice. Separate output
roots do not share a distributed execution ledger; choose meaningful trial IDs
and retain dependence groups when combining evidence. Start markers precede spawning, and role
packets follow cleanup of only that deterministic producer-owned container.
Unconfirmed cleanup leaves recoverable ownership. A crashed, uncommitted role
becomes `interrupted`; fresh observation requires a new trial ID. Completed roles
are reused. A real installed-process kill/recovery test exercises this behavior.

Receipt and completion are written after raw/context/normalized-data validation;
incomplete collection never acquires `complete.json`. Completed replay works
without Docker. A missing role cannot be replaced by a completion marker, and
changed runtime facts cannot be mixed into an unfinished trial.

Use the typed Python API after the collection commands above:

```python
from coleman.artifacts import ArtifactWriter
from coleman.corpus import SourceCache
from coleman.transports.python import load_python_recipe
from coleman.transports.python_capture import capture_python_source, validate_python_capture
from coleman.transports.python_contracts import PythonCapturePlan

cache = SourceCache("/tmp/coleman-python-source-cache")
writer = ArtifactWriter("/tmp/coleman-python-observations")
result = capture_python_source(load_python_recipe(), cache, writer, "python-source-trial-1")
plan = PythonCapturePlan.from_json((result.state_directory / "plan.json").read_bytes())
validate_python_capture(result.receipt, plan, result.dataset, cache)
assert result.receipt.status == "collected"
assert result.dataset.admission == "not_evaluated"
print(result.dataset.pairs[0].classification)  # inconclusive; original exception retained
```

Validation rebuilds the context, reparses original raw packets and compares every
normalized observation and receipt reference. Recomputed hashes do not legitimize
rewritten outcomes. These checks establish consistency, not authentication that a
hostile subject could never forge observer output.

All new records require explicit schema version 1. Missing, old, future or
unknown versions reject without implicit migration. Existing controlled/JUnit
artifacts retain their original contracts and meanings. Generic controlled
datasets remain readable through the unchanged domain API. Transport replay binds
all COLEMAN packaged bytes and version, excluding hidden/cache/bytecode files;
a changed package creates a new generation. To validate an older producer's
transport artifacts, use its original reviewed package. No automatic cross-version
rewrite or copy of old observations into a new identity is performed.

Native CI/checkpoint integration is tested separately with the owned exact-answer
[controlled CI example](controlled-faults.md). Controlled Python timing is never
fabricated into a historical build or native scheduling-cost dataset. Broader
source admission, diversity and comparative evidence have their own
[evidence requirements](roadmap.md).

Multi-case raw replay compares observations in the generic domain's canonical
logical-key order. This validation correction preserves original raw/report
bytes and case order; it does not migrate or reinterpret prior artifacts.

Physical container ownership includes the resolved output namespace. Equal logical
trials in separate output roots cannot collide or clean each other's containers;
observation identities retain their original meaning. Keep incomplete ownership
state at its original output location for recovery, and retain the original
reviewed producer package when reopening older captures.

[Pre-execution protocol records](release-history.md#pre-execution-protocol-records)
retain the historical declaration evidence for audit.

## Continue the workflow

Interpret the pair through [controlled observations](controlled-faults.md), retain its
source/context lineage in [source admission](corpus-admission.md), and compare evidence types in
[datasets](datasets.md).



### FILE: docs/quality-and-security.md

# Inspect COLEMAN's quality and security

You should be able to inspect the engineering behind a CI decision platform as
readily as its experiment outputs. COLEMAN exposes test results, advisory audit
receipts, structural limits, documentation checks and signed release artifacts.
Use this page to find that evidence and understand what each check establishes.

## Read the badges

The README links each badge to its evidence. Workflow badges show the latest
matching execution: tests and documentation use pushes to `main`, while lint and
structural checks use pull-request events. A PR badge can therefore describe a
different commit from the latest published release. Check its commit and event
before relying on it for a particular revision.

The **coverage gate 95%** badge describes the configured minimum, not a measured
percentage. Open the test run's log for its actual combined line/branch coverage,
passed tests and skips. The [coverage configuration](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/pyproject.toml)
defines the threshold, included source and exclusions. Coverage.py evaluates
the gate using its reporting precision; the current configuration uses the
default whole-percent rounding. Inspect the measured result and configuration
when a comparison requires finer precision.

Sonar badges report detected source vulnerabilities and a security rating in the
[COLEMAN dashboard](https://sonarcloud.io/summary/overall?id=jacksonpradolima_coleman4hcs).
The service retains `coleman4hcs` in its project identifier. This is the dashboard
linked by current source-analysis checks; its analysis revision and date identify
the code measured. Dependency advisories have their own audit and are not counted
by the source-vulnerability badge.

The former Codecov dashboard also retains the old identifier, but its public
`main` report is historical. It is not used as a current-coverage badge. Current
coverage qualification uses the pytest coverage gate and the matching Actions log.
Consult [GitHub's badge semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/monitor-workflows/add-a-status-badge)
for branch and event selection.

## Tests and coverage

The [test workflow](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/actions/workflows/codecov.yml)
runs the Python 3.14 suite with branch measurement and a **configured 95% combined
line/branch coverage gate**. Its frozen environment includes the optional MCP extra
for integration tests. The log retains the exact test count, coverage and skips;
a new test count does not require manually updating the README.

Tests cover native prioritization and source adapters as well as failure modes:

- Versioned result round-trips, golden artifacts, legacy readers and unsupported versions.
- Units, explicit missingness, valid signed values and non-finite rejection.
- Deterministic identities and digests, duplicate handling and idempotent replay.
- Interrupted publication and checkpoint continuation.
- Application/transport import boundaries and optional integration behavior.
- Installed-package decision benchmarks and small, owned CI fixtures.

Examples of the executable contracts live in
[result tests](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/tree/main/tests/results),
[artifact tests](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/tests/test_artifacts.py),
[checkpoint tests](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/tree/main/tests/checkpoint)
and [installed benchmark tests](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/tests/benchmarks/test_installed_benchmarks.py).
Normal tests use owned fixtures without downloading external corpora.

For a development checkout with the contributor environment installed:

```bash
uv run --frozen --no-sync python -m pytest
```

This runs the configured coverage gate too. Follow
[contributor setup](contributing.md) to install the locked test dependencies.
Coverage measures exercised code paths; the
[evaluation guide](evaluation-guide.md) explains the separate evidence needed
for conclusions about prioritization effectiveness.

## Source, dependencies and secrets

Security evidence comes from complementary checks:

| Check | When it runs | What to inspect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Complete lock advisory audit](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/actions/workflows/security-audit.yml) | Dependency PRs, dependency pushes to `main`, weekly and manual dispatch | Queried package pins, `audit.json`, job conclusion and advisory lookup errors |
| [Dependency review](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/actions/workflows/dependency-review.yml) | Pull requests | Changed dependencies, license compliance and known vulnerabilities |
| [SonarCloud](https://sonarcloud.io/summary/overall?id=jacksonpradolima_coleman4hcs) | Connected repository analysis | Revision, date, source findings and the PR's analysis check |
| GitGuardian | Connected PR checks | Secret-detection result for the proposed commit |
| [Dependabot](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml) | Configured update schedule | Dependency update PRs and repository security alerts where access permits |

The lock audit includes optional runtime extras, development/documentation tools
and packages selected only on other operating systems. It queries advisories
without installing or executing project dependencies. Known vulnerabilities,
lookup failures and unsupported package sources fail the job. There is no blanket
ignore list. Reproduce it with the complete commands in
[dependency security maintenance](dependency-security.md#reproduce-the-audit).

A zero source-vulnerability count and a clean advisory audit answer different
questions. Read the revision, scope and collection time of each result; new
advisories can require another update. Follow the
[security policy](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
to report a vulnerability privately.

## Code, documentation and complexity gates

| Gate | Enforced scope | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ruff lint and formatting | Repository Python files under configured rules and exclusions | [Lint workflow](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/actions/workflows/pylint.yml) |
| NumPy parameter documentation | The public entry points listed by `make docstrings`; this is a bounded gate | Same lint workflow and [docstring guidance](contributing.md#write-useful-numpy-style-docstrings) |
| Xenon complexity | Maximum individual block C, module B, average A | [Structural workflow](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/actions/workflows/code-cost.yml) |
| Radon maintainability | Module maintainability index at least 20; cyclomatic complexity is also reported | Same structural workflow and [measurement guide](code-cost.md) |
| Strict site build | Zensical documentation generation | [Documentation workflow](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/actions/workflows/docs.yml) |
| Deterministic documentation bundle | Exact regeneration of `llms.txt` from reviewed Markdown | [Bundle workflow](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/actions/workflows/llms-txt.yml) |

The workflow file named `pylint.yml` runs **Ruff and the NumPy parameter gate**.
The contributor workflow also uses Pyright and ty, Interrogate for docstring
presence, package builds, outside-checkout examples and manual inspection of
rendered documentation.
The [maintainability review](maintainability.md) records the broader docstring
backlog; a passing bounded parameter gate does not certify every public signature.

Reproduce the automated code/documentation gates from the installed development
environment:

```bash
make lint
make format-check
make docstrings
make cost-structural
make docs
uv run --frozen --no-sync python scripts/generate_llms_txt.py
git diff --exit-code -- llms.txt
```

The [contributor validation commands](contributing.md#validate-a-change) cover the
additional local checks. PR title validation and labels support review routing;
the relevant technical checks qualify the proposed change before integration.

## Installed correctness and performance observations

The [decision observations workflow](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/actions/workflows/decision-benchmarks.yml)
builds a wheel with locked tooling, installs that wheel and runs outside the
checkout. Choose the `correctness` or `performance` profile on manual dispatch.
The Tuesday schedule executes only when the repository variable
`ENABLE_DECISION_PERFORMANCE` is `true`; it is not an unconditional PR gate.

The workflow retains reports, including available failed-attempt artifacts.
Inspect source revision, environment, resource bounds and the selected profile
before comparing measurements. The [benchmark guide](decision-benchmarks.md)
explains independent oracles, certificates and timing limits. Neither coverage
instrumentation timings nor one fast hosted run establish a performance advantage.

## Inspect a published distribution

The [release workflow](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/actions/workflows/release.yml)
uses locked release/build tools and publishes these assets in
[GitHub releases](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases):

| Asset | What it lets you inspect |
| --- | --- |
| Python wheel and source distribution | The installable package and its corresponding source archive |
| `*.sigstore.json` bundles | Sigstore signature and identity evidence for each distribution |
| `sbom.json` | CycloneDX inventory bound to the complete wheel's SHA-256 |

Read the dependency versions and hashes from **`uv.lock` at the corresponding
release tag**. For example, the installation tutorial's wheel uses
[the lock committed at `v4.19.1`](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.19.1/uv.lock).
Choose the tag matching your wheel or source distribution when inspecting a
different release. The lock's repository revision remains directly accessible
independently of the release asset list.

The [distribution inventory contract](dependency-security.md#release-distribution-inventory)
explains the SBOM's scope: it identifies the wheel's package metadata and digest;
unbundled dependencies are audited separately through the lock. Signing binds
distribution bytes to a signing identity. Inspect the expected repository,
workflow identity and release before trusting an artifact.

Start with the [published-wheel installation example](getting-started.md), which
pins the release and SHA-256. Then inspect the corresponding bundles and lock
when your adoption process requires them. Engineering checks, artifact identity
and [scientific evidence](evaluation-guide.md) are all inspectable parts of the
same decision.

### FILE: docs/releases/3.6.1.md

COLEMAN 3.6.1 strengthens the dependency and CI foundations behind reproducible test prioritization and selection. This maintenance release prepares a safer base for the planned 4.0 feature release.

## Security maintenance

- Refresh affected runtime and optional-tool dependencies, including documentation, notebook and release tooling. The complete all-platform lock audit reports **zero known vulnerabilities at the time of validation**, without an advisory ignore list.
- Add a recurring dependency audit that checks every registry package in the committed lock, including extras and packages for other operating systems, and retains machine-readable evidence in CI.
- Pin and verify the CI package-manager download, use locked build/release/audit tools, and disable third-party source builds in Linux CI.
- Protect documentation generation against symlink/path escapes and interrupted output publication.

## Upgrade

Requires Python 3.14 or later:

```sh
python -m pip install --upgrade "https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v3.6.1/coleman-3.6.1-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=ad22e85da1ac9ca42d3e70d10e9ff0d6fecca5f7841f01bcb144a15beffc0646"
```

For contributors, synchronize the updated lock and requested extras. Zensical and Marimo are updated to admit patched transitive dependencies. Native numerical dependency pins and decision/artifact semantics are preserved.

See the [dependency security guide](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v3.6.1/docs/dependency-security.md) for exact audit commands, scope and platform limitations. A clean advisory query means no known matching reports; it does not prove the absence of undisclosed vulnerabilities.

[Full changes: v3.6.0 → v3.6.1](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/compare/v3.6.0...v3.6.1)



### FILE: docs/releases/4.0.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.0 — Make every CI budget decision inspectable

CI budgets force a choice: which tests run now, which wait, and what evidence supports that decision? COLEMAN 4.0 makes those choices easier to execute, inspect and reproduce while keeping test-case prioritization and selection at the center of the project.

This release adds a shared, bounded application API and optional local MCP tools, backed by independent mathematical checks. They build on the recent 3.x foundations for versioned results, protected evaluation, finite coverage selection and scenario-based resource allocation.

## New in 4.0

- **One workflow across library, CLI and tools.** Discover approved configurations, submit bounded CI work, inspect status, cancel, retrieve results and export portable evidence. Native COLEMAN services perform the calculation and execution.
- **Independent checks before confident claims.** Small exact reference cases check feasibility, objective values, bounds and ties without calling the production solver. Separate opt-in performance observations record their environment, resource use and limitations.
- **Results with a contract.** Versioned handles and canonical artifacts preserve explicit units, meanings, source identity and provenance. Zero, missing evidence and unavailable results remain distinct.
- **Bounded execution with clear outcomes.** Queue, work, output, retention and worker resource limits have documented behavior. Cancellation, expiry and interrupted writes cannot masquerade as completed jobs. A feasible incumbent remains explicitly different from a proved optimum.
- **Optional tools, a service-free base.** The base wheel needs no MCP SDK, model, credentials or remote service. Configure the optional local stdio adapter once; supported clients can then use its tools directly.

## Try a bounded CI decision

With Python 3.14 or later on Linux or macOS, install this repository's GitHub release wheel in an activated virtual environment:

```bash
python -m pip install 'https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.0.0/coleman-4.0.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=80736c9eb2dc8e16bd1db3c6b30e48b0a3160803b2b35ff86a99fd598541a27c'
coleman application --request '{"schema_version":1,"request_id":"first-ci-decision","spec_id":"weighted-overlap-3","parameters":{"budget":3}}'
```

The packaged synthetic fixture selects **A+C within a 3-second modeled budget** and returns the complete typed result. It demonstrates a checkable decision; it is not a measurement of production CI savings. `native-ci-smoke-v1` exercises the actual TCPCI runner on two synthetic builds.

For MCP, install the same wheel with its optional extra and configure `coleman-mcp` in a local client:

```bash
python -m pip install 'coleman[mcp] @ https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.0.0/coleman-4.0.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=80736c9eb2dc8e16bd1db3c6b30e48b0a3160803b2b35ff86a99fd598541a27c'
```

Use this repository's assets: the bare PyPI name belongs to a different project. Release assets include signed distributions and an SBOM. The [application guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/application-api/) includes complete library examples, tool operations, errors and limits.

## Compatibility and evidence

Existing `coleman run`, sweeps, RunSpec workflows and native result/checkpoint interfaces remain available. Existing Parquet fields keep their meanings; old artifacts are not silently reinterpreted. New application bundles use schema version 1 and reject unknown future versions. Portable experiment provenance explicitly declares its redactions and source digest while leaving native result/specification bytes intact.

The release is validated with the full repository suite, native CI workflows, independent reference checks and noneditable installed-wheel tests outside the checkout. Optional MCP lifecycle tests use the real SDK over stdio, offline and without an LLM. Dependency and code-scanning findings are checked before publication; advisory results are time-dependent.

Worker memory and output sampling are local guards with possible transient overshoot, not a hostile-code sandbox. Hosted deployment and durable application-job recovery are outside this release. Export/import retains completed evidence; native checkpoint continuation remains a separate interface.

COLEMAN can report **insufficient evidence**, use a conservative fallback and preserve negative or inconclusive outcomes. Seeds support reproducibility; they do not replace independent observations. No universal algorithm superiority or production wall-clock savings are claimed.

## Explore the release

- [Application API and optional tools](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/application-api/)
- [Independent decision benchmarks](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/decision-benchmarks/)
- [Protected evaluation](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/protected-evaluation/)
- [Full changes since 3.6.1](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/compare/v3.6.1...v4.0.0)

## Release integrity correction

The initial SBOM contained only the distribution-directory metadata. It was
replaced with a verified inventory of the published wheel's distribution metadata,
including COLEMAN 4.0.0 and the wheel SHA-256. Dependencies are not bundled in the
wheel; their all-platform lock audit remains separate. Wheel, source archive,
signatures and the version tag were unchanged. Installation examples now pin the
published wheel digest.



### FILE: docs/releases/4.1.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.1 — Know what your CI budget actually buys

A faster first failure is useful. Missing the failures that matter is not a saving.
COLEMAN 4.1 adds a reproducible operational pilot that makes that distinction
inspectable, using the native TCPCI runner and independent execution accounting.

## From a ranking to accountable CI evidence

Run a small, MIT-licensed synthetic CI workflow with base order, shortest first,
native Random and native Greedy. Freeze its source identity, evaluation period,
execution budget and quality thresholds before execution. Inspect every build's
failing-test recall, first failure, occupied runner time, elapsed execution time
and separately measured prioritization overhead.

The fixture's three-second budget costs 0.03 modeled credits at its explicit price.
A candidate that spends less by missing failures fails the detection gate. Faster
feedback with unchanged recall stays a feedback improvement, without being sold
as improved detection. Synthetic replay remains **insufficient evidence for
production adoption**. Negative and inconclusive findings are first-class outputs.

## Small contracts, reusable evidence

- Versioned, immutable pilot manifests and typed execution events with explicit
  units, source identity, licenses, complete test universes and frozen thresholds.
- Independent serial/parallel event accounting that keeps runner-seconds separate
  from elapsed time, and excluded failures inside the recall denominator.
- Explicit unknown/timeout outcomes, censored no-detection times and genuine zero
  values; no silent reinterpretation of existing native metrics.
- Validated report snapshots, deterministic serialization, conflicting-retry
  detection and restart from completed candidate/build pairs using existing
  artifact infrastructure.
- An installed-package native workflow, a recorded bounded evidence report and a
  practical adoption checklist covering real overhead, protected comparisons,
  mandatory suites and conservative fallback.

Start with the [operational pilot guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/operational-pilot/)
and [runnable example](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/examples/operational-pilot/run.py).
Install the COLEMAN wheel attached to this GitHub release; the similarly named
PyPI package is a different project. Verify published asset digests and Sigstore
attestations using the [installation guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/setup/).

## Compatibility and limits

Python 3.14+ and existing native scheduling/results/checkpoints remain unchanged.
No new dependency is required. Pilot schema v1 rejects unknown versions; old native
artifacts keep their original readers and meanings, with no implicit migration.

This release validates a bounded synthetic replay, not production savings,
algorithm superiority, calibrated probabilities or commercial demand. Per-build
ranges are descriptive rather than confidence intervals. Real source admission,
diverse cross-project evidence and dependence-aware confirmatory comparisons
remain work in the [public roadmap](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/roadmap/).

[Full changes](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/compare/v4.0.1...v4.1.0)



### FILE: docs/releases/4.10.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.10 — Inspect controlled faults across Java codebases

Reproduce a small, explicit matrix of real upstream fixes before making a
benchmark claim. COLEMAN now collects CLI-13, CLI-51 and CODEC-65 with frozen
sources, common test fixtures and the existing bounded JUnit producer. Every
selected result remains inspectable, including errors and failures that persist
in both revisions.

## What you can do

- **Collect a declared matrix.** One typed plan describes three focal fixes across
  Apache Commons CLI and Codec. Pinned source views, original notices, JARs,
  runtime image, architecture, timezone and harness make the protocol explicit.
- **Keep negative evidence.** The initial qualification retained 714 role
  observations / 357 same-test pairs: 348 both-pass, four both-fail, four
  assertion-failed-to-passed and one inconclusive comparison. CLI-51's test error
  remains inconclusive under the existing classifier. Three Codec triggering
  tests do not become three faults.
- **Resume without inventing observations.** Existing role acknowledgments and
  raw packets retain interruption semantics. Typed indices distinguish observed
  pairs from entirely unobserved tests; incomplete collection has no completion
  marker. A verified completed matrix reopens offline without querying Docker.
- **Verify the evidence behind the index.** Offline validation checks actual
  source/context bytes, raw protocols, normalized observations and diagnostic
  references before accepting counts, identities or collection status.

The [complete matrix guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/java-fault-matrix/)
provides installation, explicit runtime preparation, source acquisition, typed
Python use, CLI collection/validation, recovery and the installed-package workflow.
Foreign sources, dependencies and captures stay in operator-owned external storage.

## Compatibility and limits

The new optional transport adds versioned matrix plans/indices while reusing the
existing generic controlled domain, source cache, JUnit producer and immutable
artifact writer. Old single-pair recipes, controlled artifacts, native results,
RunSpec identities and learning checkpoints retain their semantics and require
no migration. Unknown matrix schemas or producers reject; there is no implicit
reinterpretation of prior evidence.
The producer identity conservatively binds all COLEMAN packaged code/resources,
so even an unrelated packaged change selects a new generation. Incidental
bytecode, hidden files and interpreter caches do not affect that identity.

Codec's common fixture is explicitly partial. Before outcomes were observed,
three fixture files were excluded because of separately noticed third-party data,
non-UTF8 source bytes or dependencies on excluded classes. Remaining source bytes
and original LICENSE/NOTICE are preserved. This is direct-upstream reproduction,
not the complete original build or a full Defects4J reconstruction.
Upstream Base64/Hex/Digest fixtures also generate unseeded random inputs whose
bytes/seeds are not captured. Those tests remain included with an explicit
limitation; deterministic saved-artifact replay does not reconstruct fresh inputs.

The CLI fixes share project history. Multiple tests, seeds or trials do not
establish independent projects or unique faults. Collection clocks and harness
nanoseconds are not historical CI events, runner work or parallel wall-clock
savings. Shared-JVM test-order independence remains unverified. All outputs retain
`not_evaluated` and `insufficient_evidence`; diversified source admission, baseline
comparisons and confirmation in #261 remain open.

Validation covers versioned goldens, old recipes, strict units/missingness,
non-finite rejection, deterministic identities, duplicate accounting, negative
results, source/raw/index correspondence, interrupted publication, concurrency,
offline continuation and domain import boundaries. Installed-package checks use
actual Java source collection and a separate native CI exact-answer/checkpoint
workflow. This validates the evidence pipeline, not algorithm effectiveness.



### FILE: docs/releases/4.11.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.11.0 — Reproduce Python faults with their execution context

A fix can reproduce in one locale and disappear in another. COLEMAN's optional
Python source producer keeps those conditions and outcomes visible: unchanged
buggy/fixed PySnooper trees, one common upstream fixture, pinned wheels and a
declared CPython image. The existing controlled-observation domain carries the
results; native TCPCI experiments keep their established runner and checkpoints.

## What you can use

- Collect the frozen `pysnooper-1-ascii-v1` and `pysnooper-1-utf8-v1` profiles
  through `python -m coleman.transports.python` or the typed Python API.
- Inspect original bounded packets, actual interpreter/locale/distribution facts,
  explicit exception identities and separate case/producer nanosecond counters.
- Install pinned wheels in an atomically allocated private temporary directory
  inside bounded container tmpfs, with explicit storage policy and cleanup.
- Reopen completed evidence offline without Docker. A real process kill recovers
  an uncommitted role as interrupted, without silently repeating its observation.
- Validate recipe, context, raw protocol, normalized observations and immutable
  receipt together. Completion is written last and requires both protocols.

The [complete guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/python-source-capture/) covers installation, explicit
arm64 runtime preparation, collection, component terms, Python API validation and
recovery. Foreign source, wheels and raw data stay outside the repository and
package. No image is pulled or project setup script executed by the producer.

## What the qualification found

The installed package collected four role observations from one selected upstream
test in two predeclared contexts. Under ASCII, the buggy revision raises
`UnicodeEncodeError` and the fixed revision passes. Under C.UTF-8, both pass.
The existing strict classifier retains the exception-to-pass pair as
**inconclusive**; it is not relabeled as an assertion failure or expected pair.

These contexts share one curated fix and dependence group. They do not establish
independent-fault diversity, a full upstream suite, historical CI chronology,
policy benefit or scientific admission. Case timing is not native scheduling
cost. Results retain `constructed`, `not_evaluated` and `insufficient_evidence`.

## Architecture and compatibility

The optional transport reuses source views, materialization, bounded ZIP
selection, process collection, immutable artifact writing and controlled-result
conversion. A small shared implementation-identity helper preserves the Java
matrix's existing hash algorithm while serving Python capture too. The core
does not import CLI, MCP, Docker or the Python producer.

New records require explicit schema version 1. Missing/future/unknown versions
and incompatible units reject. Existing controlled/JUnit schemas and meanings
remain unchanged; no old data is silently migrated. Transport validation binds
the installed package/version: retain the original reviewed package to validate
its old producer artifacts, or collect a new generation under a new package.
Generic domain datasets remain readable through their existing API.

## Terms and limits

Subject, fixture, wheels, vendored components and additional notices have
independent pins and recorded terms. PythonToolbox is not blanket MIT; its
component map retains Apache, BSD, wxPython and inferred CPython-derived code
alongside MIT components. The unused headerless mapping-test attribution remains
explicitly inferred and available for later source-admission review.

The SDK remains Python 3.14+. The historical CPython 3.8.1 image is an optional
isolated benchmark condition; SDK dependency audits do not establish that image's
security. Initial presets are native linux/arm64 and an explicitly partial
fixture. Broader source coverage, admission, comparisons and the confirmatory
corpus report remain in #261's public subtasks, beginning next with #306.



### FILE: docs/releases/4.12.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.12.0 — Inspect constructed C faults with an independent oracle

Extend controlled CI research beyond Java and Python with a deliberately bounded
C source workflow. COLEMAN's optional producer compiles original NIST Juliet
functions in a pinned GCC container, evaluates a frozen arithmetic oracle and
retains the raw evidence. Reopen completed observations offline or recover a
stopped collector without inventing successful tests.

## What you can use

- `python -m coleman.transports.c` and the typed capture API for the frozen
  `juliet-uint32-add-v1` preset. Small individually pinned raw source views reuse
  the existing cache and public HTTPS adapter; no foreign code or binaries ship
  inside the SDK.
- Explicit original `bad` and `goodB2G` entry selection against identical source,
  support files and six declared uint32 boundary inputs. The independent safety
  oracle preserves five both-pass pairs and one assertion-failure/pass pair from
  the installed qualification.
- Versioned recipes, runtime/ABI facts, full bounded child streams, negative
  POSIX exit codes, integer nanosecond intervals, immutable ownership/receipts and
  honest incomplete recovery. Compiler diagnostics and executable digests remain
  inspectable alongside outcomes.
- Existing native TCPCI policies, Parquet results and checkpoints. Observer ns
  remain separate from independently declared modeled scheduling costs.

The [complete guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/c-seeded-source-capture/)
provides installation, explicit native arm64 runtime preparation, acquisition,
collection, replay, API validation, units, component terms and recovery behavior.

## Compatibility and artifacts

The generic controlled-result schema, native runner and learning checkpoints keep
their existing contracts. New C transport records require explicit supported v1;
missing, older and future schemas reject. Old generic artifacts stay readable
without implicit migration or reinterpreted values.

A multi-case Python replay validation correction now compares observations in the
generic domain's canonical logical-key order. Original raw/report bytes and case
ordering retain their meaning. Producer-specific replay binds the original full
installed package/version: retain the reviewed older wheel for its captures, and
use a fresh generation for a changed producer.

Physical container ownership for C, Python and JUnit now includes the resolved
output namespace. Separate output roots cannot collide or clean one another's
containers; logical observation identities are unchanged. JUnit start markers now
use explicit schema v2 and persist the original physical ownership, so relocation
still cleans the original container. Legacy v1 markers retain their original
cleanup rule; future versions reject. C/Python incomplete ownership stays at its
original output location. Retain the original producer package for recovery.

The first C qualification's noexec scratch failure remains incomplete with zero
observed cases. Explicit executable tmpfs and a recorded pre-observation amendment
made native binary execution possible while retaining read-only inputs, non-root,
network, capability and resource guards. No failed evidence was rewritten into a
successful run.

## Scope of the evidence

This is **one 2017 template-generated synthetic weakness / six correlated inputs**,
not six independent faults, real application history or a complete Juliet suite.
NIST's public-domain/CC0 declaration and the four selected mirror files' exact
correspondence to the official ZIP were checked before source qualification.
SIR component/data permission remains unresolved; its accessibility is not treated
as admission evidence.

These observations remain constructed, not evaluated for admission, and
insufficient for generalization. Historical chronology, independent cross-corpus
coverage, baseline comparisons and the confirmatory report remain open under
#261. All seven required registry diversity regimes remain uncovered. No policy
improvement, calibrated probability, prospective saving or broad security claim
follows from this small controlled reproduction.



### FILE: docs/releases/4.13.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.13 — Follow CI configurations from source data to evidence

Run a real, bounded LibSSH configuration history through COLEMAN's existing
**Whole Test Set and Variant Test Set** strategies. Keep the original pipeline
and job identities, inspect which configurations have usable observations, and
resume experiments across both policies and budgets without losing a budget's
results to another budget's checkpoint.

## A complete variant-aware data path

The [HCS guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/hcs-parquet-etl/) covers the reviewed original downloads,
Parquet export, library/CLI execution and offline replay. Its frozen first-sixteen
pipeline slice retains **885 source rows**, projects **856 test executions**,
and explicitly excludes **29 records from another attempt**. Thirteen known
job labels produce a **208-cell sparse matrix**: seven labels have parsed tests,
and six remain metadata-only evidence. Forty-four cells contain retained tests.
Metadata-only labels, including `static-analysis`, do not become fabricated test
configurations or executions. WTS and VTS retain their own policy state and
result denominators.

The original data remain outside Git under their published CC0 dedication.
Typed receipts bind source versions, exact byte counts, SHA-256, component terms,
conversion code and Parquet writer. Deterministic exports publish completion last;
offline validation regenerates the expected bytes from verified source. Identical
concurrent retries converge, while interruptions cannot certify a partial export.

## Budgets and identities you can inspect

Raw pipeline/job identity avoids the duplicated commit-level keys in the
publisher's prepared files. Original variant labels map reversibly to safe
aliases, preserving punctuation and case differences. Absent parsed cells remain
absent evidence rather than fabricated passing tests.

The new recipe explicitly aligns modeled costs with the existing bandit's
binary32 duration precision before deriving budgets. Original decimal seconds
and their lexemes remain unchanged in analytical Parquet. Union and per-variant
costs therefore have one declared interpretation; this is test-only serial
simulation, not measured runner occupancy or physical savings.

Native multi-budget checkpoint namespaces now include the exact mode/value.
Single-budget paths and payloads remain compatible. Ambiguous old unscoped
multi-budget state rejects before loading, including nested extension run IDs
and legacy names resembling the new namespace. Bounded progress metadata
distinguishes scoped state without unpickling checkpoints. No migration guesses
which budget produced old results. Existing native data, source recipes and
artifacts retain their meanings.

Native local Parquet recovery also closes the gap between flushing results and
committing a checkpoint: resume reconciles the uncommitted tail before replay,
including an interruption before the first checkpoint. Complete shards publish
atomically; failed writes cannot expose partial Parquet as completed results.
Committed rows and other executions/budgets remain intact. Same-run attempts must
be serialized; this process-interruption guarantee does not imply power-loss
durability or equivalent behavior for every optional sink.

Persistent ownership bindings also prevent a fresh or emptied checkpoint
directory from erasing another run's results at matching dataset/budget keys.
Ambiguous old tails reject; completed legacy coordinates gain ownership metadata
after their loaded checkpoint is verified, preserving their original rows and
payloads. Custom providers keep their existing checkpoint behavior.

## Evidence before claims

The slice exercises Random/UCB with RNFail, ratio budgets 0.5/1.0 and checkpoint
continuation. Native zero reward means nondetection, not an observed passing
label. Upstream binary nonpass labels may include statuses already collapsed
by extraction; they are not independently mapped unique faults.

Variants, repeated pipelines and seeds do not create independent projects or
faults. Outcome/feature availability, upstream omissions, setup, shared occupancy
and concurrency remain explicit evidence gaps. This release advances public
#261 source reproduction; scientific admission, protected comparisons and the
confirmatory cross-corpus report remain open.



### FILE: docs/releases/4.14.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.14 — Reproduce the CI decisions that are hardest to trust

What happens when failures disappear for a long interval, a test changes its
name, feedback arrives late, or a suite grows to 50,000 tests? COLEMAN 4.14 adds
an owned deterministic CI stress laboratory so those questions can be examined
with explicit truth, availability and accounting.

## A small design with inspectable coverage

Eleven declared factors cover scale, failure regimes, costs, churn, drift,
flakiness, feedback, budgets, context, variants and modeled worker counts.
Thirty-two deterministic cases cover every two-factor level interaction. Each
row has a private coverage witness: inclusion-minimal, without a claim of
globally optimal size. Seven named adverse sequences add temporal mechanisms.
Nothing automatically launches the full matrix or a Cartesian explosion.

## Reuse the platform you already have

Generate one case into canonical truth JSONL and native Parquet, verify its
bytes by regeneration, then use the existing API, real Random/UCB policies,
result sinks and checkpoints. Immutable complete-last exports support identical
concurrent retry. Native recovery handles interruption between result flush
and checkpoint commit, without inventing another experiment framework.

Point-in-time feedback pages keep the established history bounds. Current truth
stays separate from decision-visible context, unknown feedback stays null and
late corrections preserve earlier knowledge. Unsupported native feedback is
explicitly incompatible instead of receiving a misleading policy score.

## Evidence with limits you can see

The qualification includes a fresh installed wheel outside the checkout, an
actual 50,000-test native history, exact tiny references, independent interaction
enumeration, mutation/leakage guards and real process-interruption recovery.
Synthetic cases remain constructed, dependent evidence. Four-worker schedules
are modeled post-hoc replay, not observed parallel CI speedups. Seeds are not
independent projects, and no algorithm superiority or corpus admission is claimed.

Start with the [CI stress laboratory guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/ci-stress-laboratory/).
Existing historical, controlled-source and HCS workflows retain their contracts.
The next #261 gate integrates source admission and production-reality evidence;
the benchmark program remains open until its complete scientific criteria pass.
