# COLEMAN 4.15 — Know what your benchmark can support

A converted dataset is a starting point. Which units does it report? Which jobs
share a build? Was a label available when the decision was made? COLEMAN 4.15 adds
an auditable source-admission workflow that makes those questions explicit before
you compare CI prioritization policies.

The published wheel was qualified outside checkout: all 306 SDK resources match
the reviewed source and tag, and 61 source bindings reproduce the same versioned
report. Both distributions have verified GitHub workflow signatures. Actual Karaf
agents reach checkpoint step 8 and resume published 4.14 results without changing
their protected bytes.

## One inventory, inspectable evidence

Reuse the existing corpus registry, data cards and source completions. Audit
retained observations, execution groups, duplicates, outcome missingness and
duration distributions without changing the source's units or old results.
Generate deterministic versioned JSON and a human report with 35 production-reality
axes, including stages, variants, availability, retries and partial outcomes.
Every fact keeps its evidence status and limitation.

## Preserve the original producer

Controlled functional qualification verifies the original raw packets with an
explicit adapter bound to the original installed COLEMAN wheel. Package/version,
SDK bytes, source context and normalized observations must agree. Readable proof
metadata cannot replace that verification. The domain remains independent of CLI,
MCP and capture transports; offline auditing does not execute the subject tests.

## A result can say “insufficient evidence”

Negative and inconclusive functional observations remain valid. Constructed C
examples stay separate from real faults, and all 39 declared stress cases are
required before covering the broad synthetic mechanism regime. Neither category
supplies missing historical CI clocks or independent projects. Uncovered diversity
cells remain uncovered; no policy advantage or production saving is implied.

## Resume without rewriting evidence

Existing source receipts, native results and learning checkpoints retain their
contracts. New schema versions reject missing, coerced and unknown versions.
Immutable complete-last publication supports interruption, concurrent identical
attempts and idempotent retry. Reading a report is inspection; explicit validation
rechecks all source bindings before reuse.

Start with the [source-admission guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/corpus-admission/)
for complete CI examples, original-package bindings, units, compatibility and
recovery. The broader [#261 benchmark program](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/261)
still requires statistical references, comparable baselines, prospective
feasibility and a frozen confirmatory report.

# COLEMAN 4.16 — Compare projects without counting repetitions as evidence

Repeated seeds and thousands of builds can make a CI experiment look larger than
its independent evidence. COLEMAN now connects a frozen corpus of those repetitions
to its existing protected evaluator, preserving the raw observations and giving
each reviewed repository family one paired mean.

## What you can use

- Freeze one fold, native-work budget, complete build/seed membership, source
  clocks, project families and metric semantics with `RepetitionDesign`.
- Keep completed, failed, aborted and skipped attempts in a versioned
  `RepeatedCorpusReport`, bound to the original data and frozen candidates.
- Bind each immutable raw key to its declared candidate, build and seed so
  rearranging unchanged results cannot change their source attribution.
- Prepare equal-seed, then equal-build means. Zero and negative measurements
  remain valid; any missing input makes its whole unit mean unavailable.
- Publish immutable raw evidence, then use the existing protected access,
  paired effects, multiplicity corrections and conservative conclusions.

The [complete installed TCPCI example](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/corpus-evaluation/)
runs actual Random/UCB policies, independently checks native NAPFD/APFDc, retains
sixteen raw cells and groups its related histories into one constructed family
with **insufficient evidence**.
Its retry and native checkpoint continuation preserve the distinction between
reproducibility and fresh protected evidence.

## Metric clarity and compatibility

The guide documents the full-universe denominator of historical native verdict
NAPFD, its distinction from a selected execution horizon, APFDc's cost denominator
and binary32 duration boundaries in the native bandit. These are explicit
definitions and independent checks, not silent changes to old results.

The native runner, existing SDK modules, result formats, source receipts,
checkpoints and protected evaluator retain their behavior. New corpus contracts
require explicit schema version 1 and reject unknown versions; old native artifacts
remain native artifacts and are not automatically migrated into a scientific
comparison.

## Evidence and limits

Qualification includes versioned goldens, signed/zero/null/nonfinite boundaries,
full-grid and pseudoreplication guards, deterministic arithmetic metamorphisms,
normal null/known-effect simulations, real metric mutations, offline installed
execution, process interruption, concurrent publication and checkpoint recovery.

Declared family identities, normal differences and source admission still require
scientific justification. This release does not add clustered inference, a formal
equivalence test or a cross-fold significance engine. It does not claim new
historical source admission, prospective savings or algorithm superiority. The
remaining benchmark corpus work continues under [#261](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/261).

The actual signed wheel also passes installed qualification outside checkout:
all 308 SDK files match the release tag; the tagged Random/UCB example preserves
24 native files on retry and rejects swapped immutable build/seed records.
Original Karaf data yields sixteen independently checked native rows and resumes
checkpoint step 8. Actual published 4.15 results continue with 28 protected files
unchanged. Revalidating 61 original source bindings preserves the existing
admission report and its four uncovered historical/HCS regimes, using the original
4.13 producer for controlled captures. Both distribution signatures, all six
asset digests, SBOM and version-only automatic bump were checked.

# COLEMAN 4.17 — Compare CI baselines with evidence you can inspect

Run comparable test-prioritization experiments through COLEMAN's native runner,
keep the evidence behind every decision, and resume interrupted work without
rewriting its history. A frozen matrix makes candidate exclusions and incomplete
results visible alongside successful executions.

## What you can use

- Freeze the source snapshot, development fold, candidates, seeds, native-work
  budgets and cooperative resource limits in a versioned `BaselinePlan`.
- Compare twelve built-in candidates: seeded Random, original order, prior-cost
  and failure-history heuristics, UCB, Thompson sampling, discounted UCB, LinUCB,
  the native Random/UCB portfolio and a labeled unattainable reference.
- Reuse the existing RunSpec runner, native policies, RNFail feedback, Parquet
  sinks and per-build checkpoints through the base-package matrix API.
- Inspect complete rankings, selected prefixes, independently checked quality
  and work measurements, resource observations and every physical attempt.
- Verify completed artifacts by their actual bytes. Retain failed, aborted and
  incompatible cells with explicit reasons; an interrupted invocation cannot
  publish a falsely complete matrix.

The [complete installed CI example](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/comparable-baselines/)
executes all twelve internal candidates and records 36 build observations. Its
three builds belong to one constructed family and correctly return
**insufficient evidence**. The DANTE declaration remains incompatible until its
external runtime, outcome unit and common-universe inputs are qualified.

## Reproducible mathematics and compatibility

The matrix computes source work with a stable binary64 sum before native budget
selection. Parallel reductions cannot change that declared budget. Native
binary32 test costs and sequential binary64 prefixes remain explicit, with
independent rational checks of full-universe NAPFD, midpoint-cost APFDc, recall,
selected work and censored first-failure time.

Zero-failure quality ratios are unavailable, while legacy native Parquet retains
its existing fallback. Missing values remain distinct from observed zero.
Existing artifacts keep their meaning and readers; unknown contract versions
reject without implicit migration. Recorded runtimes get separate scopes.
Successful process pools now finish normal worker cleanup before closing;
interruption still terminates and joins workers.

## Evidence and limits

The complete reviewed source suite passed 3,816 tests with one platform skip and
95.14% combined coverage. Ubuntu CI passed 3,814 tests with three skips and 95.10%
coverage. Qualification includes versioned goldens, round trips, exact retries,
metric-corruption guards, real process interruption and checkpoint recovery,
future-availability rejection and fresh native matrices with different Polars
thread counts.

The actual signed wheel was installed outside checkout: all 322 SDK files match
the tag, the domain import guard excludes CLI/MCP, and the tagged native example
preserves all 258 artifacts on retry. All six asset digests, both distribution
signatures, SBOM and version-only automatic bump were checked.

Original Karaf data also executes ten eligible methods across eight builds,
retaining 80 independently checked raw observations. Its mathematical digest
matches both pre-release runs with different thread counts. Actual published
4.16 results resume at checkpoint 8 with all 28 protected files unchanged.

The published wheel also revalidates all 61 original source bindings and 63 data
cards with the original default Polars thread configuration. The admission digest
remains unchanged, with six original raw-producer proofs and four uncovered
historical/HCS regimes. Changing legacy stage-ETL thread settings can reject
fixed-profile artifact bytes in both 4.16 and 4.17; preserve the original producer
configuration rather than rewriting an existing receipt.

This is development evidence preparation. Source admission, independent project
families and protected confirmation remain separate gates. Costs are declared
additive test work, not verified whole-runner occupancy or prospective CI
savings. The release makes no policy-superiority or universal-generalization
claim. Public provider feasibility and the final corpus audit continue under
[#261](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/261).

# COLEMAN 4.18 — Trace the data. Bound the claim.

Bring original industrial test results into reproducible Parquet, and compare
bounded CI metrics without assuming normal differences. This release strengthens
the path from source records to an inspectable decision: explicit quantities,
preserved abnormal outcomes, conservative uncertainty and reliable recovery.

## Explore original industrial CI results

The [Westermo adapter](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/westermo-parquet-etl/)
fetches a pinned, licensed original release only when requested. It verifies the
archive and decoded file, then writes separate typed observation and session
tables. Offline retries preserve completed bytes; interruption cannot publish a
false completion receipt.

The installed-package qualification checks all **1,063,915 original rows** and
exports **1,064 observations from sixteen frozen sessions**. Pass, fail, invalid
and unmappable outcomes remain distinct. An independent reference checks every
selected field, and different Polars thread settings produce identical export
bytes. No third-party dataset is bundled in the package.

Session duration retains its documented seconds. Per-test duration retains its
original integer and an explicitly unverified unit. Shifted source dates remain
naive labels. These distinctions help you inspect the data without accidentally
claiming physical runner savings or verified historical availability.

## Compare bounded metrics with conservative uncertainty

Use the versioned `BoundedMeanProtocol` for paired means with known metric limits
and justified independent inference units. The
[complete native CI example](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/bounded-paired-evaluation/)
adds `--bounded` to the existing Random/UCB runner, repetition records, protected
access audit and checkpoints.

The method provides full-family Holm adjustment, simultaneous confidence bounds
and explicit practical equivalence. Rational calculations and outward rounding
keep numerical approximations conservative. Missing pairs remain incomplete
evidence; observed zero and valid signed effects retain their meaning.

## Keep existing artifacts and workflows

This is an additive release. Existing Student-t contracts, golden artifacts and
default native examples retain their behavior. No old result acquires inferred
bounds, new units or a different statistical interpretation. Unknown versions
reject; preserve recorded producer/runtime configurations when reading old
source exports. Older SDKs reject the new inference method explicitly.

Build or install the 4.18 package before using the new adapter and protocol. The
guides include complete installed-package commands, source attribution, recovery,
version compatibility and evidence limits. The base package remains independent
of optional CLI/MCP transports.

## Evidence that stays honest

The native example retains sixteen build/seed observations from **one related
family** and reports **insufficient evidence**. Repeated seeds do not create
independent projects. Protected reuse is recorded and cannot create a fresh
confirmatory claim.

The source conversion is analytical access, not historical benchmark admission.
Four mandatory historical/HCS diversity regimes still lack qualified evidence.
The final protected cross-corpus program and its source qualification continue
under [#313](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/313) and
[#261](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/261). This release makes
no algorithm-superiority or universal-generalization claim.



### FILE: docs/releases/4.2.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.2 — Reproduce what your CI decision knew

CI feedback arrives late. Verdicts get corrected. A useful experiment needs to
remember which information was available when it made a decision.

COLEMAN 4.2 brings that history into the native TCPCI workflow: reconstruct an
as-of view, freeze eligible training data, produce unitful decision signals and
inspect the artifacts after an interrupted run. It also introduces the first
versioned CI corpus foundation, with independently calculated correctness cases
and visible source-admission gaps.

## Keep late feedback in its proper place

- Preserve logical observations, source availability, first receipt and explicit
  revision lineage. Query r1 before a later correction without rewriting the past.
- Fit a simple historical quantity mean only on eligible training observations.
  Actual information cutoffs also bound target intervals. Inspect the explicit
  rounding rule, exact decimal estimates and input/model fingerprints.
- Keep zero, missing, stale/unavailable and not-applicable signals distinct.
  Use a declared freshness policy and retain the full base order when the native
  example lacks usable estimates.
- Revalidate serialized mean signals against frozen evidence. Conflicting logical
  retries fail, including signed-zero payload differences that numerical equality
  alone would miss.

Start with the [point-in-time CI guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/point-in-time-observations/)
and its [native example](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.2.0/examples/point-in-time/ci.py).
The installed base package runs both fresh-estimate and stale/fallback cases;
provider SDKs and source-specific rules remain outside the core.

## Make benchmark readiness inspectable

A typed source registry and data cards now separate registration from admission.
Two owned, MIT-licensed tiny CI sources check serial budget boundaries and parallel
accounting against hand-declared answers and independent exact references. An
excluded known failure stays in the recall denominator; seven runner-seconds on
three simultaneous workers remain four elapsed seconds.

The initial inventory pins ten existing Parquet artifacts by version, digest,
size and row count. All ten existing example registrations remain blocked pending
source-specific rights, units, availability and conversion evidence. All seven
minimum diversity regimes remain uncovered. These fixtures establish functional
correctness; the diversified benchmark program in #261 remains open.

Explore the [corpus foundation guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/benchmark-corpus/)
from an installed wheel with `python -m coleman.corpus list`.

## Recovery that preserves the evidence

Native extensions publish versioned signals and domain sidecars before checkpoint
advancement. Fault-injection tests resume after signal publication, after a domain
record commit and after checkpoint commit with stable logical identities.

This work also fixes a native Parquet data-loss defect: reopened or concurrent
writers could reuse a counter/PID/second filename. Fresh per-flush filenames now
preserve each completed batch. Existing partition schemas and readers remain
compatible; previously overwritten rows cannot be reconstructed automatically.

## Compatibility and evidence

Python 3.14+ and the existing runner, sinks, checkpoints and optional transport
boundaries remain supported. No new dependency is required. New schema-v1 readers
reject unknown versions; existing native artifacts retain their original meaning.
Mathematical model/signal identities are deterministic. The existing native
checkpoint store requires separate roots for concurrent logical invocations.

The release candidate passed **1,411 tests**, lint/format, both type checkers,
Pylint, strict documentation, structural cost and package/build checks. A
noneditable base wheel runs outside the checkout with MCP absent, including real
native recovery, deterministic mathematical artifacts and the complete docs
example. Local delegation review covered every changed file, including exclusions.

These are owned synthetic functional workflows, not independent prospective
observations, calibrated probabilities, policy-superiority evidence or production
savings. Resource replay, prospective shadow evaluation and broader admitted
corpus evidence continue in the [public roadmap](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/roadmap/).

Install the wheel attached to this GitHub release and verify its digests and
Sigstore attestations with the [installation guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/setup/).
The similarly named PyPI package is a different project.

[Full changes](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/compare/v4.1.0...v4.2.0)



### FILE: docs/releases/4.20.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.20 — Plan once. Keep your CI experiment.

Compare CI prioritization policies, explore a bounded parameter grid and return
to the same experiment after the conversation ends. COLEMAN now connects its
native TCPCI engine to durable application workflows, a CLI and optional MCP
tools. Your configurations, progress, checkpoints and evidence belong to a local
workspace rather than a chat session.

## From a question to a reproducible experiment

An MCP-capable client can turn “compare Random and UCB, try three exploration
coefficients and two seeds” into an inspectable plan. COLEMAN validates the
registered history, explicit scheduling budget, objective and resource caps
before starting work. The same typed plan runs directly through the library or
CLI, without a model or API key.

The initial allowlist supports Random and UCB with RNFail, grid/zip enumeration,
explicit seeds and native ratio, fixed-time or test-count budgets. Three UCB
coefficients plus the Random baseline make **four configurations**; two seeds
make **eight logical trials**. Trials, physical retry attempts and independent
scientific observations remain separate quantities.

## Disconnect, reconnect and continue

Persistent job identities survive MCP client disconnection. Reconnect to inspect
progress, cancel work or explicitly resume compatible native checkpoints.
Completed trials retain their immutable artifacts; interrupted trials continue
their actual learned state and random generator state. Changed inputs, runtimes
or missing acknowledged checkpoints reject continuation with an explicit reason.

Completed reports publish last. Bounded summaries keep large rankings out of
model context, while immutable artifact handles provide verified downloads of
complete plans, reports, source receipts and native Parquet. Private executable
checkpoints remain local. Portable imports are read-only evidence.

## Keep tuning and evidence separate

An eligible protected workflow stops after training and validation. It freezes
the selected candidate, same-budget Random baseline, every selected seed's
learning state and the complete evaluation protocol before audited test access.
Earlier descriptive replay and imported outcomes retain their source exposure
across reconnects, re-encoding and cleanup.

This first integration exercises protected continuation on explicitly constructed
histories. Its one-family example correctly reports **insufficient evidence**
and retains Random as a conservative fallback. Original-source replay remains
descriptive; successful tuning does not grant empirical source admission or
establish that a policy is superior.

## Start with a complete example

The [durable experiments guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/durable-experiments/)
includes installation, host registration, real SDK calls, CLI/library examples,
recovery, protected evaluation and artifact downloads. A public executable
example also checks library/MCP parity against the pinned Karaf source using an
approved pre-populated cache: **eight trials, 64 native build rows and 67 artifact
descriptors**, with the same mathematical digest through both interfaces.

This is an additive release. The original seven ephemeral MCP tools retain their
contracts; a trusted `--workspace` enables fourteen additional durable tools.
Existing native artifacts keep their meanings. The new workspace namespace
rejects unknown versions and provides no implicit checkpoint migration. Local
POSIX storage and trusted host registration are required; this is not a hosted
multi-user execution service.



### FILE: docs/releases/4.3.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.3 — Account for CI work. Audit every recommendation.

COLEMAN 4.3 makes CI test-prioritization experiments easier to audit. Account for
required runner work, replay cost-aware choices and evaluate frozen recommendations
alongside an unchanged CI suite—with explicit units, recoverable artifacts and
clear evidence requirements.

The product remains test-case prioritization and selection for continuous
integration. Reusable typed contracts make the audit easier to inspect and reuse.

## Know where the budget went

New exact resource ledgers distinguish estimates, reservations, actual occupied
runner milliseconds, unused release, dispatch and shared setup. Actual overruns
remain visible and stop new analytical reservations; they are never clipped into
feasibility. Unknown costs stay unknown, zero stays zero and negative comparison
savings remain valid findings.

Historical replay compares frozen policies under equal budgets through the native
COLEMAN runner. Reports separate modeled subset work from full-suite execution,
shared costs and unavailable latency. A shorter serial duration sum is not
presented as observed wall-clock saving.

## Observe recommendations without changing required tests

A prospective shadow protocol freezes candidate/model/features, source identity,
temporal windows, trial registry, thresholds and evidence requirements before
feedback. Typed source events preserve upstream chronology and first validated
application receipt. Operational health uses an explicit local monotonic clock;
research conclusions remain separate from connectivity.

Native extension and monitor hooks seal recommendations before outcome evaluation,
persist the original source contribution, and publish audit records before native
checkpoint advancement. Duplicates are idempotent. Conflicts, stale sources,
unsupported corrections and resource/quality breaches remain explicit. Atomic
journal frames recover committed events even if a checkpoint-reference write was
interrupted.

## Start with a small reproducible CI workflow

Use Python 3.14 and the verified release wheel attached below. Copy an example
into a separate workspace and run it twice to exercise checkpoint recovery:

```bash
python ci.py shadow-output
python ci.py shadow-output
```

Choose [`examples/prospective-shadow/ci.py`](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.3.0/examples/prospective-shadow/ci.py)
for the complete native shadow workflow, or
[`examples/resource-replay/ci.py`](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.3.0/examples/resource-replay/ci.py)
for historical resource replay. The base package is sufficient; neither example
needs MCP, hosted deployment, credentials or externally triggered CI jobs.

Read the complete [shadow guide](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.3.0/docs/prospective-shadow.md)
and [resource guide](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.3.0/docs/resource-replay.md)
for units, invariants, complete API examples and compatibility limits.

## Evidence you can inspect, limits you should keep

Recovery checks inject failures around actual source, artifact, result and native
checkpoint commits. Golden fixtures, unknown-version rejection, signed savings,
unit checks, chronology, bounded retention, concurrent publication, metamorphic
independent-arrival permutations and installed-package native examples accompany
the implementation. The integrated implementation passed 1,675 tests with the
repository's branch-coverage gate, plus typing, lint, structural, documentation,
package/install and security checks before publication.

The shipped shadow source is an owned synthetic functional fixture. Two builds on
one day do not satisfy its frozen seven-day requirement: the result is
**inconclusive**, with **zero collected prospective builds**. Repeated seeds and
job retries create no independent observations. The guide includes a forward-run
source/authorization checklist and an empty report template; it does not fabricate
a live study or establish production savings, causal value or algorithm superiority.

## Compatibility and what follows

This is an additive 4.x release. Existing native scheduling outputs, v3.2 artifacts,
domain records, runner/checkpoints and the application API retain their contracts.
New resource and shadow JSON artifacts require explicit schema version 1 and reject
unknown versions. Legacy rows cannot be relabeled as prospective evidence; there
is no implicit migration. Resource v1 does not support refunds, top-ups or
retrospective occupancy corrections.

The diverse-corpus program in [#261](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/261)
remains open. Source admission, secure materialization, broader regimes, baselines
and frozen cross-corpus evidence will follow in reviewed vertical slices. No broad
external-validity claim is made by this release.

Implemented in [#259](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/259) and
[#260](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/260).

[Full changes from 4.2](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/compare/v4.2.0...v4.3.0).



### FILE: docs/releases/4.4.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.4 — Know your CI data. Reproduce your inputs.

COLEMAN 4.4 helps you inspect the evidence behind a test-prioritization experiment
before trusting its results. Profile native CI inputs, pin permitted source
packages and verify the exact bytes used by a recoverable TCPCI workflow.

## Inspect the history before comparing policies

Bounded offline profiles describe all ten existing native Parquet artifacts with
explicit unit status, missingness, raw duration distributions and rows per execution
group. Logical builds,
variant execution groups, repeated identities and conflicting outcomes remain
separate. A deterministic inventory makes data-quality limits visible instead of
turning repeated rows into independent evidence.

Profiles preserve the source data cards and their admission decisions. A readable
file or a large row count does not establish a licensed, diverse evaluation corpus.

## Pin, verify and reuse permitted source bytes

Versioned source-package recipes freeze source/version/citation, SHA-256, byte
counts, specific reviewed terms, redistribution rules, member identities and
resource limits. Raw files and conservative ZIP packages use an external immutable
cache. Complete streams must pass checksum and size validation before publication;
interruption cannot create a falsely completed blob or receipt. Identical retries
and concurrent writers converge, while conflicts fail explicitly.

Offline validation rechecks the source, archive-to-member relation and cached
members. Metadata-only receipts preserve provenance without exporting recipe-only
data. CLI acquisition checks cache/export separation first; SDK workflows use an
explicit shared preflight, repeated at publication. Archive traversal,
links, aliases, duplicates, unsupported formats and inconsistent sizes are rejected.

The library accepts explicit binary readers. An optional public HTTPS adapter
supports a reviewed origin with verified TLS and no ambient credentials, proxies
or redirects. No metadata URI silently initiates a download.

## Run a small native CI example twice

Use Python 3.14 and the verified release wheel attached below. Copy
[`examples/corpus-materialization/ci.py`](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.4.0/examples/corpus-materialization/ci.py)
into a separate workspace and select a cache outside Git repositories and outside
the output tree:

```bash
python ci.py owned-ci-output /absolute/path/to/external-source-cache
python ci.py owned-ci-output /absolute/path/to/external-source-cache
```

The base package suffices. The example builds an owned deterministic ZIP, verifies
two CI correctness fixtures, executes the existing native runner, reopens its
learning checkpoints and checks persisted rankings against an independent tiny
reference. Repeating the command preserves exactly two native result rows.

Read the complete [source-package guide](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.4.0/docs/corpus-materialization.md)
for executable SDK/CLI examples, byte limits and failure behavior. The
[corpus guide](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.4.0/docs/benchmark-corpus.md)
covers profiles, the inventory and admission boundaries.

## Validation you can reproduce

The integrated implementation passed **1,947 tests** with **95.21% combined
statement/branch coverage**, plus lint, formatting, both type checkers, Pylint,
structural checks, strict documentation and package/install tests. Installed
base-wheel workflows run outside the checkout with real native CI/checkpoints.
Golden/version/compatibility checks, source corruption, interruption, concurrent
publication, compressed-stream boundaries and malformed archive/resource-limit
cases accompany the implementation. All confirmed PR findings were reproduced or
verified and corrected; local-only OpenCodeReview and manual exclusions covered
every changed file before integration.

## Compatibility and honest evidence

This additive 4.x release reuses existing runner, results, sinks, artifacts and
checkpoints. Existing native outputs and older domain artifacts keep their meaning.
New profile, package, receipt and cache contracts require explicit schema version 1;
unknown versions reject. No old row is silently migrated into a source-admission
or scientific success claim.

Limits apply per operation, with trusted private local filesystem parents. The
cache has no global quota/eviction policy; this release is not a hostile-filesystem
sandbox or a hard operating-system deadline for network acquisition. The built-in
archive recipe excludes tar, ZIP64 and additional compression methods. The optional
HTTPS adapter is limited to `raw.githubusercontent.com`; explicit library readers
remain independent of that transport.

All ten existing registrations remain blocked pending source-specific admission
evidence. All seven required diversity regimes remain uncovered. The owned
correctness fixtures share one dependence group; they establish functional
integrity and recovery, not independent projects or algorithm superiority.
Negative and inconclusive evidence remains valid.

The diversified benchmark program in
[#261](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/261) stays open. Next come
source-specific historical and controlled-fault adapters, synthetic stress cases,
comparable baselines, protected statistical protocols and frozen cross-corpus
reports. COLEMAN remains centered on CI test-case prioritization and selection.

Implemented in [#284](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/pull/284) and
[#285](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/pull/285).

### FILE: docs/releases/4.4.1.md

# COLEMAN 4.4.1 — Keep exact CI quantities bounded

COLEMAN now enforces the declared precision of exact quantities independently of
the active Decimal context. Compact, nonzero values beyond a contract's fractional
limit reject before serialization or expensive rational conversion. They are never
rounded into a free test, a zero budget or a zero probability.

## What changed

- Nonnegative quantities, signed scenario payoffs, exact output moments, scenario
  probabilities and application budget overrides receive context-independent
  fractional-precision validation. Each quantity retains its field's existing
  limit: twelve places for ordinary inputs and 48 for exact output moments.
- Versioned artifact `from_json` readers preserve numeric decimal literals until
  typed validation. Decimal fields retain their exact input; explicitly binary64
  fields continue to project to floats. The legacy domain-record decoder keeps
  its existing binary64 behavior.
- Independent benchmark references bound text length, Decimal coefficients and
  exponents, and preconstructed integer/fraction bit lengths before Fraction
  conversion. Bounded scientific notation remains supported. Valid negative
  reference values and genuine zero remain valid.

## Compatibility and limits

This is a validation correction, not a schema migration. Canonical v1 decimal
strings, valid signed values, logical identities and existing golden artifacts
retain their meaning. Out-of-contract values formerly admitted through Decimal
underflow now reject with a validation error; no clipping, rounding, fallback
value or silent artifact rewrite occurs. No runtime, CLI, MCP or data dependency
is added.
An already serialized zero does not retain evidence of whether an earlier input
underflowed. This patch does not reconstruct missing precision; reproductions
must use the original inputs when their encoding is uncertain.

Use the documented COLEMAN `from_json` artifact readers, and encode exact decimal
quantities as decimal strings when producing JSON. Generic Pydantic JSON helpers
are not a substitute for the duplicate-key and precision-preserving artifact
reader. Explicit binary64 measurements keep their declared floating-point
semantics.

New rational-reference safety ceilings are 4096 text characters, 512 coefficient
digits/absolute exponent for nonzero Decimal literals, and 4096 numerator or
denominator bits for parsed or preconstructed exact values. These are parsing/resource
bounds, not claims about the quality or independence of an experiment. Native CI
results and source admission remain separate contracts.
Previously readable references outside these safety ceilings now reject; there
is no automatic truncation or migration.

## Validation

Regression coverage includes compact exponent amplification, JSON numeric
underflow, altered Decimal contexts, valid precision boundaries/trailing zeros,
negative payoffs, null/zero budgets, nonfinite inputs and bounded exact fractions.
The noneditable installed-wheel check exercises the corrected quantity contracts
outside the checkout alongside the real native TCPCI and optional transport
workflows. All 1,971 tests pass, including the existing mathematical golden
fixtures, with 95.27% combined line/branch coverage. Lint, formatting, type checks,
Pylint, structural checks, strict documentation and package builds also pass.

The RTPTorrent research/adapter work in [#261](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/261)
continues separately. This patch adds no source admission or cross-corpus
performance claim.

[Full changes from 4.4.0](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/compare/v4.4.0...v4.4.1).



### FILE: docs/releases/4.5.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.5 — Keep the evidence behind your CI decisions

Adaptive test prioritization starts with knowing what the data actually records.
COLEMAN 4.5 adds offline readers for RTPTorrent class executions and LRTS Jenkins
reports, preserving the source identities, units and missing observations that
can disappear in a convenient flat table.

You can inspect and reproduce a source conversion, publish its immutable
provenance artifact and exercise the native TCPCI runner through checkpoint
continuation. Source integrity and scientific admission stay separate.

## Preserve executions before learning from them

The RTPTorrent reader retains project/job/class/position identity, including
repeated class executions. Reported seconds, assertion failures, errors and skips
keep distinct meanings. Filtered published baseline tables cannot silently replace
the full raw layout or remove successful jobs from the evidence.

The LRTS reader pairs pinned processed metadata with a separately pinned raw
Jenkins report. Project, PR, build, stage, suite, node and method observations
remain explicit. Repeated methods stay separate; unknown outcomes and unavailable
durations remain visible. Scheduled timestamps, execution duration and processed
duration sums never become invented completion clocks or parallel savings.

Both readers use existing source caches and deterministic artifacts. Actual
parsed bytes are checked against their frozen digests. Identical concurrent
publication converges; conflicting or interrupted writes cannot publish a falsely
completed source artifact. No third-party dataset rows are bundled.

## Reproduce a complete native CI slice

Install the verified Python 3.14+ wheel attached to this release. Copy either
complete owned example to `ci.py` in a separate workspace:

- [RTPTorrent format and isolated job](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.5.0/examples/rtptorrent/ci.py)
- [LRTS format and isolated suite](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.5.0/examples/lrts/ci.py)

Choose a cache outside Git and separate from the output tree, then run twice:

```bash
python ci.py owned-ci /absolute/path/to/external-source-cache
python ci.py owned-ci /absolute/path/to/external-source-cache
```

Each example authors a small fixture, uses the actual materializer and source
reader, runs Random/RNFail and checks persisted metrics against an independent
exact reference. Reopening the existing learning checkpoint preserves one native
result row and the same converted source artifact. These are constructed serial
checks, with no claim of observed CI history or independent project evidence.

The [RTPTorrent guide](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.5.0/docs/rtptorrent.md)
and [LRTS guide](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.5.0/docs/lrts.md)
include complete SDK workflows, source versions/digests, field meanings,
architecture diagrams, resource limits and explicit compatibility decisions.

## What the source assessment established

One pinned RTPTorrent HikariCP member converts to 46,995 class executions across
1,662 jobs, retaining 23,302 repeated-class executions. Its published baseline
slice has different coverage. The entire multi-gigabyte archive remains
unverified; member checks do not prove container integrity.

The complete original LRTS artifact and Karaf v3 archive passed size and provider
checksum verification, with computed SHA-256. Original artifact metadata matches
the pinned Git CSV byte for byte. One checked metadata/report pair preserves
228 suites and 931 methods, including four repeated labels. Specific data terms
were reviewed separately from the repository's code license.

These are bounded descriptive checks, not cross-corpus policy comparisons or
large-suite performance claims. Neither source is admitted to protected temporal
evaluation: outcome-availability clocks, logical mappings and complete expected
suite evidence remain unresolved. The registry's seven required diversity gaps
stay visible. A reader returning records is not evidence of generalization.

## Compatibility and limits

This additive 4.x release reuses the runner, results, sinks, checkpoints and
materialization contracts. Existing native and domain artifacts retain their
meaning. New source slices require schema v1; unknown versions and incompatible
layouts reject. There is no automatic migration from native results, filtered
baseline tables or arbitrary JUnit XML.

RTPTorrent preserves exact declared class seconds. LRTS preserves explicitly
declared binary64 source projections and rejects silent rounding, underflow,
negative/nonfinite durations and incompatible units. Zero and unavailable remain
different; valid negative values in unrelated signed contracts retain support.

Whole-archive fetching is not added. The existing materializer's ZIP64 policy and
hard 128-entry ceiling remain in force; real source containers exceed them.
Supported conversion starts from separately pinned permitted decoded members.
Inputs are bounded per operation, without an OS sandbox or global cache quota.
Recipe-only rows must remain local. The base package needs no MCP or transport
dependency for these readers.

## Validation and next steps

The reviewed implementation passed **2,107 tests** with **95.40% combined
statement/branch coverage**, including installed base-wheel workflows outside the
checkout. Lint, formatting, both type checkers, Pylint, docstring and structural
gates, strict documentation and package builds passed. Local-only OpenCodeReview
and manual exclusions covered every changed file. Confirmed review findings were
reproduced and fixed with regressions before integration; source/identity/unit,
serialization, corruption, interruption, concurrent publication and recovery
checks accompany the readers.

The diversified benchmark program in
[#261](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/261) remains open.
Controlled real-fault corpora, variant expansion, synthetic stress, comparable
baselines/statistics, modern-CI feasibility, frozen confirmation and cross-corpus
reports remain sequential work. Negative and inconclusive results remain valid.

Implemented in [#290](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/pull/290) and
[#291](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/pull/291).

[Full changes from 4.4.1](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/compare/v4.4.1...v4.5.0).



### FILE: docs/releases/4.6.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.6 — Reproducible fault evidence for CI

A CI prioritization decision needs evidence you can inspect and reproduce.
COLEMAN 4.6 connects pinned buggy/fixed source revisions to versioned test
observations, retained diagnostics and immutable artifacts. You can rerun a
controlled fault recipe, recover interrupted collection and keep unexpected
outcomes visible before considering a source for a benchmark.

This release brings together the reviewed controlled-observation foundation and
an optional Java/JUnit3 producer. The existing TCPCI runner continues to execute
learning experiments, write results and resume its own checkpoints.

## From a source revision to an auditable result

The new controlled records retain the project, curated fault label, common test
fixture, source revisions, runtime, component receipts and actual producer bytes.
Each observation has a stable logical identity, explicit outcome and integer
monotonic nanoseconds. Zero, unavailable and not applicable keep distinct meanings.
Parent-process timing and per-test harness timing have separate semantics.
Neither becomes an invented CI completion time or removable scheduling cost.

Same-test comparisons preserve expected, both-pass, both-fail, reversed and
inconclusive outcomes. Missing observations stay missing. Diagnostic digests bind
to separately verified report members; schemas, source bytes and duplicate
identities are validated before immutable publication.

The bundled Apache Commons CLI-13 recipe pins both public source revisions, a
common fixed-tree fixture, component dependencies, the COLEMAN-authored harness
and a platform-specific Temurin image. Individually pinned files form bounded,
deterministic source views. Foreign source code and datasets are not bundled in
the package or mirrored into the repository.

A real installed-wheel execution collected **190 observations across 95 tests per
revision**: 92 pairs passed in both revisions, two failed in both and one failed
then passed. The two additional failures remain in the evidence. These are
functional reproduction results for this declared runtime and fixture, not an
independent-fault count or a policy-performance comparison.

## Try the pinned recipe

Use Python 3.14+, a local arm64 Docker engine and an external workspace. Install
the wheel attached to this release and explicitly prepare its public image:

```bash
python -m pip install https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.6.0/coleman-4.6.0-py3-none-any.whl
docker pull --platform linux/arm64 eclipse-temurin@sha256:e4b3ff0f1a427efb2deb02b092ff8316d58573480260720d767d6ecdd69999d8
python -m coleman.transports.junit \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-junit-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-junit-results \
  --trial source-001 --fetch
python -m coleman.transports.junit \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-junit-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-junit-results \
  --trial source-001
```

The first call explicitly permits reviewed, size/digest-pinned public GitHub and
Maven downloads. The second reopens the same committed observations without
executing those roles again. Acquisition is offline by default; subject execution
has no network and the producer never pulls an image implicitly.

The JSON summary provides artifact paths, role statuses, pair counts and explicit
admission/generalization fields. Exit 0 means the collection protocols completed;
assertion failures remain outcomes. Incomplete collection retains its evidence
and returns 2. Exceptions remain nonzero failures.

The [complete Java guide](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.6.0/docs/junit-source-capture.md)
explains source/component terms, resource limits and the runtime profile. The
[controlled-observation guide](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.6.0/docs/controlled-faults.md)
provides an offline SDK example and a complete owned native TCPCI workflow with
independently checked metrics and learning-checkpoint continuation.

## Recover without inventing success

An immutable start marker precedes each role. Completed packets replay; a started
but uncommitted role recovers as interrupted, with unavailable streams/counters
and no fabricated cases. Failed container cleanup leaves that start recoverable.
Raw output roots, concrete cache/session paths and source staging destinations
are checked outside Git worktrees with one shared storage guard. Linked-worktree
markers, symlink aliases and staged Git-marker names are covered. A POSIX lock prevents duplicate
producers for the same context/trial/output tree.
Use a new trial ID for a new execution; repeated trials retain their dependence
group and do not become independent projects or faults.

The collector bounds process time and combined output bytes. Containers are
non-root and read-only, with explicit input mounts and CPU, memory, PID and
temporary-storage limits. These guards support trusted-source reproduction.

Resume validates raw protocol bytes, exit status, discovered test IDs and the
completion trailer. Single-case terminal counters cannot exceed the one declared
run. Unavailable streams cannot retain observed process facts;
observed streams require them. Timeout/prefix claims must agree with their bounds.
Contradictory negative labels cannot silently erase complete observations.
Diagnostic envelopes use a separate bounded profile, preserving complete raw
packets for the supported 4-MiB output limit. Oversized normalized-report
configurations reject before source execution; source-view limits stay unchanged.
Coherent producer attestations still do not authenticate execution truth.

## Compatibility and validation

This is an additive **4.x** release. Existing native results, artifacts, sinks,
checkpoints and source readers retain their meaning. New contracts require schema
v1 and reject missing, unknown and future versions. No automatic migration or
reinterpretation of old results occurs. Harness changes require a reviewed recipe
update. The domain remains independent of CLI, Docker and MCP imports.

The reviewed implementation passed **2,270 tests** and the **95% combined
statement/branch coverage gate**, including a real paired source reproduction from a
wheel installed outside the checkout. Versioned golden/round-trip fixtures,
compatibility, units/missingness, nonfinite values, deterministic identities,
concurrent publication, interrupted writes, genuine child-process guards and
checkpoint recovery are covered. All lint/format/type/Pylint/docstring/structural,
strict documentation and package checks passed. Local-only OpenCodeReview and
manual review covered every changed file; confirmed findings were reproduced and
fixed with regressions before integration.

## What remains open

The records retain `admission=not_evaluated` and
`generalization=insufficient_evidence`. The shared JVM uses lexical test order;
order independence is not established. Collection clocks are not historical CI.
The recipe is one direct upstream pair, not a full Defects4J reconstruction.
Component terms remain separate from COLEMAN's MIT license; recipe-only content
stays in external caches.

The diversified benchmark program in
[#261](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/261) remains open. Source
admission, independent projects/faults, all seven diversity regimes, comparable
baselines, protected chronological evidence and cross-corpus reports remain
sequential work. Negative and inconclusive results remain valid evidence.

Implemented in [#294](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/pull/294) and
[#295](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/pull/295).

[Full changes from 4.5.0](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/compare/v4.5.0...v4.6.0).



### FILE: docs/releases/4.7.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.7 — From LRTS source data to runnable Parquet

Download a public CI benchmark, inspect its converted Parquet files and run a
declared simulation through COLEMAN's existing TCPCI runner. This release closes
that path for a pinned, bounded Karaf slice of LRTS.

The recipe downloads the verified raw-report archive and metadata, selects eight
source builds and writes three useful tables: original method observations,
source-build metadata and native-compatible input. A completion manifest binds
source revisions, data terms, implementation and file digests. Interrupted work
can reuse verified inputs; repeating a completed run resumes its native checkpoint.

## Try the complete workflow

Use Python 3.14+ and an installed wheel built from this release. Cache and data
directories must be outside Git; Docker and an optional MCP SDK are unnecessary.

```bash
python -m coleman.transports.lrts_etl \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-lrts-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-lrts-data \
  --fetch --run

python -m coleman.transports.lrts_etl \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-lrts-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-lrts-data \
  --run
```

The first command explicitly permits pinned public GitHub/Zenodo downloads.
The second works offline from the verified cache. The JSON summary gives the
actual Parquet, completion and native-result paths.

The selected real reports contain **6,876 method executions**. All original rows
remain in `observations.parquet`; **6,567** complete reported outcomes/durations
enter native input, including **29 reported failed executions**. The **309 not-run
methods** remain visible with explicit exclusions. Unknown outcomes and unavailable
durations have independent exclusion reasons; zero remains observed zero.
Metadata accounting retains the eight selected rows and 57,429 outside the slice.

Default Random and UCB (`c=1`) runs use RNFail, seed 42 and a 50% ratio budget.
Eight rounds and two policies produce 16 native result rows. Native checkpoints,
results, RunSpec and artifact manifests retain their existing behavior. The ETL
receipt is linked in the native manifest; no second experiment runner is added.

## Reproducible inputs and honest assumptions

The [complete guide](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.7.0/docs/lrts-parquet-etl.md)
documents the exact eight source builds, component/data terms, units, table schemas,
exclusions and installed-package reproduction. Third-party rows and archives
stay in external storage. COLEMAN distributes recipes and owned tiny fixtures.

Source and report digests are verified before conversion. A separate bounded ZIP
selection recipe supports the real archive directory while retaining the old
complete-package v1 limits and ZIP64 rejection. Unsafe paths, aliased entries,
unsupported types, contradictory metadata and changed bytes fail closed. New
ETL/selection schemas require version 1; unknown/future versions reject. Existing
Parquet/results/checkpoints keep their meaning without implicit migration.

Analytical records preserve raw identities, source timestamps and unavailable
values. The native projection declares **post-hoc serial simulation**: scheduled
labels order rounds, reported method seconds are added as modeled costs, feedback
uses native budget-censored RNFail rewards (zero nondetection reward also for
unscheduled cases), and matching labels/occurrences are an assumed correspondence.
Zero reward does not assert a passing source verdict. Legacy full-label receipts
remain readable but reject new exports/execution; opt-in correction creates new
identities without modifying old artifacts. These assumptions do not become observed CI chronology,
runner occupancy, parallel latency or verified stable test identities.

Admission remains `blocked_source_evidence`, and generalization remains
`insufficient_evidence`. This release makes a real bounded source usable for
inspection and that declared simulation. It does not establish protected temporal
validity, policy superiority, independent faults or prospective savings.

## Validation and next steps

Owned golden fixtures, old-artifact reads, round trips, corruption checks,
deterministic identities/bytes, concurrent publication, interrupted export,
missingness/nonfinite cases, source-order guards and native checkpoint recovery
are exercised. An installed wheel outside the checkout converts the actual source
slice and executes/reopens actual native runs. Acquisition is separately checked
against the public source with an initially empty cache.

The diversified benchmark program in
[#261](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/261) remains open. Larger
slices, other sources/languages, HCS and synthetic stress, complete baseline
matrices and protected confirmation/reporting continue as sequential work. The
seven required diversity regimes remain uncovered; the slice is useful data and
functional execution evidence, not completed corpus admission.
