# COLEMAN 4.8 — Real CI history, reproducible test prioritization runs

Turn a pinned RTPTorrent archive into inspectable Parquet and checkpointed TCPCI experiments with
the runner you already use. This release connects verified source acquisition, complete analytical
history and a bounded native replay in one documented workflow.

## What you can do

- **Prepare real RTPTorrent CI observations.** The HikariCP preset preserves 46,995 class executions
  across 1,662 source jobs in analytical Parquet, with exact reported seconds, original execution
  identities and explicit missing values.
- **Run and resume Random/UCB experiments.** An explicit eight-job preset projects 18 compatible
  executions into the existing native API. Two policies produce 16 result rows across eight modeled
  rounds; retrying resumes committed checkpoints without duplicating results.
- **Inspect every exclusion.** The other 46,977 executions remain analytical records. Source,
  projection and duplicate counts must reconcile, so a smaller native slice never erases the
  original history.
- **Verify what you downloaded.** A separate bounded ZIP64 profile verifies the full approximately 5
  GB source, selected-member membership and decoded hashes. Resumable operator downloads and an
  external cache keep large data out of the repository and wheel.
- **Reproduce artifacts deliberately.** Versioned recipes bind source terms, hashes, assumptions,
  actual producer code and Parquet writer version. Immutable tables precede the completion receipt;
  interruption, concurrent retries and unknown versions have explicit behavior.

The release also corrects Linux memory accounting for application workers: a large parent process
can no longer make a small worker appear over its RSS limit. The guard measures the worker
executable's kernel high-water mark, retains existing admission limits and fails closed when
measurement is unavailable. Real Linux regressions cover both native/coverage execution and actual
low-cap refusal.

## Try it

Use Python **3.14+** and install the verified 4.8 wheel from the release assets. After downloading
the pinned archive to an external workspace:

```bash
python -m coleman.transports.rtptorrent_etl \
  --archive /external/rtp-torrent-v11.zip \
  --cache /external/coleman-cache --output /external/coleman-data --run

# Once cached, verify and resume offline.
python -m coleman.transports.rtptorrent_etl \
  --cache /external/coleman-cache --output /external/coleman-data --run
```

See the [RTPTorrent Parquet and replay
guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/rtptorrent-parquet-etl/) for installation, source
download, offline replay and the typed API. A small repository-authored example exercises the same
complete path without downloading foreign data. The existing [LRTS
workflow](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/lrts-parquet-etl/) remains available.

## Evidence you can inspect

The installed-package workflow runs outside checkout against the real source cache, validates
Parquet, executes the actual native runner twice and checks committed checkpoint recovery. Local
regression coverage includes serialization/goldens, unknown versions, incompatible units,
zero/null/unknown/not-run semantics, source-order metamorphism, duplicate conservation, concurrent
exports, interrupted writes, forged provenance and import boundaries. Complete local review and CI
evidence are linked from the implementation PRs.

## Scope and compatibility

This delivery supports **post-hoc source-job serial simulation**. Numeric job labels are not
verified chronology; reported class seconds are not parallel CI wall-clock savings; repeated seeds
are not independent observations. Protected temporal admission remains blocked by missing source
clocks and logical build/job mapping. The broader diversified corpus and confirmatory comparisons in
#261 remain ongoing.

Existing ZIP recipes, raw readers, native Parquet, LRTS exports and checkpoints retain their
semantics. No historical artifact is silently migrated. New receipts require explicit
schema/producer/writer compatibility. Source data terms remain separate from enclosed subject-code
rights, and the workflow does not execute archived subject repositories.

Implementation and review: [ZIP64 source integrity
(#314)](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/pull/314), [real Parquet and native replay
(#315)](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/pull/315). The complete local suite passed
**2,542 tests with 95.31% coverage**, with the Linux-only regression separately exercised in Linux
and an installed wheel. [Full
changes](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/compare/v4.7.0...v4.8.0).



### FILE: docs/releases/4.9.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.9 — Larger CI histories, explicit test stages

Move beyond a single real-data demonstration while keeping every stage and
observation inspectable. COLEMAN now prepares four-build ActiveMQ and Log4j
histories as analytical Parquet and runs their declared native stage views through
the same TCPCI API, policies and resumable checkpoints.

## What you can do

- **Use larger real method histories.** Frozen source recipes preserve 18,901
  ActiveMQ observations and 30,066 Log4j observations with original PR/build,
  suite, class, method and execution identities.
- **Keep environments distinct.** Separate Log4j Ubuntu and Windows native views
  bind exact raw context arrays and build-local node IDs to processed stages.
  All stages remain in analytical files; selecting one view never erases the rest.
- **Audit every native exclusion.** Outside-stage, not-run, unknown-outcome and
  unavailable-duration records retain their original evidence and reconcile with
  the complete source. Reported zero seconds remains distinct from missing data.
- **Run, inspect and resume.** Each four-build view runs Random and UCB with the
  existing native RNFail feedback and checkpoint protocol. Immutable source and
  completion receipts make identical retries reproducible.
- **Recognize missing evidence.** Typed temporal blockers distinguish resolved
  within-report stage correspondence from unavailable executor/outcome/feature
  clocks, expected test universe, verified continuity and concurrency topology.

Use the [complete stage-view guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/lrts-stage-views/)
for exact source downloads, bounded local acquisition, Parquet schemas, typed API,
native runs, recovery and attribution. Large third-party archives stay outside
Git and the wheel. Recipes independently verify whole-archive, nested-member and
decoded-report bytes; no archived subject repository is executed.

## Compatibility and evidence

The new versioned recipe family has its own producer and artifact namespace.
Existing single-stage LRTS recipes/receipts, raw readers, RTPTorrent workflows,
RunSpec identities and checkpoints retain their semantics. Old artifacts are not
silently migrated. Unknown schemas, producers or Parquet writers reject with an
explicit compatibility requirement.

Stage views are **post-hoc serial simulations**. Reported scheduled labels are
not verified outcome chronology; method-duration sums are not physical parallel
CI savings. Both Log4j views share the same source project/build groups and do not
become independent projects or faults. The profiles retain
`blocked_source_evidence` and `insufficient_evidence`; the diversified corpus,
protected comparisons and confirmatory report in #261 remain ongoing.

Validation covers the installed base wheel outside checkout, actual real-source
Parquet/native/checkpoint workflows, versioned goldens and old artifacts,
round-trips, units/missingness, non-finite rejection, collision guards, forged
provenance, deterministic identities, duplicate conservation, interrupted writes,
concurrent retries and domain/transport import boundaries. This is evidence of a
reproducible pipeline, not an algorithm effectiveness or production-savings claim.



### FILE: docs/releases.md

# Release preparation

COLEMAN keeps public product documentation centered on CI test prioritization,
selection and evidence. Generic decision contracts support that product; a release
should explain the value to CI users before listing internal implementation work.

## Versioning and integration

The published [COLEMAN 4.9](releases/4.9.0.md) release adds [larger LRTS histories
with explicit stage views](lrts-stage-views.md): frozen ActiveMQ and Log4j source
profiles, analytical/native Parquet and actual checkpointed replay. Source
groups and temporal blockers remain explicit. The signed wheel, source archive,
SBOM and synchronized lock are available in [the release
assets](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/tag/v4.9.0).

The published [COLEMAN 4.8](releases/4.8.0.md) release combines bounded ZIP64
source integrity and the [complete RTPTorrent Parquet/replay workflow](rtptorrent-parquet-etl.md),
including the Linux worker memory-accounting correction. The verified wheel,
source archive, Sigstore bundles, SBOM and synchronized lock are available in
[the release assets](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/tag/v4.8.0).

[COLEMAN 4.7](releases/4.7.0.md) introduced the real
[LRTS download-to-Parquet workflow](lrts-parquet-etl.md), including analytical
tables, explicit native simulation input and actual runner/checkpoint recovery.
Its source-admission and confirmatory-evidence limits remain explicit.

[COLEMAN 4.6](releases/4.6.0.md) adds versioned controlled fault observations,
a pinned offline JUnit3 source recipe and recoverable raw evidence. Existing
native TCPCI experiments and learning checkpoints keep their contracts. Controlled
source reproduction remains separate from benchmark admission.

[COLEMAN 4.5](releases/4.5.0.md) added bounded RTPTorrent and LRTS source readers,
explicit units/provenance and installed native CI/checkpoint workflows. It retains
the exact numeric safeguards from 4.4.1, corpus profiles and secure source cache.
Both external sources remain blocked for protected temporal evaluation.
The public corpus program continues in subsequent compatible **4.x** feature releases; compatible corrections use patch
versions. Follow the [public roadmap](roadmap.md) in dependency order and keep each
PR runnable and independently reviewed. Publishing a slice does not complete the
remaining corpus-admission or confirmatory-evidence gates.

A release branch can collect related reviewed PRs when a capability needs several
vertical slices before publication. Keep it synchronized with security fixes from
`main`; available security corrections must not wait for a feature release.
The publication workflow runs on `main`. A compatible `feat:` merge requests the
next minor version; `fix:` requests a patch. Reserve `feat!:` or an explicit
breaking-change declaration for an actual incompatible public contract.

Before integrating a release branch, review its entire diff and pass the full
quality/security/install/native-CI gates. Do not manually edit only the package
version while leaving tags or the lock inconsistent.
The automated workflow updates the package version, synchronizes `uv.lock`, builds
the distributions, and includes the lock in the version commit before tagging.
A second lock check after tagging must find no changes. This keeps the tag, source
archive and wheel metadata consistent.

## Reviewed release descriptions

Before the final release PR, commit `docs/releases/<version>.md` with an en-US release
description. The publication workflow uses `docs/releases/<version>.md` when
present; otherwise it preserves the generated description. These notes are part
of the reviewed diff and must describe only completed, validated public features.

Write for a new CI user:

- the concrete problem the release solves and useful workflows;
- the delivered capabilities and a runnable starting example;
- compatibility, Python requirements and any migration steps;
- correctness/security evidence and its limits;
- known limitations and links to the full changes.

Avoid unsupported algorithm superiority, universal generalization or wall-clock
savings claims. Separate modeled objectives, measured CI outcomes, mathematical
correctness and protected empirical evidence. Negative and inconclusive outcomes
remain results.

After automatic publication, check the rendered GitHub description, assets,
checksums, attestations, SBOM, package version and source/lock consistency. If the
automatic description needs an editorial correction, update it from a reviewed
notes file rather than replacing it with an unverified marketing claim.



### FILE: docs/research.md

# Research behind the workflows

Use this reading path to connect a capability to the question it was designed to
study. A paper's findings apply to its own subjects, assumptions and experiment;
they do not validate every later policy, adapter or dataset in this repository.

## Adaptive prioritization

**Prado Lima and Vergilio. _A Multi-Armed Bandit Approach for Test Case
Prioritization in Continuous Integration Environments._ IEEE Transactions on
Software Engineering 48(2), 453–465, 2022.**
[DOI: 10.1109/TSE.2020.2992428](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.2020.2992428).

The original COLEMAN article motivates learning from test feedback as suites
change across CI cycles. Read it alongside [the prioritization loop](concepts.md),
[policy choices](policies.md) and [native experiments](experiments.md).
The DOI contains 2020, reflecting its publication history; the volume/issue
citation is 2022. [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/CITATION.cff)
records the preferred citation.

**Li, Chu, Langford and Schapire. _A Contextual-Bandit Approach to Personalized
News Article Recommendation._ WWW, 2010.**
[Author preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.0146).

This introduces LinUCB in a recommendation setting. It provides algorithmic
background for a contextual family, rather than evidence about this CI runner.
Continue with [contextual feature availability](policies.md#contextual-policies)
and [point-in-time observations](point-in-time-observations.md).

**Auer, Cesa-Bianchi and Fischer. _Finite-time Analysis of the Multiarmed Bandit
Problem._ Machine Learning 47, 235–256, 2002.**
[Publisher and DOI](https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1013689704352).

Read this for classical confidence-based exploration under its stated reward
assumptions. The [policy guide](policies.md) distinguishes that theoretical setting
from a particular CI history, reward transformation or implementation.

## Structured policies and subset feedback

**Chen, Wang and Yuan. _Combinatorial Multi-Armed Bandit: General Framework and
Applications._ ICML, PMLR 28(1), 151–159, 2013.**
[Original proceedings and paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v28/chen13a.html).

This provides a foundation for thinking about subset actions, component feedback
and reward structure. Read it alongside [the policy families](policies.md) and
[finite coverage selection](finite-coverage.md). A native full-ranking adaptation
or a finite solver is not automatically the paper's online feedback/oracle model;
check the actual assumptions before applying a guarantee.

## Information availability and data leakage

**Kaufman, Rosset, Perlich and Stitelman. _Leakage in data mining._
ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data 6(4), 2012.**
[Publisher and DOI](https://doi.org/10.1145/2382577.2382579).

This explains how information unavailable at prediction time can compromise an
experiment. In CI, an eventual verdict, corrected duration or late report can be
present in a later export without being available to an earlier policy.
[Late results and corrections](decisions/001-point-in-time-observations.md)
explains that problem through an execution timeline.
[Point-in-time observations](point-in-time-observations.md) provides the complete
API example, while [protected evaluation](protected-evaluation.md) adds the temporal
and grouped comparison protocol.

## Configurations and variants

**Prado Lima, Mendonça, Vergilio and Assunção. _Learning-based prioritization of
test cases in continuous integration of highly-configurable software._ SPLC, 2020.**
[DOI: 10.1145/3382025.3414967](https://doi.org/10.1145/3382025.3414967).

**The same authors. _Cost-effective learning-based strategies for test case
prioritization in continuous integration of highly-configurable software._
Empirical Software Engineering 27, article 133, 2022.**
[Publisher and DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10664-021-10093-3).

These studies motivate prioritization across changing variants. Use
[WTS and VTS explained](highly-configurable.md) before following the
[LibSSH workflow](hcs-parquet-etl.md). The current
[original CTest evidence](hcs-trace-evidence.md) adds source corroboration; it does
not reproduce all findings or qualify every historical source assumption.

## Datasets and source studies

| Publication or original source | Why read it | COLEMAN workflow |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mattis, Rein, Dürsch and Hirschfeld, _RTPTorrent_, MSR 2020. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1145/3379597.3387458) | Understand the source's collected class results and research context | [Source assessment](rtptorrent.md), [Parquet and replay](rtptorrent-parquet-etl.md) |
| Cheng, Wang, Jabbarvand and Marinov, _Revisiting Test-Case Prioritization on Long-Running Test Suites_, ISSTA 2024. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1145/3650212.3680307), [authors' artifact](https://github.com/lrtsuser/LRTS) | Understand the long-running-suite source and its original processing | [Source assessment](lrts.md), [Karaf replay](lrts-parquet-etl.md), [stage views](lrts-stage-views.md) |
| Strandberg, _The Westermo test results data set_, 2022. [Author paper, v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.13622v1) | Understand embedded-system observations, anonymization and source context | [Original analytical Parquet](westermo-parquet-etl.md) |
| Original highly configurable system data. [Dataverse versioned source](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/I1XAVR) | Inspect component terms and original CSV/JSON/log relationships | [LibSSH data path](hcs-parquet-etl.md), [CTest corroboration](hcs-trace-evidence.md) |

A source paper describes the original study. COLEMAN's adapter guides separately
state byte pins, units, exclusions and current qualification limits. Use both;
do not infer missing source clocks or test inventories from a publication's
aggregate statistics.

## Evaluation and interpretation

| Original method reference | Role in the evaluation path |
| --- | --- |
| Student, _The Probable Error of a Mean_, Biometrika, 1908. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/6.1.1) | Background for the legacy normal paired-difference protocol; read its actual assumptions in [protected evaluation](protected-evaluation.md) |
| Hoeffding, _Probability Inequalities for Sums of Bounded Random Variables_, JASA, 1963. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1963.10500830) | Concentration bound underlying the supported [bounded paired method](bounded-paired-evaluation.md), with independent bounded inference units |
| Holm, _A Simple Sequentially Rejective Multiple Test Procedure_, Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, 1979. [Original article](https://www.jstor.org/stable/4615733) | Step-down multiplicity control for the full frozen comparison family; not a way to create independence |


The [protected-evaluation guide](protected-evaluation.md) declares supported
comparison assumptions, pairing, multiplicity and practical-equivalence rules.
The [bounded paired guide](bounded-paired-evaluation.md) documents its conservative
bounds and independence requirements. Read the actual implemented protocol before
choosing an analysis by name.

[Repeated observations](corpus-evaluation.md) explains why builds, seeds and
variants cannot be pooled as independent projects. [Source admission](corpus-admission.md)
separates source integrity from scientific eligibility. [Evidence status](roadmap.md)
explains the missing prerequisites for historical cross-corpus confirmation.

The [independent decision benchmarks](decision-benchmarks.md) validate bounded
mathematical routines against independent references. Such checks establish
correctness under declared assumptions, rather than empirical policy superiority.

## Cite the software and the source

Cite the original COLEMAN article when the method contributes to your work. Cite
the HCS studies when using WTS/VTS, and each dataset's original publication and
version when using its observations. Record the actual software version,
source/adapter/runtime identities, experiment specification and analysis protocol
in your reproducibility material.



### FILE: docs/resource-replay.md

# Exact CI resource accounting and historical replay

`coleman.resources` adds a typed audit of predecision intent, reservations, actual
occupied work, release and overhead. It reuses the native runner, frozen
[CI pilot](operational-pilot.md), [temporal evaluation](protected-evaluation.md),
[domain records](domain-results.md), immutable artifacts and native checkpoints.
Available from COLEMAN 4.3. Build this revision or use the verified 4.4 release
wheel for these examples; the 4.2 wheel does not contain this module.

## Complete accounting example

The ledger uses **integer occupied runner milliseconds**. Equal unit symbols with
different meanings are incompatible. No implicit conversion, clock or external
service is involved:

```python
from datetime import datetime
from coleman.resources import (
    RUNNER_MS, IntentEvent, OccupancyEvent, OverheadEvent, ReserveEvent,
    ResourceAmount, ResourceEstimate, ResourceLedger,
)
from coleman.results.domain import fingerprint

def amount(ms):
    return ResourceAmount(value=ms, semantics=RUNNER_MS)

def metadata(sequence, identity):
    instant = datetime.fromisoformat("2026-01-02T00:00:00Z")
    return dict(event_id=identity, sequence=sequence, event_at=instant, recorded_at=instant)

source = fingerprint({"source": "owned-ci-resource-example-v1"})
estimate = ResourceEstimate(
    amount=amount(1000), source_fingerprint=source,
    observed_at=datetime.fromisoformat("2025-12-30T00:00:00Z"),
    available_at=datetime.fromisoformat("2025-12-31T00:00:00Z"),
    valid_until=datetime.fromisoformat("2026-01-03T00:00:00Z"),
)
ledger = ResourceLedger(
    schema_version=1, ledger_id="build-2:base-order", capacity=amount(2000),
    source_fingerprint=source, configuration_fingerprint=source,
)
ledger = ledger.append(IntentEvent(
    **metadata(1, "intent-a"), execution_id="test-a:attempt-1", estimate=estimate,
))
ledger = ledger.append(ReserveEvent(
    **metadata(2, "reserve-a"), execution_id="test-a:attempt-1", amount=amount(1000),
))
completion = OccupancyEvent(
    **metadata(3, "complete-a"), execution_id="test-a:attempt-1",
    amount=amount(900), terminal="passed",
)
ledger = ledger.append(completion)
ledger = ledger.append(OverheadEvent(
    **metadata(4, "dispatch-a"), component="dispatch", amount=amount(1),
))
assert (ledger.balance.available, ledger.balance.reserved, ledger.balance.consumed) == (1099, 0, 901)
assert ledger.append(completion).to_json() == ledger.to_json()
assert ResourceLedger.from_json(ledger.to_json()) == ledger
```

After reservation: available 1,000, reserved 1,000, consumed 0. Completion charges
900 and releases only the unused 100; reservation is never additional consumption.
The separately observed dispatch overhead charges 1. Initial capacity always equals
available + live reservations + consumed. V1 authorizes **no capacity adjustments**.

An estimate of 900 followed by actual occupancy 1,100 charges all 1,100. Available
capacity can become negative, and exceeding the estimate triggers sticky
`stop_new_reservations` containment even if capacity remains. Existing running
attempts must still report their work. This is accounting and predispatch checking;
it cannot interrupt an external runner or enforce a hard runtime limit.

## States, identity and compatibility

- A zero amount is an observed zero. Null is invalid consumption, but an explicitly
  null `TestEstimate.estimate` is unavailable estimation evidence and prevents dispatch.
- `OccupancyEvent.amount` is an **increment**, not a cumulative counter. `terminal=None`
  retains a live reservation. Terminal passed/failed/unknown/timeout/partial/cancelled
  releases unused reservation; unknown/timeout/partial/cancelled never imply labels.
- A zero terminal cancellation releases the remaining reservation. Retry requires a
  new execution ID with `retry_of` referencing a terminal attempt. Both attempts count.
- Negative consumption, booleans, float quantities, fractional units, nonfinite
  numbers, refunds, top-ups and capacity adjustments fail explicitly. Negative
  available balance and signed comparison savings remain valid observations.
- New events require contiguous sequence 1..n and nondecreasing first receipt times.
  Equal timestamp ties use sequence, never lexical ID. Late source events can have
  earlier event times across different attempts; each attempt and its retry retain
  causal source order. New out-of-order
  deliveries fail; replay the ordered durable source. Exact accepted duplicates may
  arrive anywhere and are ignored. Retrying an already accepted event consumes no
  new slot, including at the 4,096-event limit; raw input arrays are separately bounded.
  Changed canonical payload for an ID conflicts.
- Ledger logical identity is its declared `ledger_id`, independent of contents.
  Full content fingerprint includes schema, provenance and events. Producers own
  globally meaningful IDs and immutable estimation/source/config fingerprints.
- V1 requires explicit integer schema version 1, rejects unknown/future versions,
  duplicate JSON keys and unknown fields, and performs no automatic migrations.
  Existing native Parquet, checkpoints and domain/pilot artifacts keep their schemas
  and meanings. To adopt, create a new ledger with reviewed units and provenance;
  never reinterpret legacy durations as this resource contract implicitly.

## Native CI workflow and comparison

Build/install this revision's wheel, copy
[`examples/resource-replay/ci.py`](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/examples/resource-replay/ci.py)
into an empty local workspace, then run:

```bash
python ci.py owned-ci
python ci.py owned-ci  # completed native checkpoints and original timing are reused
```

The owned MIT synthetic source has three tests, occupied durations 1/2/4 seconds,
and two protected builds after native warmup. The native runner executes **all
three required tests** for each of two frozen candidates: base order and a simple
prior-estimate order. Prior estimates are a separate frozen 4,000/1,000/2,000 ms
vector, available before the protected period. The resource budget is 5,000 ms.

The monitor checks actual native rankings and full-suite schedules before auditing
the modeled resource selection. A selector receives `ResourceRequest`: identities,
ranking, budget, cutoff and frozen estimates. It receives no current duration or
verdict. It selects a serial stop-at-first-nonfit prefix. Missing/future/expired
estimates yield no-action. A stale/unavailable priority signal can fall back to the
full suite only if all estimates are eligible and the complete estimated cost fits;
otherwise it yields no-action. Actual work reconciliation or estimate expiry may
stop a later hypothetical dispatch even when it was initially planned. Native
required tests remain fully executed regardless of the counterfactual selection.

`ResourceReplayProtocol` reuses the pilot's source identity/digest/license,
`TemporalPlan`, freeze, baseline and complete candidate trial registry. Estimation
availability must precede freeze. Candidates share the same builds, resource
budget and failing-test outcome definition. Seeds do not count as independent
builds. `ResourceReplayRun` embeds the unchanged verified native `PilotRun` and
explicit queue/setup/occupied-setup availability; it recomputes the ledger and
summary instead of trusting supplied totals. `ResourceReplayReport` preserves
missing pairs, signed work/net differences and descriptive quality gates. Gates
retain the frozen pilot recall, runner-saving and overhead thresholds; a missing
or unsafe baseline cannot establish a passing comparison. Minimum build counts
and adoption evidence remain separate from a per-build descriptive gate.

`report.md` and typed JSON keep these quantities distinct:

| Quantity | Meaning and limits |
| --- | --- |
| Runner work | Actual declared occupied work in the modeled selection, whole ms |
| Execution elapsed | Serial selected execution, excludes dispatch/queue/setup |
| Dispatch overhead | Measured native prioritization elapsed, explicitly rounded up to ms and modeled as one occupied runner; less than 1 ms rounding excess |
| Shared setup occupancy | Separately declared resource charge; null makes accounting partial |
| Queue/setup elapsed | Separately declared delays, null when unmeasured; never inferred from work |
| Modeled credits subtotal | Frozen credit/second rate applied exactly to known charged work and overhead, excluding fixed/unmeasured/provider costs; not a bill |
| Recall | Full-source failing-test denominator; unresolved labels yield unavailable, no failures yield not applicable |
| First failure | Execution elapsed to first selected failure; null/right-censored if none, genuine zero remains zero |
| Work/net savings | Baseline minus candidate, signed ms; net includes charged overhead |

A negative or inconclusive comparison is valid. A descriptive gate cannot promote
a candidate; adoption remains **insufficient evidence**. This offline fixture
proves accounting and recovery, not independent CI observations, calibrated
probabilities, production savings or willingness to adopt/pay. Multiple candidate
trials remain visible. Protected statistical claims require a separately justified
comparison using the existing evaluation contracts and representative evidence.

## Publication, interruption and concurrency

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    E[Frozen as-of estimates] --> S[Pure estimated selection]
    N[Existing native runner and full CI suite] --> M[Extension monitor]
    S --> R[Counterfactual exact resource replay]
    M --> R
    R --> A[Existing immutable ArtifactWriter]
    A --> L[Typed resource run and ledger checkpoint]
    L --> D[Existing domain result sink]
    D --> C[Existing native checkpoint advances]
    L --> H[Human comparison and typed JSON report]
```

`publish_resource_run` uses a stable logical protocol/candidate/build filename;
changed payloads conflict. First committed timing survives replay. `publish_ledger`
writes an immutable header and stable per-sequence event files before a complete
JSON checkpoint. Concurrent identical writers converge, and different branches
conflict on event paths. Interrupted orphan event files do not constitute a completed
checkpoint. `restore_ledger(path)` reads an explicitly acknowledged complete file
and revalidates every event/balance; it never guesses a latest checkpoint from
partial files. Snapshots embed the complete log and can be copied independently.
A caller acknowledges a source event only after successful publication; its durable
ordered source owns replay after a crash.

The native example publishes resource evidence and domain sidecars before native
checkpoint advancement, and verifies immutable source/Parquet/config/spec proofs
before resuming. Only trusted local checkpoints produced by the example may be
loaded. Native execution remains single-writer per output root; use separate roots
for concurrent native runs. The example rejects unknown roots, bounded-tree excess
and existing symlink children. These checks are not an OS sandbox against hostile
concurrent filesystem mutations.

The existing atomic writer requires local hard links and directory fsync. I/O errors
propagate; temporary files are never completed artifacts. Process interruption is
covered; power-loss durability of newly created ancestor directories is outside its
contract. V1 caps each external amount at 10^12 whole units and the ledger at 4,096
deliveries. CI replay caps tests/build at 1,000, rejects fractional-ms native sources
and requires full-suite native evidence. This is a bounded correctness feature, not
a throughput benchmark or a second scheduler. Parallel scheduling, automatic external
unit conversion, billing integration, mutable capacity, live CI cancellation and
prospective evidence collection remain outside this slice.

## Continue the workflow

Connect resource observations to the [operational pilot](operational-pilot.md) and [shadow
evaluation](prospective-shadow.md). Use the [evaluation guide](evaluation-guide.md) to keep modeled
and observed claims separate.



### FILE: docs/roadmap.md

# What the current evidence supports

Choose a workflow by the question you need to answer. A reproducible source
conversion, a controlled fault observation, a mathematical correctness check and
a historical comparison provide different kinds of evidence.

## What you can use today

| Your question | Available workflow | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Can I execute and inspect a CI prioritization experiment? | [Native experiments, policies, sweeps and checkpoints](experiments.md) | Reproducible execution under your declared inputs and budgets |
| Can I replay original public CI observations? | [LRTS, RTPTorrent and LibSSH data paths](datasets.md) | Source-specific analytical/native projections with explicit grouping, exclusions and qualification limits |
| Can I reproduce a source fault? | [Controlled Java and Python observations](controlled-faults.md) | Behavior under a frozen source, observer and runtime; the constructed C workflow has its own narrower scope |
| Can I test drift, churn or delayed feedback? | [CI stress laboratory](ci-stress-laboratory.md) | Known-answer mechanism checks under authored conditions |
| Can I audit source suitability? | [Source admission](corpus-admission.md) | Byte/provenance checks and explicit scientific eligibility; missing evidence remains visible |
| Can I compare methods? | [Baselines](comparable-baselines.md), [repeated observations](corpus-evaluation.md), [protected comparisons](protected-evaluation.md) | A declared comparison, with valid outcomes including benefit, harm, equivalence and insufficient evidence |
| Can I check operational costs before adoption? | [Operational pilot](operational-pilot.md), [resource replay](resource-replay.md), [shadow evaluation](prospective-shadow.md) | Explicit observed versus modeled costs and declared deployment assumptions |

The [dataset guide](datasets.md) connects each available source to its executable
workflow, original terms and evidence type. The [research guide](research.md)
connects the underlying publications to their original questions and subjects.

## Historical corpus status

A final admitted historical cross-corpus confirmation has not been completed.
The runnable source paths do not yet establish a broad comparison across all of
these historical settings:

| Setting | Evidence needed for a defensible comparison |
| --- | --- |
| Small volatile CI | Pre-decision membership, appearance/removal of tests, outcome availability and independent project/group identity |
| Medium CI | Continuous source coverage, stable testcase identity, feedback timing and comparable budgets |
| Long-running or large suites | Original execution grouping, late results, expected test inventory and observed versus modeled physical costs |
| Highly configurable software | Variant membership, shared executions, sparse cells, attempt identity and independent-family accounting |

A processed dataset's build number alone does not establish a source clock or
prove which tests were known before execution. A complete archive can still lack
those facts. The [RTPTorrent](rtptorrent.md) and [LRTS](lrts.md) source assessments
explain the specific boundaries; the [LibSSH workflow](hcs-parquet-etl.md) retains
variant evidence and [original CTest correspondence](hcs-trace-evidence.md).

No final eligible frozen multi-corpus execution, complete confirmatory report and
end-to-end confirmatory reproduction tutorial are currently established. The
existing installed replay and evaluation examples remain usable at their declared
scopes. Controlled and synthetic observations cannot fill missing historical facts.

## What a stronger comparison would require

1. **Verify source meaning.** Retain original bytes, component terms, units,
   grouping, expected test membership and information availability.
2. **Establish eligible observations.** Apply source-specific admission and
   [point-in-time selection](point-in-time-observations.md); preserve exclusions.
3. **Freeze a comparable experiment.** Fix candidate configurations, data/splits,
   metrics, budget/resource protocol and the full hypothesis family before access.
4. **Use the correct inference unit.** Aggregate dependent builds, variants and
   seeds within the reviewed family; require justified independent units.
5. **Publish the evidence.** Retain raw records, per-project/family results,
   comparison reports, runtime/resource observations and reproduction commands.

More seeds do not create additional independent projects. A favorable average
on one subject does not establish a generally better policy. Negative and
inconclusive findings remain valid outcomes, including a conservative fallback
when the required evidence is unavailable.

## Engineering improvements with a clear boundary

The [maintainability review](maintainability.md) records measured complexity,
public-contract documentation and identity/continuation priorities. The direction
is to make available capabilities easier to understand and compose while
preserving the reusable native engine and its compatibility contracts.



### FILE: docs/rtptorrent-parquet-etl.md

# Turn RTPTorrent CI history into Parquet and native TCPCI replays

Run a complete installed-package HikariCP workflow: verified
real archive → full analytical history → bounded native-compatible Parquet →
Random/UCB → checkpoint recovery. The adapter prepares the inputs and calls the
existing native runner; analytical records and replay projections remain linked
by the source/output receipts.

The preset keeps **46,995 source class executions and 1,662 source jobs** in
analytical Parquet. It projects **18 executions from eight declared jobs** into
the existing native runner. The other **46,977 executions remain analytically
available**, with a conserved `outside_jobs` projection reason.

## Install and run outside checkout

Use Python 3.14+ and the verified published wheel. No source checkout, Docker or
MCP SDK is needed for this workflow; the URL pins the actual wheel SHA-256:

```bash
uv venv /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env --python 3.14
uv pip install --python /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env/bin/python "https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.17.0/coleman-4.17.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=e5a272ddc0edf72bd909a743fa2b3bc0dfeb8a02871c487ab22683cddeea40ca"
mkdir -p /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-workspace
cd /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-workspace
```

Download the pinned public archive explicitly. The command supports resuming a
partial operator download; the ETL verifies the complete SHA-256 before parsing:

```bash
curl --fail --retry 3 --continue-at - --max-time 21600 \
  --output rtp-torrent-v11.zip \
  https://zenodo.org/records/4046180/files/rtp-torrent-v11.zip

/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.rtptorrent_etl \
  --archive rtp-torrent-v11.zip \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-data --run > summary.json
```

`--archive` verifies the supplied file even when the expected source is already
cached. Cache and output must be separate and outside Git. Concrete Parquet and
completion destinations are checked before archive acquisition. Source URIs in
the typed recipe are descriptive; the domain opens no URL. The existing small-
source HTTP adapter retains its 300-second cap. The explicit download step keeps
this approximately 5 GB transfer outside that adapter and can resume separately.

Once the cache is populated, repeat the whole conversion/replay **offline**:

```bash
/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.rtptorrent_etl \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-data --run > resumed-summary.json
```

The two invocations return the same completion and native run identity. Existing
immutable tables are verified and committed checkpoints are reopened. With the
default two policies and eight modeled rounds, the persisted native result has
**16 rows**, including after continuation. Source verification scans the large
archive again; account for that I/O when planning preprocessing.

The summary contains `completion`, `observations`, `jobs`, `datasets_dir`,
`native_artifacts`, conserved counts and the evidence labels. Native logs go to
stderr so a fresh CLI process can write its JSON summary to stdout. An ETL
completion certifies its three data files; native execution is a subsequent step
with the existing runner's own checkpoint/completion behavior.

## What the files preserve

| File | Scope and semantics |
| --- | --- |
| `observations.parquet` | Every canonical raw project/job/class/source-position execution; exact decimal duration text, observed/unavailable status, seconds and reported-class meaning; nullable method count/failures/errors/skipped; class outcome and one primary projection exclusion |
| `jobs.parquet` | All 1,662 source job labels, source/eligible counts, selected modeled round and status; unavailable logical build ID, event clock and outcome-availability clock remain null |
| `datasets/rtptorrent-hikaricp/features-engineered.parquet` | The 18 eligible records using existing native `BuildId`, `Name`, `Duration`, `CalcPrio`, `LastRun`, `Verdict` and `SourceExecutionId` fields |
| `complete.json` | Last-written versioned recipe/producer/writer provenance, physical file hashes/sizes/row counts, canonical row digest and complete exclusion accounting |

Source `duration` values are **reported class elapsed seconds**, as documented by
the existing [raw-class reader](rtptorrent.md). Analytical `duration_decimal`
retains their exact normalized decimal value as text. Native `Duration` explicitly
projects eligible values to binary64 seconds. An observed zero stays zero; null
with `duration_status=unavailable` stays unavailable. Unknown/not-run outcomes
remain distinct from passes. Failure/error/skipped method counters remain
separate; native verdicts count failing **class executions**, not unique faults.

The physical CSV accounting is:

```text
input_rows = observed_executions + duplicate_rows_excluded
observed_executions = replay_executions + excluded_outside_jobs
                    + excluded_not_run + excluded_unknown_outcome
                    + excluded_unavailable_duration
```

Exact repeated source rows are explicitly counted/excluded; conflicting duplicate
execution keys reject. Repeated classes at distinct positions remain separate.
For selected jobs, not-run precedes unknown outcome, which precedes unavailable
duration as the primary exclusion. Outside-slice records retain their full raw
values and the `outside_jobs` reason; their raw outcome is still inspectable.

## Explicit replay assumptions

The frozen preset selects the first eight numeric job labels with at least two
raw class executions. This criterion uses record cardinality and labels, without
filtering on failures. Selected labels are:

```text
13471129, 13474093, 13476365, 13476403,
13476405, 13476407, 13505429, 13505431
```

Numeric order is an explicit **post-hoc simulation order**. Source job IDs remain
original labels. Native `BuildId` is a local modeled round; it does not assert an
observed logical CI build or join concurrent jobs. No commit/build number,
duration sum or source order becomes an observed clock.

The native model adds reported class seconds serially. It assumes correspondence
between the same class label and its within-job occurrence ordinal across jobs.
Source project/job/class/position execution IDs remain independently preserved and
joinable through `SourceExecutionId`. Occurrences are assigned before eligibility,
so changing an outcome or missing duration cannot rename later occurrences.

The receipt requires
`budget-censored-native-RNFail-zero-nondetection`: detections within budget receive
the existing native reward; other prioritized entries receive zero nondetection
reward, including unscheduled classes. Zero nondetection does not establish a
passing class or full-label feedback. The default run uses Random and UCB,
budget ratio 0.5, seed 42 and one execution per policy. Seed repetitions do not
create independent observations.

Evidence is `posthoc-source-job-serial-simulation`, admission is
`blocked_missing_temporal_evidence`, and generalization is `insufficient_evidence`.
Use this delivery to prepare and reproduce modeled CI experiments. Protected
temporal evaluation needs verified event/outcome clocks and logical build/job
mapping. The source-admission and confirmatory requirements remain unmet;
[evidence status](roadmap.md#historical-corpus-status) explains the tracking closure.

## Typed API and a custom bounded slice

The transport loads a metadata-only preset, and the domain exports/verifies it:

```python
from importlib.resources import files
from pathlib import Path

from coleman.application.corpus import run_rtptorrent_replay
from coleman.artifacts import ArtifactWriter
from coleman.corpus import SourceCache
from coleman.corpus.rtptorrent_etl import export_rtptorrent_parquet, validate_rtptorrent_etl
from coleman.corpus.rtptorrent_etl_contracts import RTPTorrentETLReceipt, RTPTorrentETLRecipe

resource = files("coleman.corpus.resources").joinpath("rtptorrent-hikaricp-first-eight-v1.json")
recipe = RTPTorrentETLRecipe.from_json(resource.read_bytes())
cache = SourceCache("/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-source-cache")
completion = export_rtptorrent_parquet(recipe, cache, ArtifactWriter("/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-data"))
receipt = RTPTorrentETLReceipt.from_json(completion.read_bytes())
validate_rtptorrent_etl(receipt, cache, completion.parent)
result = run_rtptorrent_replay(completion, cache, Path("/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-native"))
assert result.run_id
```

For a different reviewed slice, construct an explicit `RTPTorrentETLRecipe` using
one `Zip64SelectionSpec`, its exactly matching existing `RTPTorrentSpec`, a safe
single-component `dataset_id`, at most 16 distinct ascending job labels and the
required feedback declaration. All source observations remain analytical. Unknown
job labels reject. The existing raw-reader limits remain 16 MiB decoded CSV,
50,000 physical rows and 16 KiB per physical line; inputs beyond them reject
without truncation. The published filtered `untreated` baseline is a separate
input and cannot replace the complete raw history.

## Identity, compatibility and recovery

Recipe and completion require integer `schema_version=1` and recipe
`rtptorrent-parquet-source-job-replay-v1`. Missing/future schemas and unknown
assumptions reject. There is no automatic conversion of old native Parquet, LRTS
completions or standalone RTPTorrent datasets into this contract. Existing readers
remain available for those artifacts; create a consciously reviewed new recipe.

The export namespace binds the complete recipe, actual conversion implementation
digest and Polars writer version. Fixed uncompressed Parquet settings bind physical
bytes; `logical_rows_sha256` separately identifies canonical rows. Validation
recomputes actual source membership, conversion, counts and expected physical
bytes. It avoids decoding caller-provided Parquet to certify it. Unknown producer
or writer versions require their recorded implementation and reject certification
under a different one. Metadata-only reading remains distinct from verification.

All three files are immutable before `complete.json` is published last. An
interrupted write may retain individual verified files; retry converges through
the existing writer. Concurrent identical exports converge on the same completion.
Missing/corrupt files or false source/count/provenance claims reject without repair.
Empty native projections remain valid analytical exports and native execution
rejects them explicitly. Trusted local parents and existing filesystem durability
limits apply. No second runner, learning checkpoint or network implementation is
introduced.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Explicit resumed download or existing cache] --> B[Existing SourceCache and bounded ZIP64 profile]
    B --> C[Whole-source and selected-member SHA-256]
    C --> D[Existing complete RTPTorrent raw-class reader]
    D --> E[Typed source-job projection and conserved exclusions]
    E --> F[All observations and jobs in analytical Parquet]
    E --> G[Bounded native-compatible class-execution Parquet]
    F --> H[Immutable last-written ETL completion]
    G --> H
    H --> I[Shared application bridge and existing RunSpec API]
    I --> J[Native Random and UCB with existing checkpoints]
    J --> K[Results plus copied provenance receipt and manifest]
```

## Owned and real installed-package checks

The wheel contains the recipe and owned correctness fixtures. The standalone
example script is a separate repository file: download the exact release-tagged
script and verify its SHA-256, then run twice offline with the installed wheel.
It downloads no foreign dataset:

```bash
cd /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-workspace
curl --fail --location --output owned-ci.py \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/v4.14.0/examples/rtptorrent-parquet/ci.py
/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env/bin/python -c 'import hashlib, sys; from pathlib import Path; sys.exit(0 if hashlib.sha256(Path("owned-ci.py").read_bytes()).hexdigest() == "9b7c8dec20124cefe975d99a2c794a838e791000d3a7cc3046cbcbfaa5c4fd04" else "Example SHA-256 mismatch")'
/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env/bin/python owned-ci.py owned /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-owned-cache
/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env/bin/python owned-ci.py owned /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-owned-cache
```

That example preserves eight constructed records, projects four, accounts for
outside/not-run/unknown/unavailable exclusions, and resumes two native rounds with
four result rows. The test suite compares the two-job native NAPFD/APFDc results
with the existing independent exact tiny oracle under the explicit serial model.
The fresh base-wheel regression also exercises the actual real cache when enabled:

```bash
COLEMAN_RTPTORRENT_ETL_REAL_CACHE=/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-source-cache \
  uv run pytest tests/corpus/test_installed_rtptorrent_etl.py --no-cov -q
```

Source pins and data terms are documented in the
[ZIP64 integrity guide](zip64-source-selection.md) and the
[RTPTorrent source assessment](rtptorrent.md). The wheel contains metadata recipes
and owned fixtures; standalone example scripts are downloaded separately above.
Third-party archive/rows stay outside the repository. Dataset terms remain
separate from enclosed subject-code rights, and this workflow reads reported CI observations rather than executing the archived subject repositories.
